stories.title: Bomb attack on Madhumita Shukla's house:Sister says, 'Bahubali Amarmani is my enemy, if something untoward happens his family will be responsible'
stories.summary: A bomb attack was carried out at the house of poetess Madhumita Shukla's sister at 3 AM on Wednesday in Lakhimpur, UP. The matter came to light when Madhumita's sister Nidhi Shukla filed a complaint for an FIR. She has filed a complaint at Sadar Kotwali naming one person. She has demanded that the police register an FIR. Nidhi Shukla said that Bahubali former MLA Amarmani Tripathi and his family are my enemies. This attack was carried out with the intention of intimidating and threatening me and making me withdraw from the legal battle. If anything happens to my family or me in the future, the responsibility will be of those who carried out the attack. She has demanded increased security from the police. Madhumita Shukla was a 24-year-old emerging poetess. On May 9, 2003, she was shot and killed after intruders entered her house in Paper Mill Colony, Lucknow. The investigation revealed that she was 7 months pregnant. DNA reports confirmed that the child was of former Uttar Pradesh minister Amarmani Tripathi. Now know the complete matter Nidhi Shukla's house is in the Mishrana locality of the city. According to Nidhi, around 3 am on the night of June 30/July 1, there was a loud explosion outside the house. At that time, she was sleeping at home with her family. The constable deployed for her security called her in panic. He informed her, 'There has been a loud explosion like a bomb blast outside.' The constable asked her to open the door, but she refused for security reasons. After this, the constable informed Dial-112 and the police station. She opened the door only after the police reached the spot. Then she was told that there had been an explosion outside her house. Nidhi alleged that on paper, security of three armed and one civil police personnel is sanctioned at her house, but for a year only one constable has been deployed during the day and one at night. She said that despite demanding additional security several times, the demand has been ignored, citing shortage of police force. Continuously receiving death threats Nidhi Shukla said, "There was firing at my house last year as well. Despite that, my security was not increased. I have been receiving continuous death threats." She alleged that the attack was carried out to intimidate her because she is continuing the legal battle in the Madhumita murder case and is preparing to launch a book and a music album based on the case. She said, "I have no personal enmity with anyone. Apart from the families of Amar Mani, Madhu Mani, Rohit, Santosh, and Prakash Mani, I have no other enemies. If anything happens to me or any member of my family in the future, these people alone should be held responsible." Nidhi has demanded that the police conduct a fair investigation into the incident, register an FIR against those responsible, take strict action against them, and immediately strengthen her security arrangements. Now, know in graphics who Madhumita was and how she was murdered?

stories.title: Beef found in auto, driver arrested:Man caught in an accident a year ago; meat was found in tempo
stories.summary: Police arrested an auto driver while solving a one-year-old road accident case in the Gudumba police station area of Lucknow. After the forensic examination of meat pieces found in the tempo confirmed the samples to be of bovine origin (beef), police also added sections of the Uttar Pradesh Prevention of Cow Slaughter Act against the accused. According to police, a case was registered on June 7, 2025, based on a complaint by Arun Kumar Pathak, a resident of Shivani Vihar, Kalyanpur. The allegation was that Suraj, the driver of a Vikram auto, had hit a motorcycle while driving the vehicle at high speed and recklessly under the influence of alcohol. The motorcycle rider Pankaj Mishra was seriously injured in the accident. Forensic report confirms bovine meat (beef) After the accident, police had found remains of an animal's body parts from the Vikram auto. Upon suspicion, the samples were sent to the Forensic Investigation Laboratory, University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Mathura. The investigation report found the samples to be of a cow and its progeny. Following this, during the investigation, sections of the Uttar Pradesh Prevention of Cow Slaughter Act were added to the case. Arrested near 23 number crossing Gudumba Police arrested the wanted accused, Deva, a Barabanki resident, and Suraj (26), from near 23 Number Crossing on Tuesday in the case. During police interrogation, the accused stated that during Bakrid last year, an unknown person at Khurramnagar crossing had lured him with more money to deliver two sacks of beef near the Macaulay area of Shivani Vihar. He agreed to transport the meat in his Vikram auto while intoxicated. During this, an accident occurred on the way. However, the accused could not provide any satisfactory information about the person who gave the beef and the final destination of the meat delivery. After this, the police arrested him and initiated proceedings to present him in court.

stories.title: Startup funding to get a boost:Top investors gather at GIDA; UP DeepTech mission hosts major startup event
stories.summary: IIM Lucknow Enterprise Incubation Center (IIML EIC) organized a special 'VC Pitching' (Investor Meet) program for DeepTech startups at its GIDA office in Gorakhpur. The program, which started at 7 PM on Monday, was conducted under the 'UP DeepTech Mission' in collaboration with Bluehill.VC, SIDBI, and StartinUP. Startups showcased their potential before investors DeepTech startups from different sectors participated in this program. They presented their new innovations, ideas, and business models before major investors of the country. The main objective of this initiative is to provide new entrepreneurs of Uttar Pradesh with necessary funding, proper guidance (mentorship), and connect them with industry experts to accelerate their business growth. Employment and new businesses will increase in the state This event held in GIDA will promote technology and innovation-based businesses not only in Purvanchal but across the entire Uttar Pradesh. Experts believe that such programs provide new startups with direct opportunities to meet major investors, which helps them scale their businesses. This will also create new employment opportunities in the state in the coming times.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav turns 53:SP chief says, 'I celebrate my birthday several times a year;' party workers portray him as Lord Krishna
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav turned 53 on Wednesday, with party workers celebrating his birthday in different ways across Uttar Pradesh. In Varanasi, SP workers performed a havan and special prayers at 7 am. A poster displayed during the event portrayed Akhilesh as Lord Krishna, holding copies of the Constitution in both hands. Meanwhile, Akhilesh reached the SP headquarters in Lucknow, where he addressed a press conference. In a light-hearted remark, he said, "We celebrate birthdays many times a year. Whenever we feel like eating cake or laddoos, that becomes our birthday." Around 10,000 party workers gathered outside the SP office to catch a glimpse of the party chief. Supporters jostled with one another in an attempt to shake hands with him. In Varanasi, police placed SP state secretary Lalu Yadav under house arrest after he announced a protest march over the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Temple. During the action, he got into a heated argument with Kalbhairav police station inspector Dayashankar Singh. Pointing a finger at the officer, Lalu Yadav said, "I have seen many inspectors like you. I am speaking respectfully, but you are crossing the line." Around 10,000 Samajwadi Party (SP) workers gathered at the party headquarters in Lucknow to greet SP chief Akhilesh Yadav on his 53rd birthday. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also wished Akhilesh on X. He wrote, "I pray to Lord Shri Ram to bless you with good health and a long life." Outside Akhilesh's residence in Lucknow, members of the transgender community celebrated with dhols and drums, danced enthusiastically, and took out a chariot procession. SP leader Ikhlaq offered a chadar at the Dada Miyan Dargah as part of the birthday celebrations. In several parts of Lucknow, posters describing Akhilesh as the "future Prime Minister" were put up by party supporters. In Saifai, Akhilesh's uncle Ram Gopal Yadav cut a birthday cake at 9 am and marked the occasion by planting 53 saplings. Moradabad MP Ruchi Veera arranged a 53-foot-long cake to celebrate Akhilesh's 53rd birthday, while SP spokesperson Anurag Bhadauria performed 53 push-ups to mark the occasion. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya and BSP chief Mayawati also extended birthday greetings to Akhilesh Yadav.

stories.title: 5 mosques demolished in Varanasi's Daalmandi for road widening:200 workers, 1,860 security personnel deployed; Aurangzeb-era Rangeele Shah mosque affected
stories.summary: Demolition of 5 mosques began at around 7.30 am on Wednesday in Varanasi's Daalmandi area as part of the road-widening project. By 3 pm, nearly 30-40% of the identified structures had been demolished. Two minarets, each around 20 feet tall, at one of the mosques have already been brought down. Around 200 labourers are carrying out the demolition using hammers. The administration has sealed the road leading to Daalmandi with tin-sheet barricades to restrict access. Nearly 1,860 security personnel have been deployed at the site. The security arrangement includes seven companies of the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC), one battalion of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), one battalion of the Rapid Response Force (RRF), and local police personnel. A total of six mosques fall within the alignment of the Daalmandi road-widening project. The management committees of five mosques had already given their consent for the demolition, while no agreement could be reached regarding the sixth mosque. After the conclusion of Muharram, the administration on Wednesday began removing the identified portions of the five mosques that had agreed to the exercise. Meanwhile, the police and district administration have also stopped media personnel from carrying out videography and photography at the site. Under the Daalmandi road-widening project, a total of 181 houses and six mosques are to be removed. So far, action has been taken against 162 houses, of which 80 have been completely demolished. Look at 3 pictures Action started from Masjid Karimullah Beg Along with 181 houses, six mosques are being affected under the Dalmandi widening project. These include Langde Hafiz Mosque, Nisaran Mosque, Rangile Shah Mosque, Ali Raza Mosque, Sangmarmar Mosque and Masjid Mirza Karimullah Beg. Except for Langde Hafiz Mosque, the managements of all the other mosques had agreed to the widening project. Demarcation and measurements had been completed before Muharram. After Muharram ended, demolition resumed on Wednesday. In the presence of DIG Shiv Hari Meena, the administrative team reached Dalmandi at around 7 am. Tin-sheet barricades were first installed to block access, following which demolition of the boundary wall of Masjid Mirza Karimullah Beg, located behind Chowk police station, began. The identified portion of this mosque falling within the widening corridor is being removed first. 200 laborers deployed Around 200 labourers have been deployed for the demolition exercise. To maintain law and order, 1,860 police personnel and administrative officials have been stationed at the site. Public movement has been restricted in the area. Media personnel were stopped from filming and photographing the demolition process. The administration has not permitted anyone to remain near the site during the operation. The entire locality is being monitored under heavy police presence. Now know about the mosques.... More than 5 thousand worshippers pray at one time Located in the cloth market of Nai Sadak, Langde Hafiz Mosque also houses the office of the Chand Committee. The mosque is managed by the Anjuman Intazamia Masajid Committee, which also oversees the Gyanvapi Mosque. Committee Joint Secretary SM Yasin said the mosque dates back to the pre-Independence era. Friday, Eid and Bakrid prayers are offered here at the latest scheduled time, and around 5,000 to 5,500 people can pray there at one time. Nisaran Mosque built in 1826 Situated around 100 metres from Langde Hafiz Mosque, Nisaran Mosque was built in 1826 by the ancestors of its mutawalli, Mohammad Azam. He said the mosque was officially recorded in government documents in 1929 and can accommodate around 250 worshippers at a time. Rangile Shah Mosque built during Aurangzeb's era Mohammad Azam, who has been offering prayers at the mosque for the past 35 years, said it was built during the reign of Aurangzeb by Rangile Shah, a resident of Hyderabad. According to him, the mosque is around 400 to 500 years old. It is approximately 60 to 65 feet wide and 70 feet deep, and can accommodate nearly 500 worshippers. It is a Jama Masjid where Eid and Bakrid prayers are also held. Ali Raza Mosque is about 200 years old Ali Raza Mosque is located about 200 metres from the Dalmandi lane junction on Nai Sadak. It is believed to be nearly 200 years old and can accommodate around 550 worshippers. If the road is widened by 17.5 metres on both sides, only about three feet of the mosque structure would remain. Marble Mosque also in the project's purview Located near Ghughrani Gali, around 350 metres from the Dalmandi lane junction, Sangmarmar Mosque also falls within the project area. Its mutawalli, Mohammad Sajid, said he has not yet been informed how much of the mosque will be demolished. He said the mosque is around 200 years old and that its front portion was reconstructed in 1935 after becoming dilapidated. 250 to 300 people offer prayers at one time Hafeezur Rahman, also known as Babu, who runs a shop inside the mosque premises, said Friday prayers are not offered at this mosque, but around 250 to 300 people can pray there at one time. Taraweeh prayers are also conducted during Ramadan. He said the mosque is 60 feet wide from the roadside and 40 feet deep. "Its demolition will not only affect a place of worship, but also our livelihood, as our shop will be impacted," he said.

stories.title: 29 UP PCS officers promoted to IAS:Fresh postings soon; paper leak accused Anju Kataria misses out
stories.summary: 29 PCS officers of UP were promoted late Tuesday night. They have been made IAS. The promoted officers include Resident Commissioner, Special Secretary, Additional Commissioner, ADM, Secretary and officers of several development authorities. Several officers from the 2010, 2011, 2012 batches have benefited from the promotion. The promoted officers include names like Alok Verma, Dr. Vishram, Pushparaj Singh, Vivek Srivastava, Yoganand Pandey, Amit Kumar, Dr. Sunil Kumar Verma, Garima Swaroop and Sandeep Kumar among many others. This decision will bring changes at the administrative level in several districts, divisions and departments. The promoted officers will soon be assigned new responsibilities in their positions. The list of promoted officers does not include the name of Anju Kataria from the 2002 batch who has been to jail in the paper leak case. The names of Harish Chandra from the 1997 batch, Prabhunath from the 1999 batch, Amar Pal Singh from the 2004 batch, Alok Verma and Dr. Vaibhav Sharma from the 2008 batch, and Vishwabhushan Mishra from the 2012 batch are also not in the list. Before the order came, their promotion was considered certain. See full list Anju Kataria has been jailed in paper leak case PCS Rakesh Kumar Patel also got promoted Rakesh Kumar Patel, a 2010-batch PCS officer, has also been elevated to the IAS. He is currently serving as Additional Commissioner (Judicial)-IV in the Lucknow Division. A native of Maharajganj, he has previously served as Chief Revenue Officer in Pratapgarh and as Additional District Magistrate in Kasganj between July 2024 and July 2025. Officials cited his extensive administrative experience as one of the factors behind his promotion. ADM Santosh Bahadur Singh's dispute with Iqra Hasan came to light Santosh Bahadur Singh, currently ADM (Administration) in Saharanpur and among those promoted, had faced allegations from Samajwadi Party MP Iqra Hasan last year. Hasan alleged that during a meeting on July 1 with Chhutmalpur Nagar Panchayat chairperson Shama Parveen, Singh used abusive language and asked them to leave his office. According to Hasan, the ADM had said, "This is my office, I can do whatever I want." The MP subsequently lodged written complaints with the Chief Minister, the Principal Secretary (Appointments) and the Divisional Commissioner. An inquiry was ordered, while Singh dismissed the allegations as baseless. Understand the complete promotion process The Departmental Promotion Committee (DPC) meeting was held at the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in New Delhi on June 10, following which promotion orders were issued. Every year, the state government's Appointments and Personnel Department conducts the process for promoting PCS officers to the IAS and forwards proposals to the UPSC. The committee includes the Chief Secretary and the Additional Chief Secretary of the Appointments and Personnel Department. After approval, promotion orders are issued. Cases involving officers facing investigations or judicial proceedings are kept in sealed cover and are opened only after a final decision in the matter. What will be the benefit after getting promoted? Know Following promotion to the IAS, officers become eligible for postings such as Special Secretary, Director in government departments or District Magistrate. Their service comes under the Government of India's Department of Personnel and Training, and they gain higher administrative status and wider responsibilities.

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft:'Daan Patra' found at accused Avinash's home with QR code, ₹20 lakh cash, and $1,000 recovered
stories.summary: Police have recovered a wooden chest marked 'Ramrajya Kosh' (Ramrajya Fund) from the Ayodhya-based yoga centre of jailed accused Avinash Shukla in the alleged Ram Temple offering theft case. The chest had 'Ramrajya Kosh' written on it in red and also carried a Paytm QR code. A video of the police raid conducted on June 28 surfaced on Wednesday morning. Meanwhile, Ram Temple Trust President Mahant Nritya Gopal Das Maharaj has been admitted to Medanta Hospital in Lucknow after his health deteriorated. Hospital Director Dr Rakesh Kapoor said the seer was admitted on June 29 with breathing difficulties and a urinary tract infection. On Tuesday, police questioned all eight accused lodged in Faizabad Jail. The longest interrogation was of Avinash Shukla, lasting nearly two hours. Investigators questioned him about the cash and jewellery recovered from his residence on June 5, where ₹14 lakh in cash was allegedly seized. The Uttar Pradesh government has granted the Special Investigation Team (SIT) an additional 15 days to complete its probe. According to sources, the scope of the investigation may be expanded, and the Enforcement Directorate (ED) could also be brought into the case. Ayodhya Police has reportedly requested senior officials in Lucknow to involve the central agency. On June 5, security personnel of the Ram Mandir Trust conducted a raid at Avinash Shukla's residence, claiming to have recovered cash, which was taken away in bags. A major disclosure has been made regarding the recovery of stolen money in the Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation theft case. According to media reports, the highest amount of cash, ₹20 lakh, was recovered from Avinash Shukla. Police also recovered 1,121 US dollars (around ₹1.06 lakh) and gold and silver jewellery. ₹1 lakh was recovered from Tinnu, while ₹2 lakh was found with his nephew. Avinash Shukla: ₹20,39,220, 1,121 US dollars (₹1,06,667.10), one silver-like metal item, two gold chains and one gold ring. Anukalp Mishra: ₹16,82,040. Lavkush Mishra: ₹14,25,000. Ramashankar Mishra: ₹7,32,170. Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu: ₹1 lakh. Karunesh Pandey: ₹18,07,063. Manish Yadav: ₹2 lakh. Total recovery: ₹79.85 lakh and 1,121 US dollars. 400 private security personnel under scanner Around 400 private security personnel deployed at the Ram Mandir complex have also come under investigation. Authorities are examining their duty rosters, CCTV footage, and entry-exit records. Sources said the private security agency responsible for temple security is owned by a former Bihar MP. The Trust reportedly spends ₹1 crore per month, or approximately ₹12 crore annually, on private security services. During the search of Avinash Shukla's yoga centre, police also recovered several documents and books related to the Ram Mandir. Champat Rai questioned; RMO transferred Police questioned Ram Mandir Trust General Secretary Champat Rai for nearly three hours on Sunday. Investigators asked when and how he first learned about the alleged theft and what actions were taken thereafter. Earlier, a court extended the judicial custody of all eight accused by 14 days. In another development, Arjun Dev, the Radio Operation Officer (RMO) who had been posted at the Ram Temple for the past 17 years, has been transferred to Gorakhpur. The SIT is also examining his role, as he was responsible for monitoring the 1,600 CCTV cameras installed across the temple complex, including those covering the offering counting room. The alleged theft first came to light on June 7. The Uttar Pradesh government constituted the SIT on June 13, and an FIR was registered on June 25. 8 accused, including Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu, were arrested the same day. Also on June 25, Ram Mandir Trust General Secretary Champat Rai and Trustee Dr Anil Mishra resigned from their posts.

stories.title: Bad weather disrupts operations at Gorakhpur Airport:Flights to and from Delhi, Mumbai and other cities delayed; passengers left stranded
stories.summary: Poor weather conditions significantly disrupted flight operations at Gorakhpur Airport on Monday. Adverse weather caused delays to several flights operating on the Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Bengaluru routes. The disruptions directly affected passengers, many of whom had to wait for several hours at the airport. For many travellers, onward journeys and pre-arranged plans were also thrown into disarray. Incoming flights arrive after schedule time Several inbound flights reached Gorakhpur after their scheduled arrival times. Departure flights also delayed The late arrival of incoming aircraft also delayed several departures from Gorakhpur. Passengers face long waits The prolonged delays led to heavy congestion inside the airport terminal. Many passengers were forced to wait for hours, while others missed connecting flights or had their pre-scheduled meetings and other important commitments disrupted. According to the Airports Authority, flight operations gradually returned to normal once weather conditions improved. Passengers have been advised to check the latest status of their flights before travelling to the airport during the monsoon season to avoid unnecessary inconvenience.

stories.title: Ethanol vehicles beat petrol and diesel on cost:Fuel to cost ₹30 less per litre; more pumps planned after Noida and Ghaziabad
stories.summary: With petrol and diesel prices continuing to rise across India, ethanol-powered vehicles are increasingly being discussed as a more affordable alternative. In Uttar Pradesh, petrol is currently selling at around ₹102 per litre, while diesel costs approximately ₹95 per litre. Against this backdrop, attention has turned to ethanol-powered or flex-fuel vehicles, with ethanol expected to cost between ₹70 and ₹75 per litre. According to Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri, E20 fuel is now available at petrol pumps across the country. E85 is currently available at 48 petrol pumps, while E100 is being sold at 183 outlets in Maharashtra, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. The government aims to increase the number of E85 and E100 fuel stations to 500 by December 2026 and 5,000 by 2027. Pros and cons of Ethanol vehicles Flex-fuel vehicles can run on both conventional petrol and high-ethanol fuels such as E100, allowing drivers to switch between fuels depending on availability. Advantages Disadvantages Why running costs can still be lower According to automobile experts, ethanol contains around 30% less energy than petrol. As a result, vehicles running on E85 or E100 consume more fuel to travel the same distance. Although mileage is typically 25% to 35% lower, the significantly lower price of ethanol can still reduce the overall cost of travel. Example Assuming- A 100–125cc motorcycle would typically- To cover the same 65 km, the motorcycle would require approximately 1.25 litres of E100. Calculation- 1.25 × ₹70 = ₹87.50 This means that although the motorcycle consumes more ethanol due to lower mileage, the journey would still cost around ₹88, compared with ₹100 on petrol, resulting in a saving of approximately ₹12 over the same distance. Ethanol fuel availability still limited The first E85 and E100-compatible vehicles were launched during the first week of June. However, one major question remains: where will owners be able to refuel? According to the Ministry of Petroleum, E20 has already become available at most petrol stations across India. However, E85 and E100 are currently available only at a limited number of outlets. The government is upgrading fuel stations, and in the coming years, ethanol fuels are expected to become available at regular petrol pumps. At present, there are three ethanol fuel stations in the Noida–Ghaziabad region. Three key questions about ethanol vehicles 1. Can older vehicles run on ethanol? No. E85 and E100 fuels are not designed for older vehicles. Drivers will need to purchase flex-fuel vehicles specifically built to run on these fuels. 2. Can using E85 or E100 damage older vehicles? Yes. Vehicles manufactured before 2023 were designed primarily for conventional petrol. Long-term use of high-ethanol fuels can gradually corrode rubber hoses, plastic components and aluminium engine parts, potentially leading to premature engine wear or even engine seizure. Owners of older vehicles are therefore advised to continue using suitable petrol grades, including premium fuels such as XP95, where recommended. 3. What happens if ethanol runs out and there is no ethanol station nearby? Flex-fuel vehicles can operate on both petrol and ethanol-blended fuels. If E85 or E100 is unavailable, drivers can simply refuel with ordinary petrol and continue their journey. Why does India not offer E5 and E10 alongside E20 Several countries, including Brazil, the United States, France and Thailand, offer multiple ethanol blends such as E10, E15, E27, E85 and E100, allowing motorists to choose the fuel best suited to their vehicle. Owners of older vehicles in India argue that when E20 was introduced in April 2023, lower-blend fuels such as E5 and E10 should also have remained available. They believe these fuels would have been more suitable for older engines and would have provided better fuel economy. Oil marketing companies, however, argue that maintaining separate supply chains and storage systems for E5, E10 and E20 would significantly increase operational costs. Even so, companies including Indian Oil, BPCL and HPCL already market premium fuels such as XP95 and XP100 through dedicated distribution networks. Government exploring Isobutanol blend for Diesel The government is also exploring biofuel alternatives for diesel. Isobutanol, a biofuel derived from ethanol, mixes readily with diesel and is being evaluated as a future blending option. In September 2025, Union Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari said that an earlier experiment involving a 10% ethanol blend in diesel had not been successful. Attention has now shifted towards isobutanol blending. According to the Ministry of Road Transport, its use in diesel could be made mandatory by the end of 2026 if ongoing trials prove successful.

stories.title: Travellers face disruption at Varanasi Airport:Akasa Air suspends 4 flights after SpiceJet exit; Air India Express also halts Mumbai service
stories.summary: The series of flight suspensions at Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport in Varanasi continues. After SpiceJet suspended all its services recently, Akasa Air has now discontinued the operation of its four flights from 1 July. In addition, Air India Express has also temporarily suspended its daily service between Varanasi and Mumbai. Passengers are facing increasing inconvenience due to the continuous reduction in flight services. It is also believed that the shrinking number of flights could make air travel more expensive. Three Bengaluru flights among those suspended Under the revised schedule effective from 1 July (Wednesday), Akasa Air has suspended the following services- QP 1422 – Varanasi–Bengaluru QP 1524 – Varanasi–Bengaluru QP 1424 – Varanasi–Bengaluru QP 2022 – Varanasi–Navi Mumbai Similarly, Air India Express has temporarily suspended its daily IX 2547 service operating between Varanasi and Mumbai. According to reports, the airline management has withdrawn the service until further notice. IndiGo also revises flight schedule Amid the reduction in services, IndiGo has also revised the schedule of several flights. The Varanasi–Delhi service (6E 2215) will now operate only three days a week, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday, instead of operating daily. Similarly, the Varanasi–Navi Mumbai service (6E 5302) will now operate only on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday. The Varanasi–Kolkata flight (6E 507) will also not operate regularly throughout the month. Instead, it will fly only on 9 July, 21 July and 31 July. Passengers likely to face more difficulties The continued reduction in flight services is expected to create difficulties for passengers travelling to Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi, Kolkata and Navi Mumbai. The changes are also likely to have a direct impact on travellers from the tourism, business and salaried sectors. Rising ATF costs believed to be the reason According to sources, petroleum supplies have been affected following the conflict in West Asia. As a result, the price of Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) has increased, leading to higher operating costs for airlines and financial losses. Sources say this is the primary reason behind the suspension and reduction of several flight services. However, neither the airport administration nor the airlines concerned have issued an official statement on the matter. Passengers have been advised to check the latest flight status with their respective airlines before travelling.

stories.title: Sleeper bus crashes into car on Agra–Lucknow expressway:5 killed, 8 injured; bus overturns after falling into pit
stories.summary: Five people, including two young girls, were killed after a sleeper bus collided with an Ertiga car on the Agra–Lucknow Expressway in Unnao at around 4:30 am on Wednesday. The sleeper bus was travelling from Jhajjar in Haryana to Nalanda in Bihar, while the Ertiga was travelling from Agra towards Lucknow. Both vehicles were moving in the same lane when the speeding bus rammed into the car from behind before veering off the expressway and overturning. The collision was so severe that the Ertiga was completely crushed and dragged for nearly 20 feet. The crash triggered panic at the scene, with screams heard immediately afterwards. After being alerted by passing motorists, police reached the spot and launched a rescue operation. Passengers trapped inside the overturned bus were rescued after officers broke the window panes to pull them out. The injured were shifted to hospital. The accident took place in the Bangarmau area, around 65 km from the Unnao district headquarters. 8 injured, including four bus passengers Bangarmau Circle Officer Harsh Modi said there were 70 passengers on the bus and nine occupants in the Ertiga. Apart from the five fatalities, four occupants of the car and four passengers on the bus sustained injuries. All were referred to the district hospital for treatment. Bangarmau Inspector Akhilesh Pandey said- Passengers have claimed that the bus driver was under the influence of alcohol. The accident occurred after the driver dozed off at the wheel. The families of those who died have been informed. See 3 pictures- Bus was travelling at around 100 km/h According to police, the sleeper bus belonged to Baba Traveller and was travelling from Jhajjar, Haryana, to Nalanda, Bihar. It bore registration number BR 06 PF 1024. The Ertiga, registered in Sant Kabir Nagar, bore registration number UP 58 AK 3461. Police said the bus was travelling at a speed of around 100 km/h at the time of the crash. The five people who died at the scene have been identified as- District Magistrate Ghanshyam Meena and Superintendent of Police Jai Prakash Singh visited the scene to assess the situation and oversee the response.

stories.title: Rain alert issued for 55 UP districts:Temperatures fall by 5–7°C after monsoon enters; three swept away in Sonbhadra
stories.summary: The wait for the monsoon in Uttar Pradesh is finally over. On 30 June, the southwest monsoon entered the state through Sonbhadra and Maharajganj districts. Its arrival brought rain accompanied by strong winds to more than 20 districts across eastern Uttar Pradesh. In Jhansi, rain began at around 7:30 pm on Tuesday, while Prayagraj witnessed heavy rainfall for nearly 90 minutes, starting at 8 pm. One dead, One missing after flash flood in Sonbhadra In Sonbhadra, three people who had gone for a picnic on Tuesday evening at around 4 pm were swept away by the strong current of a rain-fed stream. One young man died in the incident, another was injured, while a third remains missing. According to reports, the water level in the stream rose suddenly following heavy rainfall, sweeping all three away. Rain alert issued for 55 districts The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rainfall alert for 55 districts across Uttar Pradesh for Wednesday (1 July). The weather department has also said that the monsoon is expected to become active across the entire state within the next 24 hours. The monsoon had remained stalled along the Uttar Pradesh–Bihar border for nearly 19 days. It normally reaches Uttar Pradesh by 20 June, but this year its advance has been delayed by around 10 days. See 2 pictures of rain- Monsoon enters UP through eastern region According to the weather department, after making landfall along the Kerala coast, the southwest monsoon splits into two branches. One branch moves through the Arabian Sea, bringing rain to Kerala, Gujarat and Rajasthan. The other advances through the Bay of Bengal and is responsible for rainfall in Uttar Pradesh. The monsoon traditionally enters the state through the Purvanchal (eastern Uttar Pradesh) region, and this year it has followed the same route. Scientist explains the current situation Mohammad Danish, a scientist at the Lucknow Meteorological Centre, said- The southwest monsoon has advanced into parts of Uttar Pradesh. It is currently passing through Azamgarh, Ayodhya and Bareilly. Conditions are favourable for the monsoon to advance further across the state over the next two to three days. Both eastern and western Uttar Pradesh are now expected to witness spells of heavy rainfall. Temperatures are likely to drop by up to 10°C.

stories.title: Congress pushes for equal share in UP alliance:In-charge seeks half the seats, survey underway on 170 seats
stories.summary: 'Congress is the big brother in UP. We will negotiate for equal seats in the 2027 Assembly elections.' This was stated by newly appointed Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam. The statement surfaced on June 28, following which the party has started identifying nearly 170 Assembly seats in the state that it could stake a claim on in the event of an alliance with the Samajwadi Party. After its improved performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Congress is no longer willing to remain a junior partner to SP in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls. According to sources, the party has begun groundwork on strong seats with the help of a professional agency. Demanding more seats so that seats don't reduce in negotiations A senior Congress strategist, speaking on condition of anonymity, said, "Our target is to directly contest 120-130 seats. A pool of around 170 seats has been prepared to avoid any major reduction during negotiations and to retain strong bargaining leverage." SP, however, remains cautious about Congress' assertive stance and is reportedly not inclined to offer more than 60-80 seats. This could lead to intense negotiations within the INDIA bloc in the coming months. Criteria for selecting seats Traditional support base: Seats where Congress historically enjoyed a strong and loyal voter base. 2024 Lok Sabha trend: Assembly segments where Congress secured a lead during the 2024 parliamentary elections. Organisational strength: Constituencies where the party has an active and robust booth-level network. Option of alliance with 'BSP' also open Congress does not want to depend solely on one alliance partner in Uttar Pradesh this time. New state in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam has advocated bringing not only the Samajwadi Party but also the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) into a broader alliance. He said, "I am not authorised to decide on alliances. But all parties that believe in the Constitution deserve fair representation. Whenever Behenji (Mayawati) is willing, we are ready to meet her." Notably, on May 19, Rajendra Pal Gautam reached Mayawati's residence without an appointment, though she did not meet him. Congress's Focus on 'Dalit, Brahmin and Muslim' Political observers say there was a time when the Dalit, Brahmin and Muslim vote bank guaranteed Congress' dominance in Uttar Pradesh. However, over the last three decades, the party has largely been confined to the Rae Bareli and Amethi Lok Sabha seats, while its Assembly presence has steadily declined. The new leadership being projected for 2027 is seen as an attempt to revive this old social engineering formula. Rajendra Pal Gautam, recently appointed as UP Congress in-charge, belongs to the Dalit community and hails from Meerut. He is believed to have considerable influence in western Uttar Pradesh and among Dalit voters. Congress is said to have benefited from Dalit support in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Rajya Sabha MP Pramod Tiwari and his daughter Aradhana Mishra 'Mona' remain the party's most prominent Brahmin faces in the state. Aradhana also leads the Congress Legislature Party in Uttar Pradesh. Congress is also seeking to retain its appeal among Muslim voters through Saharanpur MP Imran Masood and national minority wing chief Imran Pratapgarhi. Congress secured only 2% vote share in 2022 Congress contested the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections without an alliance with any major party. It fielded candidates on 399 seats under the leadership of Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. The campaign was centred around the slogan "Ladki Hoon, Lad Sakti Hoon" (I am a woman, I can fight), with women being allotted 40% of tickets. Despite this, the party performed poorly and its vote share fell to 2.33%. Congress managed to win only two seats — Aradhana Mishra 'Mona' from Rampur Khas in Pratapgarh district and Virendra Chaudhary from Pharenda in Maharajganj district. It marked the party's worst-ever Assembly election performance in Uttar Pradesh. Strategy aimed at putting psychological pressure on SP Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says the 'elder brother' remark and the survey of 170 seats are part of a calculated strategy to exert psychological pressure on SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. "Congress knows that its success in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections was significantly aided by SP's PDA (Backward, Dalit and Minority) formula. By staking claim to such a large number of seats nearly eight months before the Assembly elections, Congress is trying to strengthen its bargaining position." He added that extending an olive branch towards Mayawati is also a signal to Akhilesh Yadav that Congress believes it has alternatives in Uttar Pradesh politics.

stories.title: Ram Mandir offering theft report sent to Mohan Bhagwat:Trust reshuffle planned; new saints likely to join, responsibilities to change
stories.summary: A report on the alleged theft of offerings at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir has been submitted to RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat. The report was prepared by Anil Kumar, the Kshetra Pracharak (Regional Pracharak) for Eastern Uttar Pradesh, who stayed in Ayodhya for three days at Bhagwat's direction. According to sources, the report provides a detailed assessment of the Ram Mandir's arrangements, the functioning of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, and the alleged offering theft. A crucial meeting of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust is scheduled to be held in Ayodhya on 6 July. Sources claim that several important decisions could be taken in the coming days based on the Sangh's findings. RSS takes a tough stand after donation controversy Sources say that following controversies surrounding donations and Mandir management, the RSS has decided to distance itself from certain trust officials. The roles and responsibilities of some individuals associated with the trust are reportedly under review. Discussions are said to be underway to curtail the powers of certain office-bearers while redefining responsibilities for others. Following the resignations of Champat Rai and Anil Mishra, a decision regarding Gopal Rao is also expected to be taken during the 6 July meeting. Blueprint ready for Trust reorganisation According to sources, discussions have begun on restructuring the 15-member Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. One proposal under consideration is to strengthen the representation of the saint community within the trust. Sources say the name of a prominent religious leader with an RSS background, particularly from the Nashik region in western India, is being considered. Alongside this, there is also a proposal to induct a prominent saint from Ayodhya into the trust. Strongest contenders from Ayodhya 1. Swami Vasudevacharya Vidyabhaskar Among Ayodhya's saint community, Jagadguru Ramanujacharya Swami Vasudevacharya Vidyabhaskar is regarded as the leading contender. He is recognised as one of India's foremost Vedic scholars and is a prominent saint of the Ramanuja tradition. He also enjoys wide acceptance within the saint community. 2. Swami Rajkumar Das The second prominent contender is Swami Rajkumar Das Maharaj, head of Shriramvallabhakunj. He is associated with Maniram Das Chhawani and is known within the saint community as a composed, restrained, and controversy-free religious leader. His popularity among devotees and cordial relations with various organisations are also considered key strengths. Krishna Mohan's role may expand Trust member Krishna Mohan has also emerged as a key figure in recent discussions. According to sources, he is being considered for a major administrative role within the trust. It is believed that his responsibilities in the management of the Ram Mandir could increase significantly. However, the final decision is expected only after the trust meeting. Who is active within the trust? The trust currently has six prominent representatives from the saint community. However, active participation in its functioning is reportedly limited to only a few members. Trust President Mahant Nrityagopal Das has been unwell for a prolonged period. Meanwhile, several other saint members are also said to play a limited role in the trust's day-to-day administrative affairs. In contrast, Treasurer Govinddev Giri and Swami Vishwaprasanna Teerth have remained consistently active in major Mandir programmes, trust meetings, and religious events. Treasurer's role also under review Following the controversies over donations, questions have also been raised about the trust's financial management. Some believe that, given the expanding scale of the Mandir and donations worth crores of rupees, financial oversight now requires greater time, attention, and administrative supervision. According to sources, the role and functioning of the treasurer are therefore also under review. However, the trust has not issued any official statement on the matter. stories.title: FIR against SP MLA Amitabh Bajpai in Kanpur:Accused of celebrating Akhilesh Yadav's birthday at primary school without permission
stories.summary: Police have registered an FIR against SP MLA Amitabh Bajpai in connection with the celebration of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav's birthday at Parmat Primary School in Kanpur. The case was registered by Gwaltoli police on the complaint of the school's suspended headmaster. According to the complaint, the SP MLA organised the birthday celebration on the school premises without permission. It has also been alleged that although an MP was scheduled to distribute school uniforms to the children, Amitabh Bajpai distributed the uniforms instead. The school's headmaster had already been suspended over the incident. Following his complaint, police have now registered a case against the MLA. Birthday celebrated at school on July 1 On July 1, Amitabh Bajpai celebrated Akhilesh Yadav's birthday at Parmat Primary School in Kanpur. Photographs and videos of the event later went viral on social media. The following day, headmaster Naveen Kumar Tripathi was suspended over the incident. On Tuesday, suspended headmaster Naveen Kumar Tripathi lodged a complaint at Gwaltoli police station. He alleged that the SP MLA forcibly held Akhilesh Yadav's birthday celebration on the school premises without obtaining any official permission. He further claimed that Amitabh Bajpai distributed school uniforms to the children during the event. Based on the complaint, Gwaltoli police registered an FIR against the SP MLA. FIR registered under BNS Section 132 The FIR has been registered under Section 132 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with assaulting or using criminal force against a public servant to deter them from discharging official duties. The provision is intended to protect government employees while performing their official responsibilities. Police have begun an investigation into the entire matter.

stories.title: Akhilesh sends notice to Nishikant Dubey over Tinnu Yadav link:BJP MP says, 'File an FIR too, I will also go to court'
stories.summary: A political row has erupted between SP president Akhilesh Yadav and BJP MP Nishikant Dubey over Ramashankar Yadav alias Tinnu Yadav, the accused in the theft of offerings at the Ram Mandir. On Tuesday at 1:55 pm, Akhilesh Yadav, through SP state president K.K. Pal, sent a legal defamation notice to Nishikant Dubey. The notice relates to allegations that Akhilesh had spoken to Tinnu Yadav. The SP chief has described the allegations as completely false, baseless and malicious. Meanwhile, SP leaders lodged a complaint at Friends Colony police station in Etawah against Nishikant Dubey and several others for circulating social media posts claiming that Tinnu had spoken to Akhilesh Yadav. Responding to the complaint, Nishikant Dubey said- Under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Akhilesh Yadav himself will have to go to the police station and file a complaint. Follow the law. Akhilesh had warned Dubey to delete the X post Nishikant Dubey, the BJP MP from Godda in Jharkhand, had shared an X post on July 5 by Saravanna Prasad Balasubramaniam, claiming that Tinnu Yadav had been in regular contact with Akhilesh Yadav. The post cited an alleged police investigation and mobile call records. While sharing it, Dubey wrote- Wasn't Tinnu talking to Tipu? Akhilesh Yadav reacted strongly to the post and gave Dubey 10 minutes to delete it. He warned- The BJP MP should remove his false social media post within 10 minutes, otherwise a named FIR will be registered against him. Calling the allegation false propaganda, Akhilesh said it violated parliamentary traditions, public decency and the dignity of Lord Ram. He alleged that the BJP was attempting to defame the PDA alliance. Nishikant responds to Akhilesh's warning Nishikant Dubey also replied on X, writing- Hurry up, why are you so troubled? It's only a question, isn't it? Who ordered the firing on Ram devotees in 1990? I will go to court. Defamation notice demands apology and deletion of post The Samajwadi Party has now formally initiated legal proceedings by issuing a defamation notice. The notice asks Nishikant Dubey to remove the social media post and issue a public apology. It warns that if he fails to do so, further legal action will follow. Akhilesh Yadav has also warned others sharing similar posts to delete them and apologise. Pawan Pandey challenges BJP to produce evidence Former SP MLA from Ayodhya, Pawan Pandey, released a video stating that the theft allegations had already been proved, the accused had been jailed and trustees had been removed. He alleged that the BJP, RSS and VHP were now spreading false propaganda by claiming that Akhilesh Yadav had spoken to Tinnu Yadav. Pawan Pandey said- It is an open challenge. If there is proof of any phone conversation between Akhilesh Yadav and Tinnu Yadav, produce it. Otherwise, publicly apologise to Akhilesh Yadav. He added that politics should be based on facts and evidence rather than false allegations, and said he would retire from politics if BJP leaders proved their claim. Who is Tinnu Yadav? Ramashankar Yadav alias Tinnu Yadav was the driver of Champat Rai. He is a resident of Ayodhya and is currently in jail. According to the SIT report, Tinnu Yadav had control over the keys to the temple's donation boxes and access arrangements without any formal written authorisation. The report further stated that Manish Kumar Yadav was assigned donation-counting duties on Tinnu Yadav's recommendation and was later found to be involved in theft cases. The SIT described these lapses as a serious failure in the mandir's security arrangements.

stories.title: Lucknow named India's most walkable city:Tops survey among 12 major cities; Delhi ranks eighth
stories.summary: Lucknow has achieved a major milestone after being ranked the most walkable city among the 12 major cities surveyed in the State of Indian Streets Report 2026. The Vice-Chairman of the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) said the authority is continuously working to improve public infrastructure in line with people's needs. Facilities will be further enhanced through development projects and parks. Nearly 28% of roads and footpaths are pedestrian-friendly According to the report, 28% of Lucknow's roads and footpaths allow people to walk without obstruction. Bengaluru ranked second with 25.9%, followed by Hyderabad at 15.1% and Chennai at 13.9%. As part of the survey, 346 footpaths across Lucknow were inspected, of which 97 were rated as being in excellent condition. Well-developed footpaths helped secure top ranking The report attributes Lucknow's top position to its well-maintained footpaths and improved pedestrian infrastructure in areas such as Ambedkar Park Road, Lohia Path, Indira Nagar and Gomti Nagar. LDA Vice-Chairman Prathmesh Kumar said the authority's objective is to make Lucknow a safe, accessible and convenient city for pedestrians. Pedestrian facilities to remain a development priority He said the LDA is continuously upgrading footpaths, greenways, public spaces and other essential civic infrastructure. The authority will continue to prioritise pedestrian convenience in future urban development projects to ensure safer and more accessible streets across the city.

stories.title: School journeys to become safer:Drivers and conductors to receive training; strict action against safety violations
stories.summary: A major initiative is being launched in Gorakhpur to further strengthen the safety of schoolchildren. Under the programme, all school vehicle drivers and conductors in the district will receive specialised training to ensure children travel safely to and from school. The Secondary Education Department and the Traffic Department will jointly conduct the campaign, providing training on road safety, traffic regulations, handling emergency situations and ensuring the safe transportation of children. Preparations have been completed, and the campaign is expected to begin by the end of this month. Expert teams to visit every tehsil Under the plan, tehsil-wise teams will be formed according to a pre-scheduled programme. These teams will visit schools across the district to train drivers and conductors of school vehicles. The training will cover safe driving practices, routine vehicle inspections, compliance with prescribed speed limits, safe boarding and alighting of students, first aid, immediate response during accidents or emergencies, and adherence to traffic regulations. Only trained drivers and conductors to operate school vehicles As part of the campaign, all schools will be instructed to ensure that only drivers and conductors who have completed the mandatory safety training and meet all government-prescribed standards are assigned to school vehicles. The department aims to eliminate any scope for negligence in the operation of school transport. No compromise on children's safety The Secondary Education Department said that the safety of students remains its highest priority and that no negligence will be tolerated. To achieve this, the Education Department and the Transport Department will jointly implement the campaign on a large scale to ensure every school vehicle complies with safety standards, enabling children to travel safely between home and school.

stories.title: CM Yogi on a two-day tour to Varanasi:To offer prayers today, will launch cashless healthcare scheme for teachers tomorrow
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will arrive in Varanasi on Tuesday evening for a two-day visit. During his stay, he will attend the wedding of State Minister Dayashankar Mishra's son on Tuesday evening. On Wednesday, he will launch a cashless healthcare scheme for teachers. According to District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar, the Chief Minister is scheduled to land at the Police Line helipad after 6 pm on Tuesday. From there, he will proceed directly to Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham to offer prayers. After the visit to the temple, he will attend the wedding reception of State Minister Dayashankar Mishra 'Dayalu's' son, Animesh, at Hotel Lemon Tree in Rohania. He will stay overnight at the Circuit House. To launch cashless healthcare scheme on Wednesday The District Magistrate said that on Wednesday, the Chief Minister will inaugurate a cashless medical treatment scheme for teachers and Shiksha Mitras of the Basic and Secondary Education Department at Hastkala Sankul in Bara Lalpur. He will also transfer scholarship funds exceeding ₹1 crore directly into the bank accounts of students across the state through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system. Godowlia–Maidagin stretch declared a no-vehicle zone Following the programme, the Chief Minister will return to the Police Line before leaving for Vindhyachal in Mirzapur. In view of his visit, the road between Maidagin and Godowlia will remain a no-vehicle zone. No vehicles of any kind will be permitted on the stretch during the Chief Minister's movement. The traffic department has issued an advisory for commuters.

stories.title: Yogi attacks Opposition over Waqf land issue:Claims poor people's lands was grabbed, opposition changes colours like a chameleon
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday targeted the Indian National Congress and Samajwadi Party in Pratapgarh. He said that thousands of hectares of land were sold in the name of Waqf in the state and the country, while lands meant for the welfare of poor people were encroached upon. “Did SP-Congress ever raise their voice against this? No. Because their mouths get locked when it comes to Waqf,” the Chief Minister said. CM Yogi said, “The pain of the opposition is that where they wanted to see the Babri structure, a grand temple has now been built there. Looking at their double standards, it seems even a chameleon has started feeling ashamed of them, because they change colours faster than it does.” He said the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust is managing the construction and arrangements of the temple and nobody has the right to interfere in its functioning. CM Yogi inaugurated and laid the foundation stones of 111 projects worth ₹384 crore. He also honoured BPSC topper Shraddha Pandey on the stage. Read Yogi's 5 big statements- 1- ‘SP-Congress who shed tears in support of Babri structure have no right to speak’ The Chief Minister said these parties repeatedly raise the same old issues — dividing society in the name of caste and attacking faith. He said these are the only two issues left with SP and Congress today. “You have seen continuous attempts to attack India’s Sanatan faith. Remember, Congress leaders used to say that Lord Ram never existed and Lord Krishna never existed,” he said. He said those who shed crocodile tears in support of the Babri structure in Ayodhya are now changing colours and talking about faith. “They say that the faith of Ayodhya is being played with. I want to ask, what kind of interference is happening? If Ram devotees say their faith is connected with Ayodhya, they have every right to say so because their ancestors fought for Ram Janmabhoomi,” Yogi said. “But Congress does not have this right because it questioned even the existence of Lord Ram,” he added. 2- ‘How can SP, which fired bullets at Ram devotees, talk about faith?’ Yogi said, “The SP, which ordered firing on Ram devotees, how can it talk about faith today?” He alleged that these parties object to the redevelopment of Hindu religious sites but had no problem spending crores of rupees on boundary walls of graveyards. “The country will no longer fall for the deception of Congress and SP,” he said. The Uttar Pradesh government had formed an SIT to investigate matters related to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. Based on the preliminary report, the SIT registered an FIR and action was taken against those against whom evidence was found. “But Congress and Samajwadi Party do not say a single word about corruption in the name of Waqf,” Yogi said. He questioned whether Hindu sentiments were not hurt when illegal slaughterhouses were operating, cow smuggling was taking place, Ram devotees were fired upon, Lord Ram and Lord Krishna were described as imaginary, and restrictions were imposed on Kanwar Yatra. He said Congress and SP should answer all these questions. 3-'Opposition's pain that despite misinformation, crores of people are reaching Ayodhya' Yogi said SP had created an identity crisis for the youth of Uttar Pradesh and was now creating various controversies as elections approached. “The progress visible in Uttar Pradesh today, freedom from disturbances and the peaceful environment created here are not liked by these opposition parties. They also do not like respect for our heritage,” he said. He alleged that the opposition once again wants to divide society on caste lines. “We have to rise above this and move ahead on the path of development,” he said. He said Ayodhya now has four-lane roads, double railway lines and an international airport named after Maharishi Valmiki. A night shelter has also been built in the name of Nishadraj. “This is the pain of the opposition that despite their propaganda, crores of people are reaching Ayodhya,” he said. 4- ‘Earlier, some families controlled government jobs’ Yogi said he was happy that hundreds of youths from Pratapgarh were selected in nearly 60,000 Uttar Pradesh Police recruitments. He said candidates from Pratapgarh are continuously getting selected in results announced by the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission and the Subordinate Services Selection Commission. “Earlier, some families had control over government jobs. There was no transparency, due to which youths of Pratapgarh were deprived of these opportunities,” he said. He added that when youths are deprived of opportunities, they migrate and the state suffers. “This was the reason why Uttar Pradesh was once called a ‘Bimaru state’,” Yogi said. 5- ‘Whenever religion and nation faced a crisis, Pratapgarh never stepped back’ Yogi said Pratapgarh has great mythological and historical importance. “Whenever religion and the nation faced a crisis, Pratapgarh never stepped back. During the First War of Independence in 1857, Babu Gulab Singh raised the first call for revolt from this land,” he said. He said the warriors of Pratapgarh shook the foundations of foreign rule. He added that Pratapgarh has earned global recognition due to the sweetness and quality of its amla. “We started the ‘One District, One Product’ scheme in 2018, but Pratapgarh had already proved its talent before that,” he said. Yogi said those who could not even imagine before 2017 that a medical college would come up in Pratapgarh can now see the Dr Sonelal Patel Government Medical College functioning there. He added that a nursing college is also being built in the district. “Daughters of Pratapgarh will receive nursing education here and contribute to the health sector through their services in India and across the world,” he said. The Chief Minister said he got the opportunity to inaugurate and lay foundation stones of development projects related to both assembly constituencies. Recalling his previous visit, he said MLA Rajendra Maurya had complained about several pending works. “I told him — brother, all works will be completed, just feed me rasmalai one day,” Yogi said.

stories.title: Champat Rai's first statement on Ram Mandir donation theft:Shares letter, promise to answer all allegations after SIT submits its final report
stories.summary: Former Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust General Secretary Champat Rai, who is facing allegations in the Ram Mandir donation theft case, broke his silence for the first time on Tuesday. He posted a handwritten letter addressed to Lord Ram's devotees on his X account. Champat Rai began the letter with a verse from the Shri Ramcharitmanas, 'Dheeraj dharam mitra aru naari, aapad kaal parikhiyehin chaari', and said that since 2024, several allegations had been levelled against him over the alleged theft of donations during the counting of offerings. He added that he had deliberately chosen to remain silent. He said the Trust's meeting on Monday had been presented with the Special Investigation Team's (SIT) preliminary report, which has now been made public. As the report had earlier remained confidential, he had refrained from commenting. Champat Rai said he would respond with facts to all the allegations and what he described as a smear campaign only after the SIT completes its final investigation. He expressed confidence that the truth would emerge once the final report is released. In the letter, he also wrote that he was deputed to Ayodhya by his organisation in 1991. Describing his nearly 45-year public life as an "open book", he said he believed that truth would ultimately prevail. He concluded by saying that he respects the truth and would wait for the final investigation report before making any further statement. Champat Rai resigned as the Trust's General Secretary on 26 June, and his resignation was accepted during the Trust meeting on 6 July. He is currently in Ayodhya. Govind Dev Giri says Champat Rai had no moral involvement Speaking on Tuesday, Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust Treasurer Swami Govind Dev Giri Ji Maharaj said that when he described Champat Rai as "innocent", he meant there could be no moral or personal involvement on his part in the alleged wrongdoing. However, he added that Champat Rai had failed to exercise due caution. "He appointed a man with a criminal background as his driver. The driver had access to the keys and controlled everything. It was the driver who carried out all this. I suspect he had links with outsiders. This happened because there was no Chief Executive Officer (CEO). We will now appoint a CEO," he said. Meanwhile, the Trust's newly appointed General Secretary, Krishna Mohan Das, formally assumed charge on Tuesday. Three accused remanded to police custody for one day The Faizabad Anti-Corruption Court granted the police one day's remand of three accused, Karunesh Pandey, Anukalp Mishra and Lavkush. The police had sought seven days' custody. The three accused will now be brought from jail on Wednesday morning for questioning.

stories.title: UP to issue passport-style driving licences:Automatic test, police verification mandatory; cameras, sensors to decide pass or fail
stories.summary: Driving licences in Uttar Pradesh will soon be issued on the pattern of passports, with police verification becoming part of the process. After online slot booking, applicants will have to appear for an interview with officials, followed by a driving test. The Transport Department is expected to issue new rules soon. The government aims to ensure that licences are issued only to people who can drive properly and are aware of traffic rules. Digital token system will also be implemented in RTOs Like passport service centres, Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) will also introduce a digital token system. Applicants will receive tokens according to their scheduled time slots. Only after their number appears on the display screen will they be allowed to enter counters for biometric verification, photographs and other procedures. The move is expected to reduce overcrowding at RTO offices and limit the role of middlemen. Police verification before issuing driving licences Police verification will be carried out before issuing driving licences. At present, such verification is conducted only before issuing passports. It may include checking the applicant’s address and criminal record. The Transport Department is currently examining how the system can be implemented under existing laws. According to the department’s proposal, police verification will not be mandatory for everyone. It will apply in two situations: Cameras, sensors and computers will test your driving Till now, driving tests at RTOs were conducted manually. Under the new system, tests will be held at recognised high-tech driving training centres, where sensors, cameras and computer-based systems will assess driving skills. This will make it difficult to obtain licences through recommendations or bribery. Major RTOs in Uttar Pradesh, including Lucknow, Kanpur, Noida and Ghaziabad, are being connected with automated driving test tracks. These tracks have three types of tests: Chances of failing up to 40%, application cancelled if failed 3 times If the vehicle’s tyre touches the yellow line on the track or hits sensor-based poles during the test, the computer system will immediately mark the applicant as ‘FAIL’ without any human intervention. The failure rate in these tests is more than 40%. The automated driving test system has strict rules. If an applicant fails for the first time, they cannot appear for the test the next day. They will have to book a new slot after at least seven days. If an applicant fails three consecutive times, the application will be cancelled. The person will not be able to apply again for six months and will have to restart the entire process. Live photo and biometric verification before test When applicants reach the RTO, their live photograph and biometric details will be recorded and matched with Aadhaar data. The same person will then have to appear for the driving test. Biometric verification will also be done before the test, making it impossible for someone else to take the test on the applicant’s behalf. The entire process will be uploaded immediately on the government’s Sarathi portal, helping curb middlemen, recommendations and fake licences. 28-day training certificate holders to get exemption The government has also provided some relief. Applicants who complete 28 days of training at a government-recognised driving training centre and receive Form-5 will not need to appear separately for an RTO or automated track driving test. They will be directly issued a permanent driving licence. This exemption will only apply to certified Driving Training Centres (DTCs) recognised by the Transport Department. Changes being made to prevent road accidents According to the Transport Department, Uttar Pradesh currently has around 2.99 crore active driving licences. Lucknow RTO alone has issued the highest number of licences in the state, with around 13.66 lakh licences. Government inspections and road safety audits have found that many road users are unaware of traffic rules. To address this issue, the rules for issuing driving licences are being changed. stories.title: Man murdered two months after selling ₹2 crore plot:Bodies found in Jhajjar; faces beaten, attempt made to burn them
stories.summary: Several revelations have now emerged regarding the semi-naked dead body on Gurugram-Jhajjar Road. Family members say that the deceased Kamil had sold a plot worth about 2 crore rupees just 2 months ago. On July 4, he had gone to Neemrana in Rajasthan with his associate Irshad in a black Scorpio. Kamil used to run a PG here, while Irshad worked as a clerk in the same PG. On Monday morning, both their bodies were found near Sehwag International School in Jhajjar. Both bodies were lying on top of each other. One had a serious head injury. Near their bodies, a blue drum containing petroleum substance, a pipe, an iron sheet, and truck keys were found. Now Jhajjar police believe both were murdered over the 2 crore transaction. After that, their bodies were brought in a truck and dumped by the roadside. The accused were preparing to burn both bodies here, but as soon as they got wind of someone coming there, the accused fled from the spot. Police are also now investigating the transaction. Full sequence of the double murder case He said that they spoke on the phone on Sunday and everything seemed normal, but on Monday they received information about their murder. Irshad had worked with Kamal for 20 years Irshad’s brother Haqiqat said that Irshad had been living and working with Kamal for nearly 20 years. "Both worked together. Their relationship had become like that of a family. Irshad worked as a manager at the PG. Many times, they even visited home together," he said. After selling the plot, Kamal had also started working as a property dealer. Post-mortem of bodies will be done today Kamal is survived by three sons and three daughters. Two of his sons are married. Irshad’s family includes three daughters. The postmortem of both bodies will be conducted today. The report is expected to reveal the time of death, the method used in the crime and other important details. SHO said - Police investigating from every angle SHO Paramjeet said that police are investigating all possible angles, including financial transactions, property dealings and old rivalries. The investigation team is trying to identify the accused through technical evidence. Police said the complete case would be revealed soon.

stories.title: Newborn falls on floor after delivery, dies:Chaos at Lucknow government hospital; father alleges negligence, demands action
stories.summary: A newborn baby died after allegedly falling on the floor during delivery at a government hospital in Lucknow. The family created a ruckus, alleging that when they brought the woman to the hospital, they were told to wait until labour pain increased before conducting a normal delivery. The baby's father said it was his wife's first pregnancy and that she had delivered a baby boy. The incident took place at Lok Bandhu Raj Narayan Combined Hospital on Kanpur Road. Shubham, a resident of Sita Vihar Colony in Ashiyana, brought his pregnant wife to the hospital on Sunday evening after she developed labour pain. Shubham alleged that a cleaning staff member at the hospital demanded ₹500 for conducting the delivery. He claimed she told him, "The doctors give me ₹50, you give me ₹500 and I will get the delivery done." Read the child's father's allegation- Father alleges doctors delayed delivery, refused C-section The baby's father, Shubham Pal, said his wife was admitted around 4 pm on Sunday after she developed labour pain. "After admission, they kept waiting for the labour pain to increase and said that normal delivery would be done only after that. At the time of admission, doctors had said that if required, a C-section could also be performed," he said. Shubham alleged that even after five hours, normal delivery could not happen and his wife had become exhausted. "I requested them to perform a C-section, but the doctors said they did not have the facility for it. I then went to the director and told him the same. He said that the hospital had complete arrangements for a C-section," Shubham claimed. He said he submitted a written complaint to the hospital director, who assured him that the matter would be investigated and justice would be provided. Shubham also questioned whether doctors or interns were on duty during the incident, claiming that even the director did not have information about who was assigned duty at that time. My mother was pushed out of the labor room Shubham said he admitted his wife to the hospital at 4 pm on Sunday. Later, labour pain started again at around 4 am, after which she was taken to the labour room for an attempt at normal delivery until 8:30 am. "During this time, my mother was also inside the delivery room. The staff pushed her out. There was no doctor present there at that time," he alleged. He repeated that a cleaning worker told him that doctors paid her ₹50 and asked him to give ₹500 so she could get the delivery done. Baby fell on floor during delivery, family alleges doctors did not respond Shubham said his wife Kirti's condition kept worsening. Eventually, the delivery took place, but during the process, the baby fell on the floor and suffered a head injury. He alleged that despite the incident, no doctor came to check the patient in the ward. "The family created a commotion, after which some nursing staff and employees arrived," he said. Family members demanded CCTV footage The family alleged that doctors wanted to complete paperwork and send the deceased newborn home. Shubham refused to accept the body and demanded a postmortem. After receiving information about the protest, local police reached the hospital. Following the family's demand, police sent the newborn's body for postmortem. Shubham also demanded CCTV footage from the hospital administration to investigate what happened during the delivery. Hospital forms three-member committee Lok Bandhu Hospital Director Dr Rajesh Kumar said a three-member committee has been formed to investigate the matter. The committee will examine the family's written complaint and allegations. Statements of doctors, nursing staff and other employees present on duty will also be recorded. Medical records, duty rosters and the entire delivery process will be reviewed. If negligence is confirmed at any level, action will be taken against the concerned doctors and staff according to rules. The committee has been directed to submit its report soon. Deputy CM took cognizance, demanded report within 24 hours Deputy Chief Minister and Health Minister Brajesh Pathak has taken cognisance of the newborn's death. He has sought a report within 24 hours and directed the Director General of Medical and Health to investigate the matter. He said strict action should be taken against those found guilty and that negligence in healthcare services would not be tolerated. The government’s priority is to provide better treatment facilities to pregnant women and new mothers, he said.
