stories.title: Ram Mandir theft accused Avinash’s lavish spending exposed:Spent ₹6 lakh on brother’s wedding, gifted girlfriend an iPhone
stories.summary: The investigation into the Ram Mandir donation theft case has brought several new revelations during the questioning of accused Avinash Shukla. According to sources, Avinash admitted that a major portion of the allegedly stolen donation money was spent on his family, friends and personal expenses. He reportedly spent around ₹19 lakh on relatives and acquaintances. Sources said Avinash spent nearly ₹6 lakh on his brother’s wedding, gave around ₹5-6 lakh to another brother, gifted an iPhone to his girlfriend and transferred ₹2.5 lakh to her online. Investigating agencies are now examining these transactions, bank accounts and properties linked to the accused. Money transferred to others may be recovered During the investigation, it also emerged that Avinash bought a Brezza car by paying around ₹3.5 lakh as a down payment on loan. Police have already recovered the vehicle. Investigators have found that Avinash allegedly gave smaller amounts of money to several other people as well. Police questioned both of Avinash’s brothers and seized some documents. The land purchased in the name of his brother Abhishek Shukla in 2024 and related bank accounts are also being examined. Legal proceedings have been initiated to recover the money transferred to different people. Police recover ₹20.39 lakh cash, 1,121 dollars and jewellery So far, police have recovered ₹20.39 lakh in cash, 1,121 US dollars (around ₹1.06 lakh), gold and silver jewellery and other valuables from Avinash Shukla. On June 28, police raided Avinash’s yoga centre in Ayodhya. During the search, they recovered a box marked ‘Ramrajya Kosh’. A Paytm QR code was also attached to it. Police also found several documents and books related to the Ram Mandir from the premises. According to sources, Avinash’s brother Abhishek had once questioned accused Anukalp Mishra about the source of money. Anukalp allegedly avoided answering and warned him against asking further questions. Cash was recovered from the house on June 5 During the search of Avinash Shukla’s yoga centre in Ayodhya, police recovered several documents and books linked to the Ram Mandir. Earlier, on June 5, security personnel of the Trust had raided Avinash’s house. It was claimed that cash was recovered from the house. The recovered money was reportedly packed in bags and taken away by security personnel. Police are now examining the documents and other items recovered from Avinash to connect the missing links in the case. Yoga Center Staff Said - Avinash Came One and a Half Years Ago Yoga centre employees say Avinash joined around 1.5 years ago Shiv Sundar Lal, an employee at the yoga centre, said Avinash Shukla and his brother Abhishek had been associated with the centre for a long time. He said Abhishek had been staying there for around 10 years as he was associated with the centre since the time of the revered Guruji and used to serve him. Avinash also started living there with his brother around one-and-a-half years ago. “When we came to know that Avinash got a job at Ram Mandir, we were very happy. He used to leave for work on time every morning and return in the evening. His behaviour was always calm, polite and normal. He never gave any indication that could raise suspicion,” he said. However, after police arrived on June 5 and reports emerged about the recovery of cash bags during the search, everyone at the centre was shocked. “We never imagined that he could be involved in any illegal activity. As soon as the matter came out and reached the media, we took a strict stand,” he said. He added that keeping the reputation of the institution in mind, the family was asked on June 6 to make arrangements to leave the centre. “Whoever is guilty should get the strictest punishment under the law. We are fully cooperating with the investigation,” he said. Yoga trainer says Avinash was asked to leave after video surfaced Yoga instructor Seema Tiwari of Shyam Sadhnalaya Yoga Centre said Avinash had been living there for around one-and-a-half years, while his brother Abhishek had been there for about 10 years. She said the centre was run by Dr Chaitanya, who had educated and supported many young people and provided them shelter. Abhishek was also among them. She said Abhishek brought Avinash to the centre after informing them that he had got a job at the Ram Mandir. “When we heard that his name had appeared in the embezzlement case, we were shocked. Police came here on June 5. When the video went viral and we came to know that some bags were recovered from here, we spoke to Abhishek the next day,” she said. She added that they told the brothers, “Please leave from here. The centre’s reputation is being affected.” Avinash and Abhishek left the centre on June 6. Villagers claim Avinash built a new house Avinash Shukla, accused in the Ram Mandir donation theft case, is a resident of Babupur Nariyawa village under Maheshganj police station area. His father Ram Sajeevan Shukla is a farmer. Avinash is the second among five brothers. His elder brother Abhishek is a teacher in Ayodhya. Villagers told Dainik Bhaskar that Avinash’s ancestral house is a kutcha house where his parents live. However, a few months ago, Avinash and Abhishek built a new pucca house. Whenever the two brothers visited the village, they stayed in the newly built house. Avinash had been living in Ayodhya for one and a half years Avinash Shukla, accused in the Ram Mandir donation theft case, had been living in Ayodhya for the past one-and-a-half years. He was running a yoga centre and had also been working inside the Ram Mandir complex for the same period. His monthly salary was around ₹15,000. According to neighbours, Avinash and his brother used to sleep on the floor on blankets.

stories.title: SIT finds 70 theft incidents in Ram Mandir case:6 accused named after CCTV probe; staff seen hiding cash in pockets
stories.summary: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the alleged theft of donations at Ayodhya’s Ram Mandir submitted its preliminary report on Monday night around 9 pm, shortly after the Trust meeting where Champat Rai and Anil Mishra’s resignations were accepted. According to the report, nearly 70 suspicious incidents were captured on CCTV cameras between April 27 and June 5. The footage allegedly shows the eight accused, who are currently in police custody, hiding bundles of currency notes inside their pockets and shoes. The SIT has also levelled serious allegations against Dr Anil Mishra, saying he was responsible for loopholes in the existing search and security system that allowed the alleged theft to take place. The report states that Champat Rai’s driver Tinnu kept the keys of the counting room with him without any official order. It also alleges that he had recommended his nephew Manish Yadav for work related to counting donations. The Uttar Pradesh government had formed the SIT to investigate the alleged theft of Ram Mandir offerings. The team submitted its initial report to the government on June 23. The SIT includes Lucknow Divisional Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant, Lucknow Range IG Kiran S and Special Secretary in the UP Finance Department Neel Ratan. Key Points of SIT's Primary Report Anil Mishra held responsible for flaws in donation counting process The SIT said the entire process of counting donations was found to have several loopholes. According to the report, Dr Anil Mishra was overseeing financial matters and cash collection management. He also played an important role in preparing the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and coordination points with the bank. The SIT said he was responsible for ensuring proper monitoring of the process. Security system had loopholes despite information about missing searches The SIT stated that information about employees not being searched properly had already reached Anil Mishra through internal channels. However, despite this, no effective written order or instruction was issued to correct the problem. The report said the previously established search system was also weakened due to negligence attributed to Anil Mishra. No attendance system or paperwork increased chances of theft The SIT found that several important security measures were not properly implemented. These included: According to the report, weak monitoring encouraged accused employees and they continued stealing money from Ram Lalla’s treasury. Employees hid cash bundles in clothes, pockets, shoes and socks The SIT said CCTV footage recorded between April 27 and June 5, 2026 showed some employees working in the donation counting room repeatedly hiding currency bundles and loose notes inside their clothes, pockets, shoes and socks. The report said the absence of checking at entry and exit points made it possible to take cash outside the premises. Employees filled pockets with notes, alerted each other through signals The SIT said the incidents were not isolated but part of a repeated organised activity. The investigation recorded around 70 such incidents. Some employees were also seen using gestures to alert each other during the alleged thefts. Report reveals- 6 accused directly involved in theft According to the SIT, Avinash Shukla, Anukalp Mishra, Lavkush Mishra, Manish Kumar Yadav, Karunesh Pandey and Ramashankar Mishra appeared to be directly involved at the preliminary stage. The SIT said CCTV footage, recovery of stolen money and bank account investigations provided sufficient evidence against them. The report recommended registering cases against them under sections related to theft, criminal breach of trust, criminal misappropriation, possession of stolen property and conspiracy. Based on the SIT report, trustee Krishna Mohan filed the case. Later, the accused were arrested and are currently in jail. Avinash had ₹20.39 lakh cash, 1,121 dollars and car recovered According to police sources, accused Avinash has allegedly confessed that he spent around ₹19 lakh on friends and family members. He reportedly spent nearly ₹6 lakh on one brother’s wedding celebrations and gave ₹5 lakh to another brother. He also purchased a car worth ₹3.5 lakh. The investigation found that Avinash transferred around ₹2.5 lakh to a friend and also gifted him an expensive mobile phone. Officials are also investigating land purchased in 2024 in the name of his brother Abhishek Shukla. Legal action has been initiated to recover the money. So far, ₹20.39 lakh in cash, 1,121 US dollars, gold jewellery and silver ornaments have been recovered from Shukla. Tinnu had donation box keys without written order The SIT report also mentioned that Ramashankar Yadav alias Tinnu had control over the keys of temple donation boxes and related access arrangements without any formal written order. According to the report, on Tinnu’s recommendation, Manish Kumar Yadav was appointed for counting work, who was later found allegedly involved in theft. The SIT described this as a serious security lapse. Employees earning ₹20,000 had lakhs in accounts, financial transactions under scanner The SIT also examined bank accounts of the accused employees and their family members. According to the report, the employees earned around ₹20,000 per month, but their accounts showed large cash deposits, fixed deposits and other transactions that did not match their declared income. The SIT suspects that the stolen money may have been diverted into bank accounts and properties. A detailed investigation has been recommended into these transactions. 2 pictures related to the Ram Temple Trust meeting SIT says investigation still underway, final report will include more findings The SIT clarified that the current report is only a preliminary investigation. The team said investigation is still underway into security failures, responsibility of officials, system weaknesses, possible involvement of other people and measures needed to prevent such incidents in the future. Detailed findings and recommendations will be submitted to the government in the final report.

stories.title: 6-murder accused Asif Ali shot dead in STF encounter:2 bullets hit chest after firing at team, wanted in Jaunpur double murder
stories.summary: UP STF shot dead gangster Asif Ali (40) in an encounter in Ambedkar Nagar at around 4 am on Tuesday. STF officials said Asif opened fire after being surrounded, prompting retaliatory firing in which he was hit by two bullets in the chest. The encounter took place near Jagdishpur village, around 25 km from the district headquarters. Asif was the head of the Chhaimar gang and was wanted in six murders, including the killings of a husband and wife. Police said the gang used a distinctive modus operandi, carrying out robberies at night while dressed in underwear and vests. Members would enter homes, hold families hostage, loot valuables and kill victims before fleeing. Asif would then allegedly change his identity and hide in other districts and states. Investigators say almost all crimes linked to him followed the same pattern. According to Rajkumar Mishra, Additional SP of the Noida STF unit, Asif was wanted in a 2014 Jaunpur robbery in which two women were killed. Three others were also attacked but survived. Jaunpur Police had announced a reward of ₹1 lakh on him. He was facing 20 criminal cases across Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Haryana. STF surrounded him, he opened fire; killed in retaliatory firing According to the UP STF, they had received information from an informer that Asif was hiding in Ambedkar Nagar and was planning another crime. After this, the team surrounded him. Seeing himself trapped, Asif tried to escape by turning his bike. When the STF team chased him, he opened fire. A constable suffered a bullet injury in his right hand. Following this, the STF team retaliated. Two bullets hit Asif in the chest, after which he fell to the ground. The team rushed him to the district hospital, where he died during treatment. STF recovered a pistol, a country-made 12-bore firearm and a motorcycle from him. Chhaimar gang leader wanted in six murders Police describe the Chhaimar gang as a notorious criminal network operating mainly at night and involved in theft, robbery and dacoity. Members frequently shifted locations across Uttar Pradesh and other states to evade arrest, often using fake identities. The gang reportedly functioned in a manner similar to the Kachha-Baniyan and Bawaria gangs and followed a strict hierarchy. According to police, only a member involved in at least six murders could become the gang leader, which is why it came to be known as the Chhaimar gang. The most ruthless criminal within the group was given the title of "Rajkumar". Women were also part of the network and allegedly conducted reconnaissance during the day by posing as beggars or ragpickers. At night, gang members would hide near targeted homes before striking. Police said gang members worshipped Goddess Kali and offered liquor before carrying out robberies. They would then enter houses wearing only underwear and vests. If victims resisted, they were allegedly killed using sharp-edged weapons, as firearms could attract attention due to the sound of gunshots. ₹1 lakh reward announced after Jaunpur double murder Noida STF unit Additional SP Rajkumar Mishra said Ali and his gang had carried out a robbery in Jaunpur where two women were killed. Three other people were also attacked but survived. Following the incident, Jaunpur Police announced a reward of ₹1 lakh on information leading to Ali’s arrest. Police said 20 cases were registered against him across Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Haryana. Asif Ali’s major criminal cases On October 19, 2013, Asif and 10 gang members allegedly entered a house in Sultanpur, carried out a robbery and held the family hostage. One person was killed during the incident. In 2014, Asif and his associates allegedly entered a house in Shahganj, Jaunpur, held the family hostage and looted jewellery and cash worth lakhs of rupees. They also allegedly attacked five family members with sharp weapons. Two women, Swati and Suman, later died during treatment. On August 15, 2015, Asif and his gang members allegedly committed a robbery in Kaushambi, held the family hostage and killed a husband and wife. On August 19, 2015, Asif and 10 associates allegedly entered the house of Mahavir Singh in the Muzaffarnagar area and carried out a robbery. Mahavir’s daughter-in-law was allegedly attacked with a sharp weapon. The same night, the gang allegedly targeted five more houses. On January 13, 2021, Asif allegedly entered a house in Rasulabad, Kanpur Dehat, and killed a man named Tasim. Chhaimar gang: Daytime surveillance, night-time robberies The Chhaimar gang is considered one of Uttar Pradesh’s notorious criminal groups, known for carrying out thefts, robberies and dacoities at night. Police said the gang frequently changed locations across Uttar Pradesh and other states after crimes to avoid detection. The gang reportedly operates like the Kachha-Baniyan and Bawariya gangs, with strict internal rules. According to police, a person becomes the gang leader only after committing at least six murders, which is why the group is known as the “Chhaimar gang”. Police said members who commit more violent crimes gain higher status within the gang, with the most ruthless criminal being given the title of “Rajkumar”. Women are also allegedly part of the gang and conduct daytime surveillance by posing as beggars or waste collectors. Before targeting a house, gang members allegedly hide nearby at night. Police said they traditionally enter homes wearing vests and shorts and avoid using firearms during robberies to prevent attracting attention. If victims resist, they allegedly attack them with sharp weapons.

stories.title: Monsoon intensifies with heavy rain in UP:Highways waterlogged; roads turn into rivers in Mathura, cars swept away in Shamli
stories.summary: The monsoon has gathered pace across Uttar Pradesh. Since Tuesday morning, rainfall has been reported in around 50 cities, including Lucknow, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Chandauli and Moradabad. In Shamli, heavy rain turned roads into fast-flowing streams. Cars and motorcycles were seen being swept along by the water, while children were spotted swimming on flooded streets as if they were in a swimming pool. Flooding disrupts normal life in several districts In Vrindavan, Mathura, roads resembled rivers due to heavy rainfall. In Amroha, just one hour of rain caused waterlogging on the Delhi–Lucknow Highway. In Varanasi, rainwater cascaded down stairways like waterfalls. Strong winds forced boat operators to suspend services. In Hapur, markets were inundated, with floodwater entering shops. Traders were seen sitting on stools to keep themselves above the rising water. Rain alert issued for all 75 districts The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh on Tuesday, with heavy rainfall forecast in eight districts. Near the Maa Shakambhari Devi Temple in Saharanpur, the Shakambhari River witnessed a sudden surge in water levels, triggering panic among visitors. Police used loudspeakers to warn people to leave the riverbank immediately as water levels were rising rapidly. Heavy rain also affected rail services on Monday Rainfall was recorded in 48 cities across the state on Monday. At Varanasi railway station, rainwater began leaking through the roof onto Platform No. 8, with water pouring through a ceiling fan like a waterfall. During the past 24 hours, Auraiya recorded the highest rainfall in the state at 35.9 mm, which is 379% above its normal rainfall of 7.5 mm. See photos of rain- Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said a low-pressure area had formed over the north-west Bay of Bengal. It crossed the northern Odisha coast and is now centred over southern Jharkhand and northern Chhattisgarh. He said the system has significantly strengthened the monsoon across Uttar Pradesh, and heavy rainfall is likely at several places across the state.

stories.title: Ram Mandir trust members opposed Champat Rai's resignation:Accepted due to Trust constitution's rules; Gopal Rao told to leave premises
stories.summary: Place: Ram Mandir complex, Yatri Suvidha Kendra Time: 2:45 pm, July 6, 2026 The atmosphere inside the Ram Mandir complex turned tense on July 6 as the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust held a crucial meeting after the controversy over alleged theft of temple offerings. As the trust members gathered for the meeting, Treasurer Govind Dev Giri arrived at the Yatri Suvidha Kendra. The moment he stepped out of his vehicle, he spotted invited trust member Gopal Rao standing outside the facility. Giri appeared upset and told him, "Move away… leave from here. If you stay here, Nritya Gopal Das will not come." After hearing this, Gopal Rao paused for a moment, held his mobile phone in his hand and slowly walked towards the control room inside the Ram Mandir complex. He stayed there and did not come outside. Soon after this exchange, Govind Dev Giri entered the room where the important trust meeting was scheduled. Within around 15 minutes, all members reached the venue. Shortly afterwards, Trust President Mahant Nritya Gopal Das arrived in a wheelchair along with his disciple Kamal Nayan Das. Govind Dev Giri placed resignation papers before members and said: "Accept it or not..." The meeting room had sofas covered mostly with saffron cloth. Trustees including Dinendra Das, Swami Parmanand and Swami Vasudevanand were present. A laptop was placed on a table through which some trustees joined the meeting online. At exactly 3 pm, Govind Dev Giri began discussions on the agenda. He placed some documents on the table and said: “Ram devotees' faith has been hurt. Something unimaginable has happened. This has caused deep pain to Trust General Secretary Champat Rai. Until justice is properly delivered and the guilty are caught, it does not seem appropriate for him to continue in the Trust. He has submitted his resignation. Whether it should be accepted or not is not in our hands.” After making this statement, Giri stopped speaking. Silence prevailed in the room for some time. Later, most members expressed the view that Champat Rai's resignation should not be accepted. K. Parasaran read Trust rules, said resignation was automatically accepted Senior advocate K. Parasaran joined the meeting online. He explained that according to the Trust's constitution, a resignation submitted by a member is considered automatically accepted. He then displayed pages of the Trust constitution on the screen and read out the relevant clauses. This clarified to the members that they did not have the option to either accept or reject the resignation. According to the rules, the resignation had already come into effect once submitted. Following this, President Mahant Nritya Gopal Das, Dinendra Das and other trustees agreed to accept Champat Rai's resignation. Trustees express anger over Dr Anil Mishra’s role, call it negligence After Champat Rai's resignation, the meeting moved towards discussing the resignation of trustee Dr Anil Mishra. Most trustees appeared unhappy with him because the responsibility of the counting room was under his supervision. Members acknowledged that there had been clear negligence. The discussion then turned towards invited member Gopal Rao. Trustees said he was inducted into the Trust in 2020 but had not contributed towards improving temple arrangements. Members agreed to remove him from the Trust. Krishna Mohan’s name gets approval for general secretary post The trustees then discussed how the temple administration would function going forward. It was decided that Krishna Mohan would be appointed as the new general secretary to manage temple affairs. Most members agreed on his name. The trustees also agreed to appoint a Chief Executive Officer (CEO) in the future. Three names were shortlisted for setting the selection criteria: These three members will prepare the standards and present them before trustees during the July 22 meeting. Trust admitted, ‘People should have been told the right things’ During the meeting, trustees also discussed the issue of devotees claiming their donated items. Members admitted that the Trust had never clearly communicated the status of such offerings, leading to confusion among people. Treasurer Govind Dev Giri then presented a register containing details of 2,800 items. It was decided that the complete information should be made public. Champat arrived, but he was not included in the meeting Champat Rai also reached the Yatri Suvidha Kendra at the scheduled time. However, after some discussion with Trust members, he remained near the complex and did not enter the meeting room. Meanwhile, trustee Dr Anil Mishra did not attend the meeting.

stories.title: 'Honeymoon plan was a trap,' family alleges:Bihar woman dies in Lucknow, husband accused of planned murder over dowry disputes
stories.summary: "I can say with complete conviction that my sister-in-law was not the kind of person who would take her own life. She was a B.Sc graduate, academically bright and mentally strong. She faced every challenge head-on. She was murdered in a planned manner, and more than one person is involved. The accused husband first called her to Lucknow on the pretext of taking her to Kashmir for a honeymoon. Two days before the incident, he shifted to a new flat. After that, she was killed. The flat he moved into had no neighbouring tenants nearby, which made it easier to execute the crime without any disturbance. Our family wants justice. Police should arrest not only accused Kamalakant but also his family members." These are the allegations made by the victim's brother-in-law, Ravishankar Dubey. A 24-year-old woman from Bihar's Buxar district died under suspicious circumstances in Lucknow on 4 July, barely four months after her marriage. Her family has accused her husband and in-laws of dowry murder. The deceased has been identified as Sonali, daughter of Virendra Ojha, a resident of Khadhatand village in Buxar district. The accused, Kamalakant Mishra (28), belongs to Pinjarouli village under Sandesh police station limits in Bhojpur district. On the evening of 6 July 2026, Lucknow Police arrested Kamalakant after questioning him. Police are currently awaiting the post-mortem report. A team visited Sonali's parental home, located around 50 kilometres from the Buxar district headquarters, and spoke to her father, brother and brother-in-law. Now read the complete news in a sequential manner... First, see the pictures related to the incident... Son-in-law killed daughter after arranged marriage Family alleges husband photographed body before taking her to hospital According to the victim's family, photographs submitted to police show that instead of rushing Sonali to hospital, her husband first took pictures with her body. The family also produced WhatsApp chats in which Kamalakant allegedly abused Sonali, called her "illiterate" and used derogatory language. Father alleges repeated demand for car despite ₹15 lakh dowry Sonali's father, Virendra Jain, said his daughter married Kamalakant Mishra in an arranged marriage on February 26, 2026. He alleged that the family gave ₹15 lakh in cash, around 250 grams of gold jewellery and furniture worth nearly ₹2.5 lakh as dowry. "Despite this, Kamalakant and his family repeatedly demanded a car after the marriage," he said. According to him, for nearly two months after the wedding, Kamalakant neither took Sonali with him nor allowed her to go to her matrimonial home. The family allegedly insisted that she would be accepted only after a car was provided. After persuasion, they reportedly agreed to take Sonali but told her family that a car should be gifted later. Virendra alleged that Kamalakant's family wanted Sonali to be sent to her marital home with a car during the gauna ceremony. However, due to financial constraints, Sonali was sent to her in-laws in April 2026 with her brother Abhishek. After moving there, Sonali allegedly told her siblings that she was being abused, beaten and harassed for dowry. Her father claimed she sent screenshots of abusive messages from her husband to her brother. In the chats, Kamalakant allegedly threatened her, used obscene language, mocked her appearance and called her an "illiterate villager". He alleged that the accused had already planned the murder. See pictures of the wedding... Brother says Sonali spoke of harassment and later Kashmir honeymoon plan Sonali's brother Abhishek said she stayed at her parental home for two months after marriage and moved to her in-laws' house only in April 2026. He alleged that Sonali regularly informed the family that her in-laws, including her parents-in-law, sister-in-law, elder brother-in-law and his wife, verbally abused and physically assaulted her. When the family learned about the alleged harassment, they contacted her in-laws and told them that they had already spent everything they had and could not provide any additional dowry. Abhishek said Sonali spoke to him on June 20 and said Kamalakant was taking her to Kashmir for a honeymoon. "She told me that Kamalakant had started behaving lovingly and that everything between them was improving. She said he would take her from Ara to Lucknow by the end of the week and assured us that things would become normal," he said. The family believed the relationship was improving and hoped to discuss the car issue later. However, on June 26, Sonali reportedly called her brother in tears and said Kamalakant had abused her, called her uneducated and that she no longer wanted to go with him. The family assumed it was a temporary marital dispute and advised her to talk things through. On June 28, Sonali travelled from Ara to Lucknow. Couple was scheduled to leave for Kashmir on July 5 The couple was supposed to fly to Jammu and Kashmir on July 5. However, on the afternoon of July 4, Kamalakant called Abhishek and informed him that Sonali had died by suicide. He also allegedly sent a WhatsApp photograph showing Sonali lying on the floor while he was posing beside her body. The family maintains that Sonali was murdered and that an attempt was made to portray it as suicide. They claimed that when they saw the body, they noticed injury marks not only around her neck but also on both hands and legs. According to the family, these injuries suggest that Sonali's hands and legs may have been restrained before she was killed. They have demanded a fair investigation into the role of Kamalakant and other family members. Abhishek said the family possesses WhatsApp chats and other evidence showing prolonged harassment and threats against Sonali, which they plan to submit before investigators and the court. They have appealed to the government and administration to ensure a scientific, transparent and impartial probe. Injury marks found on neck, legs and hands Ravishankar Dubey, Sonali's brother-in-law, said he lives in Ara and works with the railways in Madhya Pradesh. He said he reached home immediately after receiving information about the incident. "I have known Sonali for eight years. Based on her personality and determination, I can say with certainty that she was not someone who would commit suicide. She was mentally strong and faced every challenge fearlessly," he said. He alleged that the death appeared to be a carefully planned murder disguised as suicide. Dubey said the injury marks on Sonali's neck, hands and legs raise suspicion that more than one person may have been involved. At the same time, he acknowledged that the truth would emerge only after the post-mortem report, forensic examination and an impartial police investigation. He urged authorities not to close the case by treating it as a suicide and instead investigate every angle scientifically. Family questions lack of public support Dubey also expressed disappointment over what he described as a lack of public attention. He referred to the recent Bharat Tiwari murder case, saying society, media and public representatives had raised their voices strongly in that matter. "What happened to him was wrong and the guilty should be punished. But similar sensitivity is not being shown in our daughter's case," he said. He alleged that people still try to murder women and disguise such crimes as suicides. The family claimed that no social organisation, community representative or public figure had visited them to understand what happened. They further alleged attempts were made to suppress the case and claimed police were initially reluctant to conduct a post-mortem examination. According to them, the autopsy was carried out only after persistent pressure from family members. Dubey appealed to society, the media and authorities to treat the matter seriously, saying it was not just about one family's daughter but about justice and safety for all women. He said the family would cooperate fully with investigators and provide every piece of evidence available with them. "Our only demand is a fair and thorough investigation so that the truth comes out and whoever is responsible receives the strictest punishment under the law," he said. Husband claims dispute began after flight tickets were cancelled During questioning, Kamalakant told Lucknow Police that he and Sonali could not go on a honeymoon immediately after marriage because of his job commitments. He said they planned a trip to Kashmir a month ago and booked flight tickets. According to him, bad weather forced him to cancel the July 3 flight and book train tickets instead. He claimed Sonali became upset because she wanted to travel by air and that an argument followed despite his attempts to calm her down. Kamalakant said he left for work at around 10 am on July 4 as usual. At around noon, he called Sonali but received no response. He then contacted the landlord and asked him to check on her. According to his statement, the landlord found the door locked from inside. Kamalakant said he rushed home and found Sonali hanging from the ceiling when he opened the door. Following a complaint filed by Sonali's brother Abhishek, Indiranagar Police in Lucknow registered a case of dowry death and other related charges against six members of the husband's family, including Kamalakant, his mother Ramavati, father Shardanand, sister Girija Chaubey, elder brother Laxmikant and sister-in-law Lakshmi. Police have arrested Kamalakant and seized the mobile phones of the husband and wife. Investigators have recovered chats exchanged between the couple as well as conversations between Kamalakant and his sister Girija. According to police sources, the chats allegedly contain references to "teaching Sonali a lesson" and even discussions about taking her life.

stories.title: Shankaracharya's sexual exploitation case was 'conspiracy':Ashutosh Maharaj used threats to secure false statements, claims 'batuk'
stories.summary: At the Magh Mela in Prayagraj, chants from a tent marked the conclusion of a yajna ceremony. After the ritual ended, Shakambhari Peethadheeshwar Ashutosh Brahmachari allegedly called two batuks, placed his hand on their heads, gave them ₹6,000 each as dakshina, collected their Aadhaar cards for making dakshina cards and obtained their signatures on blank sheets of paper. According to an investigation by Dainik Bhaskar, it was from this point that an alleged conspiracy to implicate Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand in a sexual exploitation case began. The report claims Ashutosh later used those signed blank papers to prepare statements alleging sexual harassment. Bhaskar said it conducted a four-month investigation, during which a batuk, his father and uncle spoke on hidden camera about the alleged sequence of events. Why these two batuks were allegedly chosen The report traces the story back nearly a year. The two batuks had participated in yajnas held in two different cities of Uttar Pradesh and had reportedly received ₹60,000 each as dakshina. It was during this period that they came into contact with Ashutosh Maharaj. According to the investigation, four reasons were cited for allegedly choosing them as complainants in the Shankaracharya case: Batuk says he never knew or met the Shankaracharya Dainik Bhaskar reporters visited a village near Lucknow where one of the batuks lives with his family. They first spoke to the batuk. Reporter: Do you know Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand? Batuk: No, I do not know him. Reporter: Have you ever met him? Batuk: No. Reporter: Did you ever go to his ashram to study? Batuk: No, never. Reporter: Do you know what the case was about? Batuk: No, I did not know. I came to know later. Reporter: What did you come to know later? Batuk: That Ashutosh made us level false allegations. Reporter: What allegations? Batuk: Allegations of sexual misconduct. Reporter: Did anything like that ever happen to you? Batuk: No, never. Reporter: Never? Batuk: Never. Reporter: How did Ashutosh take you along with him? Batuk: We had gone there to perform a yajna. He had called us to Prayagraj saying some acquaintances had organised a programme and that two of us should come. I and another batuk went there. Ashutosh then told us that we had to give testimony for Lord Krishna. During the conversation, the batuk's uncle arrived and took the reporters towards the fields outside the village. Reporter: When did the batuk go to Ashutosh's ashram? Uncle: During Magh, in January. Reporter: How did he go? Who took him there? Uncle: A person named Devikishore (name changed), who is older than him. We can introduce you to him. He took him there. Earlier, they had earned ₹60,000 from yajnas. He called and said, come with us and you will earn good money. They got tempted. Reporter: Then what happened? Uncle: We do not know how they trapped him. They said it was a case related to Laddu Gopal. Ashutosh came home carrying large idols of Laddu Gopal and said a case was going on in which they had to testify. How was the boy supposed to know whether he was giving testimony for Laddu Gopal or for someone else? Reporter: How much money have you received so far? Batuk: ₹6,000. Reporter: Did he mention the name of any official? Batuk: No. Reporter: Did he say that if you gave your statement, you would get something in return? Batuk: He said we would live in Mathura. He asked us to testify for Lord Krishna. He said a temple-house would be arranged there and life would be comfortable. The reporters then spoke to the batuk's father, who broke his silence for the first time. Reporter: Do you know what happened? Father: We have nothing to do with this. If someone can safely take us and safely bring us back, then we will tell everyone the truth. This boy is my son, and he has been trapped. Batuk says he was taken away while appearing for an exam The reporters later spoke jointly to the batuk, his father and uncle. Reporter: Did you stay with Ashutosh? Batuk: Yes, we had gone for a yajna. Uncle: The Aadhaar cards given for preparing dakshina cards were later used for everything else. Reporter: The FIR says that you studied at Shankaracharya's place and that he sexually assaulted you and made you sleep beside him. Was anything like that true? Batuk: No, I never even went there. Uncle: If he never went there, how could he tell lies? We too have to answer before God one day. The child went to Prayagraj for the first time. He went because of money or temptation. Reporter: Did Ashutosh make you level allegations that something wrong had happened? Uncle: Yes. Reporter: Did he promise money or anything else? Father: He said there would be ₹21,000 as dakshina. Batuk: I was writing an examination at school. Ashutosh sent two boys outside the school. They forced me and my father onto a motorcycle. Reporter: Where did they take you? Batuk: To a hotel. Then an SUV came and we were taken to Lucknow. Uncle: They effectively kept him under control for four or five days. Father: I was with him. They took away our mobile phones. We were locked inside two or three rooms. We kept crying. There were policemen there too. We pleaded with them to let us go, otherwise we would kill ourselves. Only then were we sent back home in a private vehicle. Signatures allegedly taken in advance on blank papers According to the report, Ashutosh anticipated that the batuk or his family might back out later. To ensure that his alleged conspiracy did not weaken, he first got both batuks to sign blank papers in the name of preparing dakshina cards. He later allegedly wrote statements of sexual exploitation on those papers himself. Reporter: The FIR states that you had gone to Prayagraj during the Kumbh. Is that true? Batuk: No, I never went there. Reporter: Then how did allegations of sexual assault get written into the FIR? Batuk: Ashutosh submitted written statements on his own. Reporter: But the signatures are yours. Batuk: He had taken our signatures earlier in the name of preparing dakshina cards. He said he would make dakshina cards for us and asked us to sign. Reporter: Did you read the FIR? Batuk: No. What is the current status of this case? Police are still investigating the matter. So far, no chargesheet has been filed before the court, nor has police questioned Avimukteshwaranand. Shankaracharya's disciple Mukundanand Giri has approached the court claiming the case is false. The matter is scheduled for hearing on 28 July. After speaking to the batuk and his family members, Dainik Bhaskar also spoke to Ashutosh Maharaj.

stories.title: Violence after child dies in accident:Tractor-trolley set ablaze; police drive away protesters after lathi-charge
stories.summary: In Aligarh on Thursday, a 14-year-old boy died after being crushed under a tractor-trolley. This sparked anger among the people. They placed the body on the road and blocked traffic. They set fire to the tractor-trolley loaded with wheat. Firefighters who arrived after receiving information brought the fire under control. Police tried to pacify the protesting people. However, the family members remained adamant on their demand for compensation of one crore rupees and arrest of the accused driver. Police officers had to face opposition from the people. However, as the commotion escalated, police dispersed the crowd. The incident occurred at 4:10 PM in Chandaus town, about 35 km away from the district headquarters. The deceased was identified as Vansh Pratap (14), son of Kalicharan. See 5 pictures Now know the sequence of events in detail... The deceased boy was studying in 8th grade Vansh, a resident of Elampura village in Aligarh, was an 8th-grade student. He had come to the nearby Chandaus town on a bike with his cousin brother around three o'clock on Thursday afternoon to get samosas. After getting the samosas packed, both brothers were returning to the village. At 4:10 PM on the Chandaus-Pisawa road, near Khair Adda, the bike suddenly skidded. Vansh came under the rear wheel of a tractor-trolley loaded with wheat that was moving alongside, resulting in his death on the spot. Meanwhile, his cousin brother also sustained minor injuries. Relatives adamant on demanding action As soon as the news of the accident reached the village, hundreds of people from the village along with family members reached the spot. Angered by Vansh's death, people set the tractor-trolley on fire. Within moments, the trolley started burning. Due to the arson and protest, a chaotic situation developed at the scene. As soon as the information was received, the Kotwali police, administrative officers, and fire brigade team reached the spot. However, the angry crowd prevented the police from lifting the body and the fire brigade from extinguishing the fire. For a long time, police officers tried to convince the people, but they remained adamant on their demand for action. Uncle said - Ambulance arrived two hours later Vansh's uncle Arjun Singh said - The ambulance did not reach the spot until about two hours after the incident. How did heavy and overloaded vehicles reach the area where no-entry is enforced. The police take bribes and allow heavy vehicles to come and go in the no-entry zone. The accident occurred due to police negligence. A fair investigation of this entire matter should be conducted. The guilty police personnel should be identified and strict action should be taken against them. Tension in the area, heavy police force deployed After the incident, there was a tense atmosphere in Chandaus town. Considering the situation, additional police force was called to the spot. The police kept trying to pacate people and normalize the situation. Meanwhile, SP City Aditya Bansal and CO Gabhana Mahesh Kumar reached the spot. They assured appropriate action on all demands of the family members. After this, around quarter past seven in the evening, the family members handed over the body to the police. The police took possession of the body and sent it for post-mortem.

stories.title: ‘No offerings, no votes for BJP’:Akhilesh Yadav dares BJP to hold polls in September
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav held a press conference on Thursday afternoon at around 3:30 PM in Lucknow. During this, he raised questions on the role of the government and trust regarding the Ram Mandir donation controversy. He said - Ram Mandir was forcibly occupied. No account was given of the donations coming to the temple. Despite complaints, the police took no action. He also claimed that the UP assembly elections should be held in September instead of November. We are fully prepared. SP has never broken and will never break. During this, Harishankar Safariwala, the Panch Pramukh of Ayodhya's 'Mandir Ram Niwas', was also present. Along with this, Akhilesh also cornered the government on law and order, cybercrime, expressway quality, and the 2027 assembly elections. Read the major statements made by Akhilesh SP is the only party that has not split Akhilesh Yadav said- Samajwadi Party is the only party that has not split till date. BJP has betrayed both the Constitution and God. They betrayed the Constitution, they betrayed God. When the public learns the truth about donation theft, they will remove them from power in the assembly elections and they will be wiped out. If the government is serious about corruption, then bulldozers should be run on the houses of the accused arrested in the Ram Temple donation theft case as well. Donations were stolen by turning off CCTV Akhilesh said that in a state where CCTV is turned off and temple offerings can be stolen, the increase in incidents like cyber fraud is not a big deal. This raises serious questions about the state's security system and surveillance mechanism. Lord Shri Ram himself will take account of this entire matter. The Samajwadi Party will continue to work towards building a nation of brotherhood and harmony. There is a poll in the news, you can participate before moving ahead The public should get an account of the offerings Akhilesh Yadav said - The allegations of irregularities in the offerings received in the name of Lord Ram are extremely serious. The complete account of devotees' donations should be made public. If there is no transparency even in matters related to faith, people's trust will be broken. The impact of this issue will also be visible in the elections. This time BJP will get neither donations, nor offerings, nor votes. We are ready for the 2027 elections If the government wants to hold the 2027 assembly elections before the scheduled time, the Samajwadi Party is fully prepared for it. Those who wanted to hold elections in November, let them hold them in September itself, we are ready. During the press conference, someone said that BJP people say that you are not a devotee of Ram. On this, Akhilesh said in an interesting manner - I am getting a temple built. From now on, whoever questions about God, I will collect donations from them for the temple. Police stations are working at the government's behest Akhilesh mentioned the murder of Sandeep Yadav in Siddharthnagar and an incident in Kaushambi. He said that the police in the state are not working impartially. Victims are not getting justice in many cases. There is political pressure on police stations. Cyber crimes are increasing rapidly in UP. In many cases, FIRs are not even registered and actual figures are not brought forward. Quality of expressway deteriorated due to corruption Referring to the Bundelkhand Expressway, Akhilesh said that flaws in the road came to light shortly after its inauguration. Quality is being compromised in development projects. Such situations are arising due to corruption. Farmers and Traders' Discontent in Ayodhya Became Reason for Defeat Referring to the Lok Sabha elections, Akhilesh said that the discontent of farmers and traders in Ayodhya became a major reason for BJP's defeat. There was dissatisfaction among local people due to land acquisition for the airport and other projects and displacement of traders. Its impact was visible in the election results. Made Several Promises for Sikh Community In a press conference, Akhilesh Yadav said that when the Samajwadi Party government is formed, the Sikh community will be given proper representation in power and organization. He also promised to resolve land-related disputes, raise the issue of release of imprisoned Sikhs, and give priority to eligible Sikh candidates in elections. Akhilesh concluded by saying that SP will continue to struggle for democratic values and protection of the Constitution. It will continue to strongly raise public issues. Meanwhile, Harishankar Safariwala alleged that Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust's General Secretary Champat Rai has occupied his historic temple. Safariwala claimed that the temple's donation money has also been withheld. He was lured with crores of rupees to suppress the matter. He tried to file a complaint with the police, but no action was taken. Business is being done in the name of religion and faith.

stories.title: Sanjay Nishad threatens party leader:‘Even your father will do the work’| WATCH
stories.summary: UP government's Cabinet Minister and Nishad Party's National President Dr. Sanjay Nishad reached Jalaun at 1:30 PM on Thursday. During the program here, he got angry at his state secretary. He reprimanded state secretary Bharat Lal right on the stage. He said, "Get your mind right, I will set your mind right, even your father will do the work." A video of the incident has surfaced. In the video, leaders and workers present nearby can be seen trying to mediate. Read the complete matter Dr. Sanjay Nishad had arrived on Thursday to attend a booth workers' conference at Shyam Palace in the Kalpi assembly constituency of Jalaun. During the conference, he was being welcomed. Meanwhile, around 1:45 PM, a dispute arose over the stage arrangements during the garland ceremony. State Secretary Bharat Lal suggested removing the women present on the stage. The minister got angry over this remark. He reprimanded Bharat Lal right from the stage. An argument began between the two. Seeing the situation deteriorate, leaders and workers present on the stage intervened to mediate. Bharat Lal said that he has been working for the party for a long time, but he is not getting opportunities according to his hard work. At this, Dr. Sanjay Nishad lost his temper. He said that work has to be done. Your father will also have to do it. Set your mind right... I will set your mind right. Party losing due to traitors Dr. Sanjay Nishad said that there were some seats where the party's victory was almost certain, but due to some traitors, the party had to face defeat. He claimed that he has a list of such people. Organizational action will be taken against them. Meanwhile, on the Ram Mandir donation issue in Ayodhya, the minister said that the government is keeping a serious watch on the entire matter. Investigation agencies are doing their work. If anyone is found guilty, strict action will be taken against them according to law. They will be sent to jail. Appeal to strengthen booths While addressing the conference, Dr. Sanjay Nishad appealed to the workers to strengthen the organization up to the booth level. He said that previous governments ignored the rights of the Nishad community. He called upon the workers to unite and fight for the rights of the community and engage in preparations for the assembly elections. State Secretary Bharat Lal said that the party's dedicated and active workers are being ignored. stories.title: Reshuffle in UP police department, 125 DSPs transferred:Kamlesh Kant sent to Noida; Ashok Singh transferred to Gorakhpur
stories.summary: The Yogi government transferred 125 DSPs on Thursday afternoon at 2:30 PM. Most of these are those who were promoted from Inspector. DSP Kamlesh Kant from Moradabad has been sent to Noida Commissionerate. Shiv Thakur from Saharanpur has been sent to Meerut. Manjari Rao has been made Deputy Superintendent of Police of Ballia. Shilpa Verma has been sent to Kannauj. Apart from this, Ashok Kumar Singh has been made DSP in Gorakhpur Railway from DSP Sant Kabir Nagar. Imran Khan has been appointed as Assistant Commandant in Prayagraj PAC from Lalitpur. Dharmendra Singh Yadav has been made DSP of Moradabad Police Academy from PAC Lucknow. Apart from this, changes have also been made in the Chief Minister's security. Sudhakar Dwivedi and Bhanu Pratap Singh from Lucknow Commissionerate have been deployed in the Chief Minister's security. stories.title: ₹3 crore rent, ₹200 crore scam:Fake call centre operated from luxury commercial tower In Lucknow; 119 people detained
stories.summary: A fake international call centre operating from Lucknow's Summit Building has been busted, exposing what police believe was a large-scale cyber fraud network targeting foreign nationals. The office, which reportedly cost nearly ₹3 crore a year to run, recruited employees through a five-stage interview process. When police received information that the operation was not a legitimate call centre but a cyber fraud hub, they raided the premises on Wednesday afternoon. The operation led to the detention of 119 people. Police also seized 100 laptops, 178 calling phones, digital devices and several documents. When Dainik Bhaskar visited the site after the raid, the office was locked, but the lavish interiors inside the hall reflected the scale of the operation. Family members of one employee reached the building soon after the raid. While they refused to speak on camera, they revealed that their son had cleared five interview rounds to get the job. Most employees were paid between ₹25,000 and ₹28,000 a month, but those involved in successful scams allegedly received a 10% commission from the amount defrauded. Here's how the gang allegedly operated, who worked there, how much they earned, how the racket was exposed, and how much money investigators believe has been siphoned off. See 2 pictures- Modus operandi of the fraudsters- The scamsters would become active at night According to preliminary police findings, the group was running an application called Dollar App under the guise of a call centre. Through it, callers allegedly lured victims from different countries and cheated them over the phone. The centre functioned primarily between 7 pm and 3 am, with overseas customers being the main targets. The accused had rented two offices on the 11th floor of Summit Building and were allegedly operating under the company name Solaris Solution. Mastermind sitting abroad would hire employees and get the work done During the raid, police detained Narayandas Khairajani, Lalit Khairajani from Ahmedabad, Gujarat, and Vikram Singh Parmar. Both Lalit and Parmar currently reside in Gomti Nagar Extension and were working as operation managers. Police believe they handled the India-based operations and supervised a large team of employees. Investigators are now questioning them to identify and reach the main mastermind, who is suspected to be operating from abroad. They would trap victims on refund processing or Google search Police say the fraudsters exploited online refund queries. People often search online for refund assistance after making purchases. Investigators claim that once a person searched for refund-related information, their details reached the fraudsters. The scammers would immediately call back, pose as customer support executives and guide victims through various processes. Eventually, they would obtain OTPs and gain access to bank accounts, siphoning off money. Working and Salary- Majority were girls from North-East Police sources say a significant number of employees were women from North-Eastern states. During questioning, many reportedly admitted they joined the company because of the promise of high earnings. Investigators believe their fluent English and neutral accents helped convince foreign nationals that they were speaking to genuine representatives. This, police say, made it easier to gain trust and execute the scams. Bonus was more than salary Employees at the call centre were required to communicate entirely in English. Their monthly salary ranged between ₹25,000 and ₹28,000, but the major attraction was the incentive structure. Workers allegedly received 10% of the amount recovered through fraud, which often exceeded their fixed pay. According to sources, some employees were earning between ₹80,000 and ₹1 lakh every month through commissions alone. Investigators also believe that most employees were aware that the operation involved fraudulent activities. Income and Expenditure- Defrauded more than 200 crore rupees Based on the evidence recovered, police suspect the network may have cheated foreign citizens out of more than ₹200 crore. Investigators say victims were trapped using different kinds of inducements and deceptive tactics. All electronic devices seized during the raid have been sent for forensic examination, while financial transactions and money trails are also being scrutinised. Sources claim the office occupied two sections of the building and incurred an annual expense of around ₹3 crore, including rent and operational costs. The call centre had reportedly been functioning for nearly a year. Officials believe the investigation began after complaints were received from overseas, eventually leading to the crackdown. All documents will be sent for forensics Crime branch officials said all recovered digital devices and documents have been taken into custody for technical and forensic analysis. The aim is to identify the broader cybercrime network, trace victims, understand the calling modules and uncover crucial evidence linked to financial transactions. ADCP Crime Kiran Yadav said the investigation is continuing and efforts are underway to arrest the remaining accused at the earliest.

stories.title: Mother files FIR against PCS officer daughter:Alleges ₹15 lakh black money deposited in her account, land mafia links
stories.summary: A case has been registered against five people, including a District Supply Officer (DSO) posted in Hapur, in Saharanpur. The FIR has been filed on the complaint of her mother. On 30 June, police registered the case under charges of cheating, forgery, criminal conspiracy and criminal intimidation. The complainant, the mother of the DSO, has alleged that her daughter used her bank account to hide “illicit income”. She claims that ₹15 lakh was deposited into her account without her permission or knowledge, and that there was an attempt to grab her land. She further alleges she was threatened with death when she objected. The case has been registered at Sarsawa police station. ‘My bank account was used without consent’, says mother Munesh Rani, a resident of Mirpur Sitapur village, said her daughter Seema had opened a bank account in her name at an ICICI Bank branch in Ghaziabad and operated it herself. She alleged that she was never informed about the transactions in the account. She came to know about the matter only after receiving a message on her mobile phone. When she checked at the bank, the details were confirmed. She further alleged that ₹15 lakh was deposited into her account by her daughter, and claimed it was done to conceal her daughter’s “illegal earnings”. Daughter accused of being part of land mafia gang The complainant has further alleged that her daughter is part of a land mafia gang. She claims Seema, along with Sanjeev Chaudhary and Gambhir from Mirpur Sitapur (Sarsawa), Rajendra Rana from Mirpura village in Baghpat, and Naresh Kumar from Pahlanpur village in Sarsawa, conspired to grab her land. She alleged that a forged receipt dated 16 September 2023 was created using fake signatures in an attempt to take over her property. She said she came to know about it through the tehsil administration. When she opposed the alleged attempt, she was threatened with death, she further claimed. She also said she was forced to sell her land to Nancy, a resident of Dehradun. She added that she first filed a complaint at Sarsawa police station on 13 May, but no action was taken. She later approached the SSP, after which the FIR was registered on 30 June around 4:30 pm against Seema Chaudhary and four others. Police say investigation underway Police have registered the case under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 506 of the IPC based on the complaint and have begun an investigation. Officials said a fair and impartial probe is underway, and the allegations will be verified during the investigation before any conclusion is reached.

stories.title: Lucknow Sahara City land battle escalates:270-acre green belt dispute reaches Supreme Court after 30 years
stories.summary: The long-running dispute over 270 acres of land developed as Sahara City in Lucknow’s Gomti Nagar has now reached the Supreme Court. The Municipal Corporation claims that Sahara violated lease conditions by carrying out residential and commercial construction on land originally allotted for a green belt, and also says the 30-year lease period has expired. On the other hand, Sahara argues that it has invested ₹2,480 crore in the project and that the land was taken over without following due legal procedure. Meanwhile, the state government is preparing plans to build a new Assembly complex on the same land, with the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) assigned responsibility. The land was originally allotted by the Lucknow Municipal Corporation to Sahara India on a ₹100 stamp paper. The key question now is who has the legal right over this land. At present, the Municipal Corporation has taken possession, alleging breach of lease conditions. The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear the matter on 31 July. 100-rupee lease that sparked a 270-acre dispute The dispute over 270 acres in Vipul Khand, Gomti Nagar, dates back nearly three decades. It began on 22 October 1994, when the Lucknow Municipal Corporation allotted the land to Sahara India Housing Limited through a licence deed executed on a ₹100 stamp paper. Under the agreement, the company was required to pay ₹1,000 per acre as a fee. The parcel included around 170 acres of Municipal Corporation land and 100 acres of LDA land. A key condition of the lease was that the entire area would be developed as a green belt. Petitioner advocate BK Singh alleges that the lease process itself was against rules from the beginning. According to him, allotting such a large parcel on a ₹100 stamp paper for 30 years did not comply with LDA regulations. After the completion of the 30-year period, the Municipal Corporation has alleged that the land was used for purposes contrary to the agreement and that lease conditions were violated. On this basis, in September 2025, the Corporation cancelled the lease and took possession of the land. 'Land was given to Sahara bypassing rules' In the ongoing legal battle, petitioner advocate B.K. Singh has consistently described the lease as illegal and against regulations. He says that in 1994–95, the Municipal Corporation and LDA bypassed rules while allotting the land to Sahara. No registered deed was executed; instead, the lease was granted on stamp paper with an annual rent of ₹1,000 per acre, which he claims was not as per prescribed procedures. According to him, the land was meant exclusively for green belt development under the master plan, but later commercial activities and construction began. He alleges that several structures within the complex violate lease conditions. Singh further says that instead of challenging these orders directly, the matter was prolonged through multiple litigations for years. He argues that the 30-year lease period has now ended, and no authority is obligated to renew it. He also cites a 2017 award by Justice Kamlesh Nath, stating that the matter linked to SEBI proceedings should be resolved first, but reiterates that no authority can be forced to extend a lease. He maintains that the land was never used for its intended purpose, and instead of a green belt, it was turned into a commercial zone. He adds that the High Court has also made observations in this regard. Singh claims Sahara has already failed to obtain relief from the Supreme Court in the past and argues that violation of lease terms gives the government full right to reclaim the land. He further says that Municipal Corporation is only a custodian of public property, while LDA should have strictly followed legal procedures during allotment. Municipal corporation’s stand: lease violations alleged The Municipal Corporation maintains that the land allotted for green belt development was gradually converted into residential and commercial use. According to the Corporation, luxury bungalows, a modern theatre, a 5,000-capacity auditorium, and even airport-like security arrangements were developed within the premises. It alleges that the original lease conditions were not followed and that about 40 acres were meant to remain reserved as green belt, but were diverted for other uses, violating land use regulations. Officials say several notices were issued in 2020 and again in 2025, but no corrective action was taken. The Corporation claims adequate opportunity was given to rectify violations, but compliance never followed. Land was to be used for Green Belt As per the lease deed, the land was to be used exclusively for developing a green belt in the city, with no commercial use permitted. Around 40 acres were to remain green area, and any construction was to follow LDA and Municipal Corporation rules. No deviation from land use norms was allowed, and all fees and conditions had to be followed regularly. The Municipal Corporation states that if lease conditions are violated, the lease can be terminated and possession of land can be taken back. It further claims the licence deed was terminated as early as 1997, followed by multiple notices, and formal action was taken in 2025. The LDA first cancelled the lease, followed by the Municipal Corporation’s action. How much money did Sahara pay to the Municipal Corporation and LDA in exchange for the land? Advocate B.K. Singh claims that the 270 acres were given on a ₹100 stamp paper. He says a land development agreement was made between the Municipal Corporation, LDA, and Sahara India, but the entire lease process was against rules. He also states that Sahara has claimed in court that it invested around ₹2,480 crore in the project and developed over 87 buildings. The company has also said it was willing to deposit additional funds for lease renewal if required. Sahara's petition was dismissed on April 22, 2026 The Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court rejected Sahara’s petition on 22 April 2026. Following this, Sahara moved the Supreme Court through a Special Leave Petition (SLP). In its plea, Sahara referred to an arbitration order by retired Justice Kamlesh Nath and argued that it supported lease renewal considerations. Here is the English translation of the infographic detailing Sahara's arguments in the Supreme Court: What arguments did Sahara present in the Supreme Court? The 2017 arbitration order is in its favor: In September 2017, the decision in the mediation/arbitration case was ruled in favor of Sahara. The entire land is not a green belt: The company claims that the Municipal Corporation is taking action on wrong grounds by declaring the entire area a green belt. Crores of rupees were invested: Sahara states that it has spent approximately ₹2,480 crore (24.8 billion rupees) on the project. Principles of natural justice were not followed: Possession of the land was taken away without providing an adequate or fair opportunity to be heard. Were ready to extend the lease: If any fee or charges were required to be paid, the company was completely ready to deposit it. What has the Supreme Court asked? On 29 May 2026, a bench comprising Chief Justice Suryakant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice Vipul M. Pancholi issued notices seeking responses from the government, Municipal Corporation and LDA. What grounds did the Municipal Corporation cite for canceling the lease? The Municipal Corporation says that constructions deviated from the original purpose, green belt conditions were violated, repeated notices were ignored, and lease conditions were not followed. 'No possession without compensation and legal process' Sahara has argued in the Supreme Court that thousands of crores were invested in the project and that the arbitration order of 2017 is in its favour. It claims the entire land is not a green belt and that the Municipal Corporation’s action is not legally valid. It further argues that possession cannot be taken without compensation and proper legal procedure. Now Eyes on July 31 The hearing scheduled for 31 July 2026 is considered crucial in this high-profile dispute. It is expected to determine whether control over the valuable land in Gomti Nagar will remain with Sahara or go to the government. The future of the proposed new Vidhan Sabha complex on this land will also largely depend on the Supreme Court’s decision.

stories.title: 13-year-old girl falls 15 feet to death:Feeding monkeys when one lunged at her; CCTV captures fatal fall
stories.summary: A 13-year-old girl died after falling from the first floor of a building in Vrindavan on Wednesday evening. She was feeding monkeys from a window when one of the monkeys suddenly lunged at her. The sudden attack caused her to lose balance, and she fell nearly 15 feet onto the street below. The incident took place around 4:30 pm on Wednesday in the Banke Bihari police outpost area. The CCTV footage of the incident surfaced on Thursday morning, showing the girl falling from the first floor. At the time of the accident, only her younger brother was at home, while her parents had gone to work. Locals rushed her to a hospital immediately, where doctors declared her dead. The deceased has been identified as Poorva (13), daughter of Anil Pandey, a resident of Sant Colony. Now, read what is visible in the CCTV CCTV footage shows a three-storey building with iron grills on the first-floor window, where the girl was feeding monkeys. A white car is seen parked in the lane below, and a young man is sitting outside the house. Suddenly, the girl is seen falling straight from the first floor onto the road. Hearing the sound, the man rushes outside, and within seconds a crowd gathers at the spot. See 3 pictures Family was at work, younger brother at home The girl’s father, Anil Pandey, lives with his wife, son, and adopted daughter Poorva in a rented first-floor accommodation in Sant Colony. The family originally hails from Ayodhya and earns a living by running a food cart near Parikrama Marg. Monkeys are frequently seen in the area. On Wednesday, both parents had left for work, leaving Poorva and her younger brother at home. Feeding monkeys turned fatal In the evening, Poorva was standing on a stool and feeding monkeys from the window when one of the monkeys suddenly attacked. She lost balance and fell from the first floor onto the street below. She suffered severe head injuries, and blood was seen on the road. Locals immediately informed her parents and rushed her to the hospital, but doctors declared her dead. Police also reached the spot and began an investigation. Police statement and final update Banke Bihari outpost in-charge Shiv Kumar Sharma said the girl died after falling from the first floor of the building. He added that she was mentally unwell. The family refused to take legal action, after which the body was handed over to them.

stories.title: SIT questions Ram Mandir trustee Anil Mishra behind closed doors:Demolition of two donation theft accused’s homes planned
stories.summary: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) is questioning Ram Mandir trustee Dr Anil Mishra in a closed room inside the Ayodhya temple complex in connection with the alleged donation theft case. Invited trust member Gopal Rao has been asked to wait outside while the questioning continues. The development comes after SIT questioned trust General Secretary Champat Rai for nearly three hours on Sunday. Investigators are now questioning Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao to cross-check his statements. The probe is focused on their alleged role in the appointment of accused Lavkush Mishra and Anukalp Mishra. The SIT reached the temple at around 3 pm on Thursday. Earlier, the team had conducted an extensive investigation between 15 and 20 June. Meanwhile, Ayodhya Police have taken jailed accused Avinash Shukla on a 24-hour remand. Investigators had earlier recovered a Ram Mandir donation chest, ₹20 lakh in cash, more than 1,000 US dollars and jewellery from his house. Police allege that Shukla was involved in counting temple donations. Separately, the administration has begun preparations to demolish the newly built houses of the accused in the alleged donation theft case. The Ayodhya Development Authority (ADA) has identified properties that either lack approved building plans or were constructed in violation of regulations. Bulldozer action on properties of accused likely According to sources, the government is preparing strict action against those accused in the donation theft case. The administration has begun preparations for bulldozer action on properties linked to the accused. The Ayodhya Development Authority (ADA) has identified houses where construction violates rules or where building maps were not approved. Properties under scrutiny include houses built by the accused after joining temple-related work. These include the under-construction house of accused Lavkush Mishra in Shahadatganj and Anukalp Mishra’s house in Kaushalpuri, which may face demolition. ADA is likely to issue notices to them soon. A video has also surfaced showing accused Avinash Shukla’s brother Amit Shukla holding bundles of cash, which is currently under police investigation. Further questioning of trust members likely After questioning accused Avinash Shukla in Ayodhya jail on June 30, police are continuing their investigation. Earlier, Ram Temple Trust general secretary Champat Rai was questioned for nearly three hours on Sunday. Now, Anil Mishra may also be questioned for cross-verification, particularly regarding the appointment of accused Lavkush Mishra and Anukalp Mishra. The case first came to light on June 7. The Uttar Pradesh government formed an SIT on June 13. An FIR was registered on June 25, and eight accused, including Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu, were arrested. On the same day, Trust General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Dr. Anil Mishra also resigned.

stories.title: Mother, daughter among 3 killed as Scorpio crashes into truck:People were returning from Haridwar; 4 others critically injured
stories.summary: A high-speed Scorpio rammed into a truck from behind on Thursday morning around 7 am in Ayodhya. Three people travelling in the vehicle died in the accident, while four others are critically injured. The impact was so severe that the vehicle’s roof was ripped off and the front portion was completely crushed. The wheels of the Scorpio came off and were thrown out of the vehicle. Seven people were inside at the time of the crash. Three of them died on the spot after getting trapped inside the mangled car. Locals rushed to the scene after hearing screams and immediately informed the police and ambulance services. Police and emergency teams later arrived at the spot and rescued the trapped passengers by breaking the vehicle’s windshield. The injured were taken to the district hospital by ambulance, where they are currently receiving treatment. The accident took place on the Ayodhya-Lucknow National Highway near Mubarakganj in the Raunahi police station area, around 35 km from the Ram Mandir, at about 7 am. First see three pictures Severe impact: roof ripped off, wheels detached The collision between the truck and the Scorpio was so powerful that the vehicle’s roof was completely torn off. The car was heavily crushed from the front, and its doors were broken apart. The passengers were trapped inside the wreckage due to the impact. One of the wheels broke off and fell at a distance. The entire roof collapsed and separated from the body of the vehicle. Family returning from Haridwar among injured Doctors at Ayodhya District Hospital, including Dr. Pankaj Kumar, said that four injured persons were brought in around 10 am by ambulance. All of them belong to the same family. They were returning to Gonda’s Maskanwa village after visiting Haridwar. The injured have been identified as Vijay Lakshmi, Abhishek Gupta, Radheshyam and Ayush. All are undergoing treatment. Overspeeding suspected, vehicle lost control According to eyewitnesses, the Scorpio was coming from the Lucknow side at a very high speed, reportedly over 100 km/h. As it reached Mubarakganj on the Ayodhya-Lucknow highway, it approached a truck ahead of it. Due to excessive speed, the driver lost control and the vehicle rammed into the rear of the truck. The Scorpio partially went under the truck, creating a loud explosion-like sound. Parts of the vehicle were scattered across the road, and bloodstains were visible at several spots. High alert on highway, traffic jam after accident Following the crash, traffic on the highway came to a standstill. Police were informed immediately and reached the spot along with ambulances. A crane was also called to the scene. Rescue teams broke the vehicle’s windshield to pull out the trapped passengers. After shifting the injured to hospital, both vehicles were removed using cranes, and traffic movement was restored. Identities of deceased not confirmed yet Raunahi police station in-charge Ratan Sharma confirmed that three people died in the collision between the truck and Scorpio. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem. Four injured persons are undergoing treatment at the hospital. The exact cause of the accident is still under investigation, officials said.
