stories.title: UP TET exam begins amid tight security:Women asked to remove bangles, anklets; 20 lakh candidates to appear in 3 days
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Teacher Eligibility Test (UP-TET) 2026 began on Thursday, marking the first day of the three-day examination scheduled till July 4. Candidates were allowed entry at examination centres between 7.15 am and 8.45 am after multiple layers of verification, including admit card checks, biometric matching and retina scanning. The first shift is being conducted from 9.30 am to 12 noon, while the second shift will run from 2.30 pm to 5 pm. Strict security checks across centres In Gorakhpur, female candidates were required to remove bangles, anklets, hairpins and gold chains before entry. Male candidates were asked to leave scarves, caps and belts outside, while shirt sleeves were unfolded for inspection. In Hathras, girls were asked to open their hair buns for checking, while in Prayagraj, candidates had to remove shoes and socks during frisking. In Deoria, 330 police personnel are also appearing for the examination, having taken official leave for the same. The examination is being conducted across 955 centres in 60 districts over three days. A total of 19.94 lakh candidates are appearing, including 17,67,180 from Uttar Pradesh and 2,27,481 from other states. Around 1,85,791 in-service teachers are also part of the examination. Anti-cheating measures and security arrangements The examination authorities have implemented strict measures to ensure a fair and transparent process. Intelligence agencies have been placed on alert, while question paper boxes have been colour-coded and fitted with one-time digital locks. These will be opened 45 minutes before the exam begins to prevent any possibility of leakage. The examination materials are sealed in tamper-proof containers, and different sets of question papers will be decided just five hours before the exam. CCTV feeds from all centres are being monitored live from a control room in Lucknow, while district-level control rooms have also been set up. Biometric verification and iris scanning are mandatory at entry points to prevent impersonation. The entire verification process has been designed to be completed within one minute per candidate. Guidelines and restrictions Candidates have been advised to reach centres at least 60 minutes before the exam. Mobile phones, smart watches, earphones and all electronic devices are strictly prohibited. Any violation of OMR sheet rules, including incorrect marking or multiple responses, will lead to disqualification. On ground reports from districts In Bareilly, candidates were seen interacting with officials before entry into centres. In Hathras, female candidates were checked after opening their hair buns, while in Gorakhpur, strict frisking included removal of jewellery and accessories. In Deoria, biometric machines arrived late at one centre, causing delays and queues. Around 303 police personnel are also appearing for the exam in the district. In Prayagraj, candidates underwent detailed frisking, including removal of footwear and socks. In Ayodhya, 17 centres are hosting 37,920 candidates under tight security arrangements with CCTV surveillance and deployment of magistrates and police personnel. In Kanpur, nearly 70,000 candidates are appearing across 32 centres over three days, with strict multi-layered checks before entry. Government and administrative measures Prayagraj DM Manish Kumar Verma confirmed adequate police deployment and monitoring of candidates arriving from outside the state. Social media surveillance is also being carried out to prevent misinformation. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed strict action against any attempt of cheating or paper leaks, with intelligence units and cyber teams placed on alert across the state. Why many teachers are appearing for TET Around 1.86 lakh in-service teachers who have not cleared TET are also appearing for the exam. Following a recent Supreme Court directive, clearing TET has been made mandatory for teachers teaching up to Class 8 by August 31, 2027, failing which they may face job implications. Promotion opportunities have also been impacted for those without the qualification. Exam design and paper security OMR sheets and question papers are stored in sealed trunks with one-time locks, opened only 45 minutes before the exam using wire cutters. The selection of question paper sets will be finalised just hours before the exam to ensure security. Invigilators are being assigned through randomisation 30 minutes before the exam to ensure transparency and prevent manipulation.

stories.title: Rain in 20 UP districts as monsoon reaches Lucknow:Thunderstorm alert issued across all 75 districts amid changing weather patterns
stories.summary: In Ayodhya, cloudy conditions were reported with local reporters providing continuous updates. In Barabanki, the weather changed suddenly and heavy rain began around 7 am, disrupting normal activity. In Ballia, continuous rainfall since early morning damaged parwal crops, with farmers fearing significant losses if the situation continues. In Sikanderpur area, a lightning strike killed farmer Premchand Yadav while he was working in the fields. Rampur witnessed heavy rain from the early hours, accompanied by strong winds, marking a sharp change in weather conditions. In Kanpur, dense clouds covered the sky with intermittent drizzle throughout the morning. Although wind remained calm and humidity stayed high, rainfall is expected later in the day. Meerut also remained under cloudy skies since morning, with temperatures dropping by nearly 10 degrees following the previous day’s rain. The possibility of further rainfall remains high. Rain alerts and warnings The Meteorological Department has issued heavy rainfall alerts for 24 districts, including Banda, Prayagraj, Sonbhadra, Meerut, Rampur and Bareilly. An orange alert has also been issued for thunderstorms and lightning in 28 districts, including Banda, Prayagraj, Sonbhadra, Mirzapur, Chandauli and Varanasi. Flooded streets and rain damage In Mirzapur, nearly two hours of rainfall led to waterlogging in an underpass along the Varanasi–Mirzapur road. In Azamgarh, several roads were submerged under knee-deep water, leaving vehicles stranded. In Lalitpur, heavy rain caused flooding in the GRP police station and nearby areas. Weather conditions (2nd July, 2026 – Morning) In Varanasi, light cloud cover was observed with wind speeds of around 10 km/h. The temperature was recorded at 30°C with humidity at 84%, and rainfall is expected in the coming days. In Saharanpur, cloudy skies persisted since morning, with a rain alert issued till July 7, which is expected to bring a drop in temperatures. Monsoon forecast and rainfall outlook Weather experts have warned that rainfall in Uttar Pradesh this monsoon season may remain around 8% below normal. The expected rainfall is projected between 754 mm and 773 mm, compared to the average of 820 mm to 840 mm. Why rainfall may be lower this year Meteorologists say weakening La Niña conditions and a shift towards El Niño may reduce rainfall activity this year. Reduced snow cover in the Northern Hemisphere earlier in the year is also expected to impact monsoon strength. In contrast, Uttar Pradesh recorded 10–15% above-normal rainfall during last year’s monsoon season.

stories.title: Lucknow fire-linked illegal building to be demolished after 7th July:LDA to recover expenses from plot owner; no response to notice received
stories.summary: A building in Aliganj Sector-D in Lucknow is now likely to face demolition as the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) prepares for bulldozer action over alleged illegal construction. The LDA had issued a notice to the landowner on June 23, asking them to explain within 15 days why the construction was carried out without approval. Officials said no response has been received so far from the owner. With the notice period ending on July 6, demolition action is expected to begin on July 7. LDA officials said the entire cost of demolition will also be recovered from the property owner. Preparations for the action are in the final stage, and police support will be taken to maintain law and order during the drive. SIT report flags Electricity Department role in fire case Meanwhile, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing a fire incident has nearly completed its investigation and submitted its report to the government. According to sources, the findings not only point to lapses by LDA engineers but also raise serious questions about the functioning of the electricity department. The report states that the building was given an electricity connection in violation of rules. It also notes that even after increased electricity load, no effective action was taken by the department, leading to continued safety violations. Statements of suspended engineers recorded During the investigation, the SIT also recorded statements of LDA engineers who were suspended following the fire incident. The report is now under review at the government level, after which further action against officials and departments will be decided.

stories.title: Woman films reel on SP's chair:Spins around in seat; deletes Instagram account, apologises after action
stories.summary: A reel shot by the daughter-in-law of a retired police sub-inspector inside the SP office auditorium in Auraiya has triggered controversy. The video was recorded at around 2 pm on June 30 and surfaced at around 4.30 pm on Wednesday after she uploaded it on Instagram, from where it was widely shared. The video shows the woman sitting on the SP's chair and spinning around in it. After the clip went viral, SP Abhishek Bharti ordered action. The woman and her father-in-law later apologised, and she deleted her Instagram account. Family members attended retirement ceremony A farewell function for retired police personnel was held at the SP office on Tuesday. Dibiyapur sub-inspector Nem Singh was among those retiring, and members of his family had attended the programme. After the event concluded and the auditorium was vacated, Nem Singh's daughter-in-law, Soni Chaudhary, sat on the chair and recorded a reel. She later uploaded it on Instagram. The video went viral on Wednesday, causing a stir within the police department. After being informed about the viral reel, SP Abhishek Bharti directed immediate action. Retired officer Nem Singh and his daughter-in-law admitted their mistake and apologised. Soni Chaudhary also released a video apologising for the incident. Daughter-in-law had 16000 followers on Instagram Police let her off after issuing a warning and asking her not to repeat such an act in the future. Soni later deleted her Instagram account, which reportedly had around 16,000 followers. SP Abhishek Bharti said the reel had been recorded after the auditorium became empty. Since she apologised and assured police that she would not repeat the act, no further action was taken. Father-in-law said - I have got the reel deleted Nem Singh said a programme had been organised in the SP office conference hall to mark the retirement of police personnel and that members of his family had attended. He said his daughter-in-law recorded the reel after the event ended and that he had it deleted immediately after learning about it. Daughter-in-law apologized with folded hands, said - A mistake was made Soni Chaudhary said she had attended her father-in-law's retirement ceremony and made the reel while sitting on a chair kept inside the conference room after the programme ended. She said she later realised her mistake and deleted the reel immediately at her father-in-law's insistence. "Such a mistake will not happen again. I should not have done this. I sincerely apologise for my actions. It was a very big mistake on my part," she said.

stories.title: 2 years after Hathras stampede, accused out on bail:Bhole Baba's whereabouts unknown; devotees return to ashrams
stories.summary: 2 July 2024 — exactly two years ago today. A stampede broke out at the ashram of Surajpal alias Bhole Baba in Hathras, claiming 121 lives. Hathras Police named 11 people linked to the event as accused, but left Bhole Baba out of the charges. Seven months after the incident, Bhole Baba received a clean chit. One by one, the accused were also released on bail. Bhole Baba mostly stayed at two ashrams — one in Bichhua (Mainpuri) and another in Patiyali in Kasganj. However, he has not visited either place in the past two years since the stampede. To find out where Bhole Baba is now, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to sevadars residing at his ashrams across five districts in Uttar Pradesh. However, even they were unaware of his exact location. Over the past six months, though, Bhole Baba's followers have started returning to the ashrams. Large gatherings are once again being seen at the weekly satsangs held every Tuesday. Meanwhile, the trial in the case related to the deaths of 121 people has begun in the Hathras district court, where 30 witnesses have been examined so far. What has changed in the ashrams of Mainpuri, Kasganj and Hathras after 121 deaths? Read in this report Large number of devotees reaching Mainpuri ashram Bowing before empty seat, sevadars giving sermons To find out where Surajpal alias Bhole Baba is, we first reached the Narayan Sakar Hari Ashram in Mainpuri. Spread across 21 bighas in Bichhua village, the ashram has six large rooms reserved for Surajpal and his wife. Before the stampede, Bhole Baba often stayed here. His followers say that he has not returned even once since the tragedy. Despite his absence, devotees continue to visit in large numbers. The central hall houses Bhole Baba's seat, before which followers bow their heads. Only his close sevadars sit below the seat and conduct satsangs. Devotees listen to them and later return to their respective cities. Sevadars said - No samagam (congregation) for 2 years, permission not being granted At the entrance of the Mainpuri ashram, we met chief sevadar Vinod Babu Anand. He said, "Narayan Sakar Hari (Bhole Baba) is the Supreme Being. I have been associated with him since 2004. He has not come here in the last two years, and no congregation has been organised anywhere during this period." "The reason is that we are not getting permission from the administration. We once sought approval for his stay here, but that too was denied. Narayan Sakar Hari does not come without administrative permission." Vinod Babu Anand added, "We want Baba to come here, but the administration is not allowing it." Baba had built his first ashram in Kasganj Thousands of followers visit, devotees say Baba has not come in two years Bahadurnagar village in Patiyali area of Kasganj district is Bhole Baba's ancestral village. He built his first ashram here under the Hari Charitable Trust. The ashram is surrounded by high walls, guard posts and massive gates, resembling a fortress. A board at the entrance prohibits photography and videography inside. Inside, several women were seen displaying unusual behaviour — some thrashing their limbs, others shaking their heads violently. We were told that they were believed to be under the influence of evil forces. Followers said that thousands gather at the ashram every Sunday and Tuesday. Prema, who came from Hathras, said, "We have been attending Narayan Sakar Hari's satsangs for 17-18 years. We have not had his darshan for two years. We come here, pay respects to his seat and leave." Prema said faith in Baba remains intact and that he was not responsible for what happened. 'Haven't been able to meet Baba since the stampede' Uday Singh, a follower from Bahadurnagar village, said, "I have been associated with Narayan Sakar Hari for more than 20 years. Since the Hathras incident, I have not met him. We do not know where he is. We come here, remember him and seek his blessings." He added, "Visiting the ashram gives peace. We get time to think about ourselves. It would feel even better if we could have Baba's darshan." Ashram in Bidhnu, Kanpur Fewer followers are reaching here now Bhole Baba has more than 25 ashrams spread across eight states. One of them is located in Kasui village in Kanpur's Bidhnu area and spans 14 bighas. At present, around ten sevadars reside there, conducting daily prayers and rituals. Devotees still visit on Sundays and Tuesdays, but their numbers have fallen considerably compared to earlier. An ashram spread over nearly 15 bighas in Sarai Bhupat area near Etawah was also found deserted. A luxurious ashram in Ilabans village of Sector 87 in Noida's floodplain area has remained closed since a satsang held there on 1 November 2022. Bhole Baba also has ashrams in Lakhimpur Kheri, Pilibhit and Firozabad, though fewer followers visit them. The combined value of Bhole Baba's ashrams is estimated at over ₹100 crore. Each ashram is registered under a trust, and the names of donors are inscribed within the premises. Stampede Case - Lawyer Fighting in Court Speaks 'It was an accident, court's time is being wasted' Bhagdad case lawyer Munna Singh Pundir said witness examination is currently underway and 30 witnesses have already testified. "This entire incident was merely an accident. Nobody is at fault. It had rained that day, temperatures were high and the crowd was huge. The police failed to control the gathering despite being informed in advance and granting permission accordingly." He added, "It was the responsibility of the police to manage the situation. Instead, they blamed devotees and organisers to hide their own shortcomings. People spent a year in jail and have now been released. Nothing is being achieved except wasting the court's time." Government lawyer said - The accused came out on bail Senior advocate Triloki Sharma, representing the government, said the 31st witness would depose on 2 July. "All accused are currently out on bail. Bhole Baba's role in the case is still under examination. If anything emerges, it will be disclosed." Chargesheet filed 3 months after stampede Inspector's claim - Sevadars wielded sticks at Baba's behest Police formed special investigation teams to probe the 2 July 2024 stampede. After 91 days of investigation, a 3,200-page chargesheet was filed on 2 October 2024 naming 11 accused. The main accused was Dev Prakash Madhukar, chief organiser of the Hathras satsang. Others arrested included Megh Singh, Mukesh Kumar, Manju Devi, Manju Yadav, Ram Ladete, Upendra Singh, Sanju Kumar, Ram Prakash Shakya, Durvesh Kumar and Dalveer Singh. Manju Devi and Manju Yadav later received interim bail because they had young children. The chargesheet also contained the statement of sub-inspector Brijesh Pandey, who had lodged the FIR. He told investigators that organiser Dev Prakash had concealed the actual crowd size and sought permission for only 80,000 people. Security and traffic arrangements were made accordingly, but more than 2.5 lakh people attended the event. Pandey stated that when Baba was leaving the venue, devotees rushed towards him to collect dust from his feet. At that point, Baba allegedly pushed the crowd and told sevadars carrying sticks, "Why are you just standing there? Move these people away." He alleged that sevadars and Baba pushed people, sticks were used, and the ensuing chaos triggered the stampede that led to the deaths. Organisers allegedly offered no assistance, while police and administration shifted victims to hospitals. Judicial Commission gave clean chit to Baba A judicial commission was also constituted to investigate the incident. On 21 February 2025, nearly seven months after the tragedy, the commission's report gave Bhole Baba a clean chit. Celebrations were reportedly held across his ashrams following the report. Bhole Baba has spoken publicly only once about the tragedy. A day after the stampede, he told a news agency, "I am deeply saddened by the 2 July incident, but destiny cannot be avoided. Whoever is born must one day depart, whether earlier or later." The one made the main accused is still a devotee of Bhole Baba today Dev Prakash Madhukar, chief organiser of the Hathras satsang and the main accused in the case, was released on bail after spending nearly 11 months in jail. He had earlier worked on contract at a block headquarters but lost his job after the incident. Madhukar says he remains devoted to Bhole Baba. "I was engaged in service earlier and continue to serve now. Wherever service is required in future, we will continue." On the stampede, he said, “Every permission had been obtained. Crowd management and traffic arrangements were the responsibility of the police and administration. But only 60 policemen were deployed for 80,000 people. Mischievous elements took advantage of the situation and sprayed poisonous substances on women, leading to panic and the stampede. We have no information about Baba's whereabouts.”

stories.title: Ambika becomes Lucknow festival's costliest mango variety:Priced at ₹800 per kilogram, matching almonds in retail market today
stories.summary: More than 800 varieties of mangoes are on display at the Lucknow Mango Festival, being held from July 3 to 5 at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan. Besides showcasing a wide range of mangoes, the festival serves as a platform to connect farmers with buyers, exporters, and the latest agricultural technologies. For the first time, the event has placed special emphasis on buyer-seller meets and technical workshops aimed at promoting mango cultivation and trade. Unique varieties grab visitors' attention The festival features mangoes distinguished by their names, colour, size, aroma, taste, weight, and price. Among the most talked-about varieties is 'Modi Mango', while 'Sensation' has attracted attention for its vibrant colour. Hathijhool and Raja Wala stand out for their massive size, whereas Gulab Khas is drawing visitors for its distinctive fragrance. The most expensive variety on display is 'Ambika', priced at ₹800 per kilogram, making it as expensive as—or even costlier than—almonds in the retail market. Another highlight is 'Chakapat', a premium variety originally from Thailand, which is now being cultivated in Malihabad, Uttar Pradesh. See 12 varieties of mangoes in 12 pictures Ambika mango arrives after the monsoon Arun Kumar Kanaujia, a participant from Lucknow, said his display features 165 varieties of mangoes, with Ambika attracting the maximum attention. He said the variety usually becomes available in September, after the monsoon, when the overall mango supply declines. "People often consider mangoes to be an inexpensive fruit. Since almonds sell for around ₹600 per kilogram in the market, Ambika, priced at ₹800 per kilogram, is as expensive as—or even costlier than—almonds," he said. Visitors are also showing keen interest in learning about mango plants and cultivation techniques. American and apple-like mango varieties on display Sanjay, a participant from Uttarakhand, showcased 35 mango varieties, including Tommy Atkins, an American variety priced at ₹350 per kilogram. He said the variety has a comparatively mild taste, making it popular among people with diabetes. He also displayed Arunima, which remains fresh for up to 20 days after harvesting, and Apple Mango, a variety that resembles an apple in both appearance and flavour. According to him, mangoes grown in Uttarakhand remain available in the market until September 15. Aranima mango remains safe for up to 20 days after picking Sanjay, who came from Uttarakhand, said that he has brought 35 varieties of mangoes. Among these, Tommy Atkins is the most special. This is an American variety, priced at ?350 per kg. It has a slightly bland taste, which sugar patients prefer more. Besides this, there is the Aranima mango, which remains safe in the same condition for 20 days after picking. Also, 'Apple Mango' is quite famous. It looks exactly like an apple, and its taste is also like an apple. Those from Uttarakhand are available in the market until a maximum of September 15. 'Modi mango' attracts visitors Vinay Saini from Malihabad said he began developing the 'Modi Mango' in 2023, inspired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said the variety is known for its elegant appearance, attractive aroma, and nearly uniform fruit size, with only slight variation between individual mangoes. Saini added that visitors have been lining up throughout the day to take selfies with the display. He also expressed excitement about the Chakapat variety, saying the Thailand-origin mango would soon become more widely available through cultivation in Malihabad. Potato farmers inspired to grow mangoes The festival has also attracted farmers from other agricultural sectors. Rajesh Yadav, a potato farmer from Badaun, attended the event along with 40 fellow farmers. He said seeing so many mango varieties at one place had inspired them to consider mango cultivation. The group is interacting with agricultural scientists and experts to understand which mango varieties are best suited to their region. They also plan to visit Malihabad to meet experienced mango growers and purchase saplings from local nurseries. Rajesh said the festival has encouraged many farmers to explore mango cultivation as a potential alternative crop. Finally, 3 pictures of hundreds of mango stalls -

stories.title: Yogi, Nitin Nabin attend Brajesh Pathak's mango party:BJP leaders shares Dussehri mangoes, signalling unity before 2027 elections
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) National President Nitin Nabin, Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya, and Uttar Pradesh BJP President Pankaj Chaudhary attended a lunch hosted by Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak at his residence in Lucknow on Sunday. Following the lunch, the leaders participated in a traditional mango party, where they were served Dussehri mangoes while seated on woven cots in a rustic setting. Brajesh Pathak personally served Dussehri mangoes After lunch, Brajesh Pathak personally carried plates of Dussehri mangoes to the guests. CM Yogi, Nitin Nabin, and Pankaj Chaudhary were seated together, while Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak sat alongside them. The BJP leaders enjoyed the mangoes in a traditional village-style setting. Earlier, the guests were welcomed with Tilak at the entrance of the residence. When Yogi Adityanath arrived, Namrata Pathak, wife of Brajesh Pathak, greeted him by touching his feet to seek his blessings. See 5 pictures of the Mango Party Warm welcome by Brajesh Pathak and his family Brajesh Pathak and his wife welcomed every guest at the entrance and remained there until all invitees had arrived. Pathak applied Tilak to CM Yogi and presented a bouquet to Nitin Nabin. During lunch, Namrata Pathak personally served food to the guests and encouraged them to enjoy the meal. Now see 4 pictures of the welcome Nitin Nabin continues meetings with top BJP leaders The lunch came a day after Nitin Nabin attended a dinner hosted by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday. Later on Sunday, he was also scheduled to attend a tea gathering at the residence of Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya, continuing his meetings with the state's top BJP leadership. Visit seen as message of party unity ahead of 2027 polls Political observers view Nitin Nabin's two-day visit as significant ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. During his visit, he interacted with everyone from booth-level workers to senior party leaders. The series of social gatherings—including dinner, lunch, and tea—was widely seen as an effort to project unity within the BJP. According to party insiders, Nitin Nabin has consistently urged leaders to remain united. Addressing MPs and MLAs during a meeting on Saturday, he reportedly told them to focus on fighting the opposition rather than fighting among themselves, adding that preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections had effectively begun.

stories.title: Illegal foetal sex determination racket busted, 4 arrested:₹10,000 for test, ₹20,000 for abortion
stories.summary: Police arrested four members of a gang for illegally conducting abortions and foetal sex determination tests in a moving car in the National Capital Region (NCR). The arrests were made in the intervening night of Saturday and Sunday. A portable ultrasound machine and other medical equipment were seized from the accused. The gang used to roam in Ghaziabad, Delhi, and other parts of NCR. In the car, they checked whether the child in the woman's womb was a boy or a girl. For this, ₹8,000 to ₹10,000 were charged. If a woman wanted an abortion, she would be taken to a nursing home and an abortion would be performed by a quack doctor. Police took this action on Nalkuan Road in the City Kotwali area. Around 12 AM on Saturday night, the police received information about the gang from an informant. Following this, a four-member team was formed under the supervision of a Nodal Officer. At 2 AM, a moving car with registration number UP14FL 9355 was stopped and searched. Four youths, including the driver, were in the car. During the search, a portable ultrasound machine and other equipment were recovered. Following this, the police arrested all four accused and seized the equipment. Know the full case Kotwali SHO Sachin Baliyan stated that around 12 AM on Saturday night, the police received information from an informant that some people were conducting foetal sex determination tests in a moving car. They had called a woman to Nalkuan Road for the test and were waiting for her in a car with registration number 4FL 9355. Following this, a joint team of police and the health department reached the spot. Around 2 AM, the car was stopped and all four accused were arrested. Abortion for ₹20,000 According to the police, the accused have been identified as Sandeep (35), Salman (32), Shahid (29) and Tasleem (27). During interrogation, Sandeep revealed that he is the mastermind of the gang. He has been jailed before in a case of foetal sex determination. The accused used to roam in different areas of Delhi, Ghaziabad and NCR. Customers were contacted via WhatsApp. Foetal sex determination was done for ₹8,000 to ₹10,000. The ultrasound report was given in the car itself. If a woman wanted to have an abortion, ₹20,000 were taken from her and the abortion was performed by a quack doctor in a makeshift nursing home. To avoid police, they conducted tests in the car Sandeep revealed, during interrogation, that to avoid action by the police and health department, they used to conduct foetal sex determination tests in the car itself. Money was taken from customers according to their financial status. More money was extorted from affluent families. After the deal was finalised, the woman was taken to a temporary nursing home for an abortion. Conversations used to happen on WhatsApp Sandeep stated that to avoid getting caught, they only spoke to customers via WhatsApp calls. After the conversation was complete, they would delete the call and chat data. He also mentioned that Salman, a member of the gang, would go to different locations and contact women who wanted to undergo foetal sex determination tests. He was solely responsible for bringing in customers. Sandeep, owner of Sai Hospital Sandeep is the owner of Sai Hospital located in Banthla Colony, Loni town, Ghaziabad. He has studied up to 12th grade. Women were brought to this hospital for abortions. ACP Kotwali Upasana Pandey stated that an Ertiga car belonging to Sandeep, found with the accused, has been seized. A portable machine made in China, a probe jelly, a USG machine, and ₹20,000 have also been seized from the accused.

stories.title: Food safety officials raid at pizza outlet:Worm found in online order, paneer sample sent for lab testing
stories.summary: A case raising concerns for online food delivery customers has come to light in Gorakhpur. At around 6 pm on Saturday, the Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) launched an investigation after receiving a complaint that a worm had allegedly been found in a pizza ordered online from a pizza outlet on Medical College Road. Following the complaint, an FSDA team visited the outlet and began inspecting the quality of the food as well as hygiene and sanitation standards. According to reports, city resident Anand Krishna had ordered the pizza through an online food delivery app. While eating it, he allegedly discovered a worm and immediately lodged a complaint with the Food Safety Department. Acting on the complaint, the department's team, under the direction of Assistant Commissioner (Food Safety) Dr Suresh Kumar Singh, inspected the outlet. Paneer sample collected for laboratory testing During the inspection, officials observed the entire pizza preparation process. A sample of the paneer being used at the outlet was collected and sent to a laboratory for analysis. The department said the laboratory report will determine whether the food met the prescribed quality standards. Further action against the establishment will be taken in accordance with the findings. Hygiene and food safety standards were also examined The Food Safety team also inspected the kitchen's cleanliness, pest control measures, food storage practices and compliance with food safety protocols by staff. Officials instructed the outlet owner to improve hygiene standards and strictly comply with all food safety regulations. An improvement notice was also issued during the inspection. Clarification sought from food delivery platform The department has sought explanations not only from the outlet operator but also from the online food delivery platform through which the order was placed. Officials said complaints affecting consumer health would be treated with utmost seriousness and strict action would be taken against anyone found responsible after the investigation is completed. Department urges consumers to report food quality concerns The Food Safety Department has appealed to consumers to immediately report any complaints regarding the quality of food ordered from hotels, restaurants or online food delivery services. Officials said timely reporting enables prompt investigation and appropriate action, helping ensure that consumers receive safe and hygienic food.

stories.title: UP STF seals illegal factory; 800 kg fake tea seized:Used tea sold as fresh after chemical treatment
stories.summary: A joint team of the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) and the Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) uncovered an illegal tea-processing unit operating from a house in Barabanki at around 4.30 pm on Saturday. The factory owner was arrested and the premises sealed. During the three-hour raid, officials recovered 800 kg of re-coloured tea leaves, 5 kg of artificial colouring, and large quantities of packaging material. The investigation found that used tea leaves collected from hotels and roadside eateries after being brewed were being reprocessed, mixed with artificial colour and repackaged before being sold in the market under branded labels. The raid was carried out in the Baddupur police station area, around 45 km from the district headquarters. See pictures of raid- Artificial colour poses serious health risks, say officials FSDA officials warned that the artificial colouring used in the tea leaves poses a serious threat to public health. According to the department, regular consumption of such adulterated products may increase the risk of serious illnesses, including cancer. Officials said the accused had been operating the illegal factory from his two-storey house for nearly two years. A complaint regarding the operation had been received around one-and-a-half years ago, but investigators were unable to identify its exact location until now. Used tea leaves were reprocessed and resold Food Inspector Dr Ankit Yadav said the artificial colour mixed into the tea leaves could be extremely harmful. He warned that prolonged consumption of such chemicals could increase the risk of serious diseases, including cancer. He also urged consumers to purchase food products only from trusted brands and authorised retailers. Sample collected from another restaurant As part of the same enforcement drive, Food Safety Officers Pallavi Tiwari and Arshi Farooqui inspected a restaurant on the Ayodhya–Lucknow Road. During the inspection, they collected a sample of ground red chilli powder for laboratory testing. The restaurant operator was issued a notice directing them to rectify the deficiencies identified during the inspection. The department warned that failure to comply within the stipulated period could result in cancellation of the establishment's licence and its closure.

stories.title: Retired IAS officer's son attacks girlfriend with brick:He drags her out from car and beats her after she refuses marriage
stories.summary: A 38-year-old man, identified as Devashish Nigam, the son of a retired IAS officer, allegedly assaulted his girlfriend inside a moving car after she refused to marry him in Kanpur. According to police, he repeatedly struck the woman on her head and face with a brick before dragging her out of the vehicle onto the road, where he allegedly continued to assault her with kicks and punches, leaving her seriously injured and bleeding. Police said the incident took place at around 7 pm on Saturday while Devashish and the woman were travelling to Brahmaghat in Bithoor in his Honda Amaze. Near Model Dairy, on the railway service lane, he allegedly began attacking her. Hearing the woman's screams, local residents rushed to the scene, overpowered the accused, assaulted him, and later handed him over to the police. The injured woman, who works at IIT Kanpur, was admitted to Rama Medical College for treatment. She told police that Devashish had been pressuring her to marry him and became violent after she refused. The incident occurred within the jurisdiction of Bithoor police station. A video of the assault surfaced on Sunday morning at around 8 am. See 3 pictures of the incident- How the incident unfolded The accused, Devashish Nigam, lives in Raj Tower, Swaroop Nagar. His mother, Chandra Nigam, is a retired IAS officer who previously served in the Lucknow Development Authority. His father, Ramesh Shankar Nigam, died a few years ago. According to police, Devashish drove to IIT Kanpur to pick up his 38-year-old girlfriend. He called her and asked her to meet him at the institute's gate, after which the two left for Brahmaghat in Bithoor. Devashish was driving while the woman was seated beside him. During the journey, the couple reportedly argued over marriage. As the argument escalated, Devashish allegedly stopped the car on the service lane and slapped the woman two or three times. He then got out of the vehicle, picked up a brick from the roadside and returned. To protect herself, the woman locked the car doors. Police said Devashish struck the car window two or three times with the brick, smashing the glass. He then allegedly dragged the woman out of the vehicle, threw her onto the road and repeatedly hit her on the head and body with the brick. Locals intervened after hearing screams The woman screamed for help, attracting nearby residents. Locals rushed to the scene, restrained the accused, and informed the police. According to police, when officers arrived, Devashish allegedly attempted to intimidate them by saying: ‘My mother is a retired IAS officer.’ Accused married in 2014, victim is a widow Residents of Raj Tower in Swaroop Nagar said Devashish owns two guest houses in Barra. They said he married in 2014 and has a daughter. He has reportedly been living separately from his wife for the past six months. According to sources, the injured woman's husband has died. She also has a daughter. Residents said Devashish and the woman had known each other for a long time and were frequently seen together. Police begin investigation DCP (West) S. M. stories.title: Kashi scholars determine auspicious time for Simhastha Kumbh flag hoisting:Festival to begin in Nashik on November 29, devotees expected from India and abroad
stories.summary: The Simhastha Kumbh Mahaparv, to be held in Nashik, Maharashtra, will officially begin on November 29, 2026. The traditional flag-hoisting ceremony will be performed with Vedic rituals at the Kapil Mahamuni Ashram, situated at the confluence of the Godavari and Kapila rivers. The auspicious timing (muhurat) for the ceremony has been determined by Vedic scholar Ganeshwara Shastri Dravid of Kashi. Flag hoisting to take place during Amrit Yoga Jagadguru Kalkiram Maharaj, pontiff of the Adinath Sampradaya, and Mahant Ramnarayandas Guru, President of Kapil Mahamuni Ashram, said the flag hoisting ceremony will take place between 8:45 am and 9:00 am on Sunday, November 29, 2026 (Kartik Vadya Panchami) during Pushya Nakshatra and Amrit Yoga. They said saints, seers and spiritual leaders from across the country, along with distinguished personalities from various fields, are expected to attend the ceremony. Devotees from India and abroad expected to participate Jagadguru Kalkiram Maharaj said the original site of Simhastha is believed to be around 1.132 million years old. According to tradition, it has served as a place of penance for numerous sages and saints, including Sant Dnyaneshwar, Samarth Ramdas Swami and Gajanan Maharaj. He added that millions of devotees, saints, ascetics, Akharas (Hindu monastic orders) and religious leaders from India and around the world are expected to take part in the spiritual and cultural gathering.

stories.title: Ram Mandir theft case:Police interrogate five accused in jail after they are shifted in separate barracks
stories.summary: Police reached Ayodhya Jail on Sunday afternoon to question the five accused in the Ram Mandir offering theft case. Eight accused are currently lodged in jail, while police have already questioned three others in connection with the alleged theft. The five accused being questioned on Sunday are Ramashankar Mishra, Manish Yadav, Lavkush Mishra, Anukalp Mishra and Karunesh Pandey. Meanwhile, all the accused were shifted to separate barracks in Ayodhya jail on Saturday. They had previously been housed together. Police feared the accused could assault one another or hatch a conspiracy if kept in the same barrack. Investigators have earlier questioned Avinash Shukla and Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu inside the jail. Meanwhile, a poster reading 'Chanda chor party ka pravesh varjit h' was put up outside the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) office in Lucknow on Sunday amid the ongoing controversy over the alleged theft of offerings at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir. BJP state president calls incident 'wrong' BJP Uttar Pradesh president Nitin Nabin commented publicly on the Ram Mandir donation theft case for the first time on Saturday. Speaking in Lucknow, he said- What happened was wrong. It has sent the wrong message to the public. This is an adverse situation and has given the Opposition an issue. The state government is taking action. Those responsible will not be spared. SIT may register FIR after July 15 According to sources, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) may register an FIR after July 15 once its investigation is complete. The case could reportedly name Champat Rai, who resigned as General Secretary of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, along with Trustee Dr Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao, as accused. Treasurer Govind Dev Giri arrives in Ayodhya ahead of Trust meeting Ahead of the proposed meeting of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, Treasurer Govind Dev Giri Maharaj arrived in Ayodhya on Saturday evening. On Sunday, he is expected to meet trust office-bearers, saints and other prominent individuals. The meeting is expected to include discussions on various aspects of the Ram Mandir construction, administrative arrangements and future plans. Major decisions likely at July 6 Trust meeting The donation theft case is expected to dominate discussions at the Ram Mandir Trust meeting scheduled for July 6. According to sources, questions have also been raised over the functioning of Treasurer Govind Dev Giri. It is alleged that he did not devote sufficient time to Trust affairs and failed to adequately discharge his responsibilities. Sources further indicated that the resignations of Champat Rai and Dr Anil Mishra are likely to be accepted. If replacements are not finalised immediately, Trust President Mahant Nritya Gopal Das may be granted additional administrative powers to ensure the Trust continues to function smoothly until new appointments are made. Mahant Nritya Gopal Das returned to Ayodhya on Friday after being discharged from Medanta Hospital. He had travelled to attend the last rites of his disciple, Kripalu Ram Das Punjabi Baba. The July 6 meeting of the Ram Mandir Trust will be chaired by Mahant Nritya Gopal Das.

stories.title: 1.22 million died from tuberculosis in 2023:Gorakhpur AIIMS global analysis published in 'The Lancet Infectious Diseases'
stories.summary: Tuberculosis (TB) continues to be the world's deadliest infectious disease. In 2023, around 9.11 million new TB cases were reported globally, while approximately 1.22 million people died from the disease. The findings were shared by Dr U. Venkatesh, Associate Professor in the Department of Community and Family Medicine at Gorakhpur AIIMS, and Dr Arup Mohanty, Media In-charge, based on a meta-analysis of a global study published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. Study analysed data from 204 countries over three decades The doctors said the original study was led by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) at the University of Washington. Researchers analysed TB-related data from 204 countries and territories covering the period from 1990 to 2023. The study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases on July 1, 2026. HIV-related and drug-resistant TB remain major challenges According to the meta-analysis, around 781,000 new TB cases were reported among people living with HIV in 2023, while approximately 210,000 people died from HIV-associated TB. The study also identified around 466,000 new cases of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB), with approximately 102,000 deaths attributed to the drug-resistant form of the disease. TB cases and deaths have declined, but drug-resistant TB remains a concern Dr U. Venkatesh and Dr Arup Mohanty said that between 2015 and 2023, the number of new TB cases fell by around 19%, while TB-related deaths declined by 23%. However, they noted that progress in controlling multidrug-resistant TB remains slow, making it a continuing global public health concern. According to the study, South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa continue to bear the highest burden of tuberculosis. The researchers identified smoking, alcohol consumption and poorly controlled diabetes as the major risk factors for developing the disease. They said that effective control of these risk factors, along with early diagnosis and timely treatment, could save a significant number of lives. Funding cuts could jeopardise WHO's 2035 TB elimination target The doctors warned that declining global financial support for TB control programmes is a serious concern for future efforts to eliminate the disease. They stressed that diagnosis, treatment and prevention strategies must be further strengthened. Without sustained action, achieving the World Health Organization's (WHO) target of eliminating TB by 2035 could become increasingly difficult. Key TB statistics

stories.title: ₹10 lakh travel insurance for just 45 paise:Accident cover available with train, flight, bus and cab bookings
stories.summary: When booking a train ticket through the IRCTC website or mobile app, passengers are shown a small checkbox before proceeding to payment asking whether they want travel insurance worth ₹10 lakh for just 45 paise. Many passengers select the option without a second thought because ₹10 lakh of cover for 45 paise appears to be an excellent deal. However, simply ticking ‘Yes’ while booking the ticket does not guarantee that your family will receive the insurance benefit. Under the current rules, it is mandatory to provide the nominee's name along with the details of a government-issued identity document. If these details are not updated, the insurance claim may not be settled smoothly. Travel insurance and accident cover are now also offered while booking flights, buses and app-based taxi services such as Ola, Uber and Rapido. Here's what you need to know. 90% of passengers make mistakes while booking train tickets The ₹10 lakh travel insurance is available only to passengers who select the "Travel Insurance" option while booking tickets online through the IRCTC website or mobile app. It is not available on tickets purchased from railway booking counters. Once the insurance option is selected, the insurance company sends a policy number and a link to the passenger's registered mobile number and email address. Using this link, passengers must enter the nominee's name, age and relationship. If the link cannot be found, nominee details can also be updated through the "Booked Ticket History" section on the IRCTC website or app. If an accident occurs during the journey and nominee details have not been updated, the insurance company does not automatically release the claim. Instead, the legal heirs may have to obtain a Succession Certificate through the courts before the claim can be processed. It is also important to note that the immediate financial assistance of ₹5 lakh or ₹10 lakh announced by the Railway Minister or the government after major train accidents is an ex gratia payment. This is entirely separate from travel insurance and statutory compensation. Flight bookings offer personal accident cover of up to ₹50 lakh Passengers booking domestic flights through MakeMyTrip, EaseMyTrip, IRCTC Air or directly through airline websites are also offered the option of purchasing Domestic Travel Insurance. After purchasing the policy, passengers should visit the insurance partner's portal and update their nominee details. Failure to do so may complicate the claims process. The premium generally ranges from ₹149 to ₹399 per passenger. The policy typically provides- Bus ticket bookings provide accidental cover of up to ₹7.5 lakh Passengers booking private or state-run bus tickets through platforms such as RedBus, AbhiBus and other online booking apps are also offered accident insurance. The cover is generally provided by insurers such as Acko and Tune Protect. The premium usually ranges from ₹10 to ₹25 per seat. The insurance typically includes- Government bus tickets already include accident insurance Passengers travelling on government-operated bus services, including Uttar Pradesh Roadways, are already covered by accident insurance as part of the ticket price. There is no need to pay an additional premium or tick any insurance option. The insurance premium of around ₹1 to ₹2 per passenger is already included in the fare. Under the Uttar Pradesh Roadways scheme- To make a claim, passengers or their families must submit the ticket, FIR and medical documents to the District Magistrate's office or the nearest office of the State Transport Corporation. Ola, Uber and Rapido also offer low-cost accident cover Passengers booking cabs or bike taxis through apps such as Ola, Uber and Rapido are also offered optional insurance at a nominal cost. Many users ignore the option, despite the fact that a premium of just ₹1 to ₹5 can provide accident cover of up to ₹1 lakh or more, depending on the platform. On Ola, premiums generally range from ₹1 to ₹49 depending on the type of ride. The policy provides accident cover of ₹5 lakh to ₹7.5 lakh in the event of accidental death or permanent disability. Uber offers accident insurance for approximately ₹3 per trip. The policy provides compensation of up to ₹10 lakh in the event of accidental death and up to ₹2 lakh towards hospital expenses. Rapido offers accident cover of up to ₹5 lakh for a premium ranging from 50 paise to ₹1. The policy also includes hospital expenses and, in certain cases, compensation for damages. For this reason, overlooking the insurance option while booking a journey could prove costly if an accident occurs.

stories.title: Rain alert issued for 25 UP districts:State records 44% rainfall deficit, monsoon to regain strength in two days
stories.summary: After covering the whole of Uttar Pradesh, the monsoon has weakened. As a result, only light rainfall is expected across the state over the next 48 hours, while humid conditions are likely to make the weather increasingly uncomfortable. On Sunday morning, the weather remained clear across almost all major cities, including Lucknow, Kanpur and Barabanki. Bright sunshine prevailed, although relatively cool winds provided some relief from the heat. Rain alert in 25 districts; heat and humidity warning for 26 The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rainfall alert for 25 districts on Sunday. At the same time, 26 districts have been placed under a warning for intense heat and high humidity. According to the IMD, Uttar Pradesh has received only 44 mm of rainfall between June 1 and July 4 this season. During the same period, the state normally records around 118 mm of rainfall. This means the state has received 44% less rainfall than normal so far this monsoon season. Rain recorded in 36 districts over the past 24 hours During the past 24 hours, scattered rainfall was reported in 36 districts, including Lucknow. In Mathura, two hours of rain led to waterlogging in low-lying areas. In Hathras, just 45 minutes of rainfall left roads submerged under knee-deep water, while power supply was disrupted in several localities. Light showers were also reported from Agra and Etawah. Monsoon likely to revive after two days Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said the weakening of the monsoon is linked to a weather system near the northern Odisha coast. He said- The weather system that developed near the northern Odisha coast has influenced weather conditions in Uttar Pradesh. As a result, the monsoon will remain weak across the state for the next two days. Only a few districts in western and southern Uttar Pradesh are likely to receive light rainfall, while humidity and heat will increase across eastern and central parts of the state. The monsoon is expected to become active again after two days, following which rainfall will resume across the state.

stories.title: Woman digs 1.5-foot pit to bury husband:Wife dragged body to bathroom, paid ₹1,200 to make floor over it
stories.summary: 'My husband, Surendra, was addicted to alcohol. He used to beat me after drinking. I endured this for 16 years. Eventually, I decided to kill him. I crushed sleeping tablets and mixed them into his food. I woke up around 3 am and realised he was no longer breathing. I moved the children into another room and waited until morning. After sending my mother-in-law and the children away with my brother-in-law, I dug a pit in the bathroom and dragged my husband's body there. I buried it in the pit. To cover the area, I ordered soil worth ₹400, levelled the ground myself, and, the following day, hired labourers to lay a cement floor over it. They had no idea there was a body buried underneath'. This is the statement given by Ruby, who has been arrested for allegedly murdering her husband in Agra. Here is how, according to the police, she planned the killing and concealed the body beneath the bathroom floor. Read how the wife killed her husband and buried him in the bathroom Surendra Kumar Sharma (44), originally from Bharatpur in Rajasthan, lived in Renuka Dham Colony, Dahtora, in Sikandra, Agra. He married Ruby, a native of Etawah, in 2010. The couple had two daughters, Riddhi (13) and Siddhi (9). Surendra's mother, Kamala, who has poor eyesight, also lived with them. His father, Radheshyam Sharma, a retired teacher, had died a few years ago. Surendra had been missing since May 18. On May 26, Ruby lodged a missing person's report at the local police station and repeatedly told relatives and neighbours that her husband had disappeared. On Friday (July 3), police visited the house after receiving information from Surendra's brother. Officers reportedly found Ruby's behaviour suspicious. During a search of the property, they became suspicious of the bathroom floor. After excavating it, they recovered Surendra's skeletal remains. Ruby's confession to police Following her arrest, Ruby allegedly told police- ‘My marriage took place in 2010. I am from Etawah and we have two daughters, Riddhi and Siddhi. My marriage itself was built on lies. Before the wedding, I was told Surendra was educated and had a good job. After marriage, I discovered he did not work at all. I accepted it as my fate. But he was addicted to alcohol and regularly assaulted me after drinking. Even after our daughters were born, I continued to endure the abuse.’ Argument in Bharatpur before the murder Ruby told police that two days before the alleged murder, on May 16, Surendra visited relatives in Bharatpur. 'There, we had another argument. My relatives advised me to file a police complaint. On May 17, Surendra sent me back to Bharatpur to persuade them, but I was treated badly there as well. I was threatened that I, along with my husband and children, would be sent to prison. That deeply hurt me. I had built up a great deal of anger because of my husband's behaviour.' Sleeping tablets mixed in food; body buried in a 1.5-foot pit Ruby said both her husband and mother-in-law regularly took sleeping tablets. 'I crushed sleeping tablets and mixed them into my husband's food. After dinner, my husband and the children fell asleep in the same room. Around 3 am, I woke up and realised my husband had stopped breathing. I moved the children into another room and locked the room where my husband's body was lying. Since he usually woke up late, nobody became suspicious'. She further said, 'The next morning, I called my brother-in-law and sent my mother-in-law and the children away with him. Once everyone had left, I locked the house, dug a pit about one-and-a-half feet deep in the bathroom and dragged my husband's body there before burying it.' Soil ordered for ₹400 to conceal the grave Ruby further stated- 'I ordered soil worth ₹400 from a contractor to fill the bathroom. The soil was delivered to the house. I covered my husband's body myself and levelled the surface. The following day, I hired two local labourers and paid them ₹1,200 to lay a concrete floor. I ordered two bags of cement and had the floor plastered. The labourers never knew they were building over a buried body. When asked whether she regretted killing her husband, Ruby allegedly told investigators- 'I had endured 16 years of abuse. When my children were threatened with prison because of my husband's actions, I reached my breaking point. After his death, I cried. Whenever my daughters asked where their father had gone, I lied to them. Every time I entered the bathroom, I remembered that night. But I kept lying because I believed I was protecting my children's future.' Truth revealed to brother-in-law after 45 days According to police, Ruby initially tried to mislead everyone. She told her mother-in-law and brother-in-law, Anil Sharma, that Surendra had left home after an argument. She also filed a missing person's complaint and publicly mourned her husband in front of neighbours. However, Anil Sharma became suspicious. Their late father's pension of ₹64,000 was credited to a bank account operated through an ATM card that remained with Surendra. Continued transactions from the account after Surendra's disappearance raised doubts. On Friday (July 3), Anil told Ruby, 'Crying will not solve anything. If something has happened, tell me. If you are in trouble, I will help you. I will not let any harm come to you.’ Police said Ruby then broke down and confessed that she had buried her husband's body beneath the bathroom floor. Labourers broke the floor in 20 minutes Police were informed at around 12 noon on Friday. Officers reached the house and called five labourers, who broke the bathroom floor within 20 minutes before excavating the area. stories.title: Champat Rai not to lead Ram Mandir Trust meeting:Decision on his resignation to be made on July 6; discussion likely on 5 points
stories.summary: The meeting of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, scheduled for July 6, will be led by Treasurer Govind Dev Giri. The meeting will be held at Maniram Das Chhawani under the chairmanship of Trust President Mahant Nritya Gopal Das. General Secretary Champat Rai and Trustee Dr Anil Mishra have also been invited to attend. During the meeting, trustees will decide by majority vote whether to accept or reject the resignations submitted by Champat Rai and Dr Anil Mishra. Champat Rai previously handled all Trust meetings Since the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust was constituted on February 5, 2020, every Trust meeting has been conducted by General Secretary Champat Rai. He was responsible for issuing official notices, setting the agenda and presenting all key information. Champat Rai, who stepped down on June 26 following allegations relating to the theft of offerings from the Shri Ram Mandir, submitted his resignation along with Trustee Dr Anil Mishra. Treasurer Govind Dev Giri confirmed that both resignations had been received. In view of the situation, the Trust convened a meeting for July 6. Treasurer Govind Dev Giri's role has expanded Following Champat Rai's resignation, Treasurer Govind Dev Giri has assumed a larger administrative role. He issued the official notice convening the July 6 meeting and circulated it to all trustees. The meeting will begin at 3 pm at Maniram Das Chhawani, where five key agenda items will be discussed- Rules for appointing or removing Trust members The procedures for appointing or removing members of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust are governed by the Trust Deed, the Trust Bylaws and the Indian Trusts Act, 1882. The Trust may have a maximum of 15 members, comprising three ex officio members and 12 lifetime trustees. One lifetime trustee, Vimalendra Mohan Pratap Mishra, passed away in August 2025, leaving one position vacant. The resignations of Champat Rai and Dr Anil Mishra have created two additional vacancies, subject to the Trust's decision. Two-thirds majority required to remove a trustee A trustee may be removed if they act against the interests of the Trust, but only through a two-thirds majority vote. Before any such decision, the trustee must be served with a show-cause notice and allowed to present their case before the Trust members. The Trust Deed also lays down rules for resignations. A trustee must submit at least one month's written notice. A resignation does not automatically take effect upon submission; it must be placed before the Trust at its next meeting, where members may either accept or reject it. Accordingly, the resignations of Champat Rai and Dr Anil Mishra will be considered during the July 6 meeting. The remaining 12 trustees will collectively decide the matter. A two-thirds majority requires the support of at least eight members. Appointment of new trustees rests with the Trust Board The Trust Deed also specifies the procedure for appointing new trustees. The decision rests with the Trust Board and is not confined to members nominated by the Central or State governments. The only mandatory qualification is that the permanent or nominated member must be a Hindu. Under the Trust Deed and Sections 73 and 74 of the Indian Trusts Act, a new trustee can be appointed only with the approval of a two-thirds majority of the Board. Who can convene a Trust meeting? The Trust Deed ordinarily authorises the General Secretary to convene Trust meetings. However, it also allows another responsible office-bearer to perform this role in exceptional circumstances. Following Champat Rai's resignation, this responsibility has been assigned to Treasurer Govind Dev Giri. The Board also has the authority to amend the Trust Deed, provided that any amendments remain consistent with the basic framework laid down by the Supreme Court's 2019 judgment and applicable laws. Champat Rai and Dr Anil Mishra were invited despite resignations Although Champat Rai and Dr Anil Mishra have submitted their resignations, they will continue to be regarded as trustees until those resignations are formally accepted. For this reason, both have been invited to attend the July 6 meeting. Trust President Mahant Nritya Gopal Das has returned to Ayodhya after receiving medical treatment in Lucknow and is reported to be in better health. The meeting will be held at his residence in Maniram Das Chhawani, where he will preside. Founding Trust member K. Parasaran is unlikely to travel to Ayodhya due to ill health. He is expected to participate virtually. Any other trustees unable to attend in person will also have the option of joining the meeting online.

stories.title: Man murders girlfriend after she refuses to elope:Accused arrested in Delhi; friendship started on Instagram
stories.summary: A man allegedly murdered his girlfriend in Amethi after she refused to elope with him. The accused travelled from Pratapgarh on the night of 30 June and called her to a field near her home in Jangal Ramnagar village at around 8.30 pm. During their meeting, he raised the issue of marriage and pressured her to run away with him. When she refused, an argument broke out. Enraged, he allegedly smothered her to death, then covered the body with eucalyptus leaves before fleeing. Police arrested him in Delhi on 3 July and disclosed the case on Saturday afternoon, revealing that the two had become friends through Instagram. Understand the whole case Kajal (19), daughter of Amarjeet Singh, who lives with his family in Jangal Ramnagar village, about 3 km from the Amethi district headquarters, left home at around 7.30 pm on 30 June but did not return. Her family informed the police that night and continued searching for her. On Wednesday morning, villagers found Kajal's body in bushes around 200 metres from her home. Police, along with the CO, ASP and SP, reached the spot and sent the body for post-mortem. Initial investigations indicated it was a murder. Father expressed suspicion on the lover Father Amarjeet Singh filed a case against his daughter's lover, Surjeet Singh. Surjeet is a resident of Udaipur village in the Lalganj police station area of Pratapgarh. Meanwhile, the post-mortem report stated that the girl died due to suffocation. Following this, the police started searching for the accused Surjeet. SP Saravanan T formed 10 teams to unravel the incident. Kajal's mobile was not found at the crime scene. Therefore, the police started tracking Kajal's and Surjeet's mobiles through surveillance. After continuous investigation for 48 hours, the police found Surjeet's location in Delhi. Following this, he was arrested on July 3 from the Kamla Nagar area of Delhi. Misled police, broke down when confronted with location The SP interrogated Surjeet. At first, he denied killing Kajal. Later, when asked about both mobile locations being at the same place, Surjeet broke down. He confessed to the murder. SP Saravanan T said, Kajal and Surjeet had been talking for about two and a half years. Their friendship started on Instagram. On Tuesday night, lover Surjeet reached the village and called Kajal to meet. He pressured Kajal to elope from home for marriage. Pushed her to ground and covered her mouth with both hands Upon Kajal's refusal, he pushed her to the ground. Then, he covered her mouth with both his hands. She died due to suffocation. After this, he broke eucalyptus branches and leaves and placed them over the dead body. Meanwhile, hearing someone approaching, he fled from the scene. While fleeing, he also took Kajal's mobile phone with him. Then, he took a bus from Amethi to Lucknow. From there, he reached Delhi by bus. The police continuously pursued Surjeet. His mobile phone also kept turning on intermittently. Tracking it, the police reached Kamla Nagar in Delhi, where Surjeet was taken into custody and brought to Amethi. SP Sarvanan T said, Kajal's mobile phone has also been recovered from the accused. The police timely solved this case and arrested the accused. The team that worked on the case will be given a reward of 35000 rupees.

stories.title: Doctor allegedly murdered by wife her brother-in-law:Brother says victim married again two months ago
stories.summary: A doctor who had a love marriage two months ago died in hospital at 4 am on Saturday in Bareilly. His brother alleged that the doctor's wife and her brother poisoned him before dumping him outside the Mayor's camp office in the Civil Lines area. Passers-by admitted him to hospital at around 8 pm on Friday. According to the family, the doctor told them before his death that his wife and her brother had brutally assaulted him. They also said his wife had been staying at her brother and sister-in-law's house for the past one and a half months. The incident falls under the Subhash Nagar area. Doctor had love marriage on April 15 Dr Kuldeep Goswami (40), who lived near Balaji Dham Temple in the Subhash Nagar area, ran a private clinic. He had divorced his first wife, Daya, three years ago and had a 13-year-old son, Utkarsh, a Class 7 student at Mother's Public School. Kuldeep married Gunjan (38) in a love marriage on 15 April. According to his brother Vinayak, Gunjan had been pressuring him to live separately from his parents since the wedding and frequently argued with his family members. About 15 days after the marriage, Gunjan left her in-laws' home, allegedly taking jewellery worth lakhs of rupees. She had since been living with her sister and brother-in-law in Sadar Bazaar, under the Cantt police station area. Kuldeep had gone to convince his wife According to the family, Dr Kuldeep had gone to his wife's house on Friday (3 July) to bring her back. They alleged that his wife, along with her sister and brother-in-law, poisoned him. After he died, the accused allegedly dumped his body by the roadside. On Saturday, the deceased's brother lodged a complaint at Cantt police station, accusing the trio of murder. Police have registered a murder case, sent the body for post-mortem, and launched an investigation. What Kuldeep said in the video Kuldeep's video has surfaced. In it, he said, I have become very troubled, that's why I am making this video. My marriage to Gunjan took place two months ago. After marriage I felt that I have been trapped in a well-planned conspiracy.After marriage, cash, gold-silver and other items from my house started disappearing. I once caught Gunjan giving 70 thousand rupees to my sister Reena. When asked, she said she was lending it and would return it later.Gradually, I became convinced that the theft happening in the house was being done by Gunjan herself. When I complained to her family members, they instead became ready to fight and assault. Gunjan's brother Amit had wrong intentions towards our younger sister-in-law. On the 30th, he behaved obscenely with sister-in-law. A complaint was filed at Subhash Nagar police station, but no action was taken.I had great faith in the law, but now I am completely broken. I want an investigation against Gunjan, Reena, Satish, and Amit. They should get the strictest punishment. With folded hands, I request CM Yogi, DM and SSP to conduct an impartial investigation of this entire matter. What happened to me should not happen to anyone else.Utkarsh, son, I love you. Take care of grandfather-grandmother and progress a lot in life. I also request my friends to support my son.
