stories.title: 'I'm thinking of stepping down':Kanpur councillor leader's AUDIO emerges; says mayor could have resolved the controversy
stories.summary: We are completely trapped, Vikas... We are thinking of resigning. These unnecessary troubles we are getting, they will stop, Vikas. Those new big leaders of our party (BJP) have come recently, Saurabh Dev, Golu... They don't have to do anything themselves... they are causing us trouble. If we want, we can make everyone sit down and fold their hands today, end the matter, but the Mayor doesn't want to. These things were said by Naveen Pandit, leader of the councillor group, to Vikas Jaiswal, who was opposing the Mayor, after holding a press conference against the rebel councillors in Pramila Auditorium. On Friday, the Dainik Bhaskar App received an audio of the conversation between the two councillors. So, what exactly was discussed for 5 minutes between BJP councillor Naveen Pandit, who held a press conference against the rebel councillors and then on the other hand claimed to be trapped, and rebel councillor Vikas Jaiswal? Read the report Now read the conversation between rebel councillor Vikas Jaiswal and councilor party leader Naveen Pandit Vikas Jaiswal- Where are you? Naveen Pandit- I am at home. Vikas Jaiswal- What happened today, what was the press conference for? Naveen Pandit- Brother, what can I say, I am absolutely... absolutely feeling like this, that it seems to me that in two-three days... what can I say, man, I... Vikas Jaiswal- The matter had just gotten on track with great difficulty. Naveen Pandit- Nothing, these days new big leaders of our party have arrived, Saurabh Dev, Golu. There should be a press conference; they don't want to do anything themselves... Vikas Jaiswal- Saurabh Dev brother, is building houses, bungalows of two hundred square yards each, his wife is working. Golu has earned crores of rupees, have these people come to ruin the BJP or the organisation? Naveen Pandit- They are ruining us. Vikas Jaiswal- Naveen brother, you... I can understand your compulsion. I know how revolutionary you are, I... people were telling us. Naveen Pandit- We are completely trapped, Vikas... Vikas Jaiswal- You told us so many times, let's sit and sort this out... but what to say, we said these people are using Bunty. Naveen Pandit- You understand, they should understand, man, they don't seem to understand. Vikas Jaiswal- They are steeped in arrogance. Naveen Pandit- What to say, they... let's finish the talk, it bothers me, they are family members, it's a family, still nothing. If we want today, we can make everyone sit down and fold their hands, and end the matter. Vikas Jaiswal- Oh, you told us many times, did we ever refuse you? Naveen Pandit- No, never, Vikas Bhai. Vikas Jaiswal- Till date, the Mayor has never called anyone and said, "Come, let's sit." Naveen Pandit- You are not our companion of today, but of 15 years. We've started feeling ashamed to talk. What should we talk to you about, tell us? Vikas Jaiswal- We understand your helplessness, my brother. We can understand your pain. Where you are stuck, in what predicament. On one side, Kapoor Sahab is busy there, in Govind Nagar, we can understand those people, you never work by bending so much, my brother. Today, we can understand your helplessness. Naveen Pandit - We are thinking of resigning. Yes, resign from the post of councillor, and say, "Brother, this is not going to feed us." These unnecessary troubles we are getting, they will stop, Vikas. Vikas Jaiswal- Brother, tell me, now we got information that the Mayor's father had an operation. Naveen Pandit- Operation? Vikas Jaiswal- Yes. Naveen Pandit- Not an operation, chemotherapy is happening. Chemotherapy is happening daily. Vikas Jaiswal- Yes, yes, some health issues were going on in Delhi. Naveen Pandit- Chemotherapy happens from Monday to Friday, Vikas Bhai, and mother is staying there. She will come now, she will come by train. Vikas Jaiswal- So, at this time, what was the need for Bunty to get all this done? Naveen Pandit- He is getting chemotherapy, not an operation. Vikas Jaiswal- I am saying that father is unwell, there is so much pain for father at home, so the mayor... what was the need for Bunty to do all this? Naveen Pandit- That's right. His own... Vikas Jaiswal- And Saurabh Dev understands this, Bablu Bhaiya Vajpayee ji was such a good friend of ours, his son is getting contract work done by Vikas Vajpayee. Don't we know what all is happening in the water department, and what is not happening? Naveen Pandit- You know everything, my brother, you are not new to the municipal corporation. You know everyone down to their hair. You also know everyone, you recognize every flying bird. Vikas Jaiswal- Man, if Vikas Jaiswal has ever taken even an inch of space, we fought for them last time, how much disrepute we brought to the party. Naveen Pandit- You are a councilor for three-four terms... You always used to dedicate yourself to the service of society, what are you saying? Vikas Jaiswal- Brother, they did not accept our Tapeshwari temple proposal for the temple, Maa Tapeshwari Devi temple. They did not accept the waterlogging at Phoolbagh on Birhana Road. They stopped the beautification work of Birhana Road. They didn't give money for the Baratshala. Oh man, we never asked for anything. Naveen Pandit- Our image shouldn't be built, let everyone else's be built. We are just... like, when we are needed, call us... use us like a tool and throw us away. Vikas Jaiswal- Brother, don't ruin your career because of these people, my brother. Naveen Pandit- I am going to Vaishno Devi, we are going. Navin Pandit- We are going to Vaishno Devi, will go on the 10th-12th. Vikas Jaiswal- Poor Pawan was in great pain, we explained to Pawan repeatedly. This is not Navin Bhaiya, he is being made to say this. Navin Pandit- Suppose two people were sitting with us, what kind of written agreement did we make or did something or... did something. But they should also speak everything with restraint on Facebook, man. Huh? Now he... Vikas Jaiswal- Has anything been written on Facebook? Navin Pandit- Yes, you know these people's habit, all this Facebook-WhatsApp... Oh, we can also make 50 people say it, but what's the need for us? Vikas Jaiswal- No, no, we'll talk now. Listen, someone must have written that for you, but listen, he respects you. Poor guy was crying. Navin Pandit- Brother, this small... Vikas Jaiswal- His wife is admitted, brother. Naveen Pandit- Oh man, tell me, God! Today Sandeep Paswan came, he told me. Vikas Jaiswal- Tell me, his wife was in emergency, in ICU. She has been admitted three times, everything is going on in his family too. Naveen Pandit- My brother, I don't understand. What should we do? Vikas Jaiswal- Let's go. Naveen Pandit- Understand, see you tomorrow. See you tomorrow at the Municipal Corporation. Vikas Jaiswal- You meet separately, not at the Municipal Corporation, meet somewhere else. Naveen Pandit- Okay, you come to Jageshwar, come to Govind Nagar, come to some place. Vikas Jaiswal- We will come, we will come tomorrow. We will sit one on one. Naveen Pandit- We will not go to the Municipal Corporation tomorrow, we will not go... Vikas Jaiswal- No-no, we will sit one on one, you guys, okay, you and I will sit. Naveen Pandit- Okay brother. Vikas Jaiswal- Good night. Now we tell you what the whole dispute is Complaints made from District President to Defense Minister and CM, yet the dispute was not resolved The house was in session at Kanpur Municipal Corporation on December 26, 2025. During this, councillors Pawan Gupta and Ankit Maurya created a ruckus over their demands. After the ruckus, the Mayor had expelled both councillors from the house meetings for three days. In protest of the expulsion, four other BJP councillors also came out in support of the two councillors, accusing the mayor and her son of not providing budget for regional development works, which further deepened the dispute. 6 councilors opened a front against the mayor and first presented their case before Kanpur District President Anil Dixit. When the dispute did not stop even after this, they took their matter to Yogendra Upadhyay, the minister in charge of Kanpur. The minister in charge also spoke to the 6 councillors and understood the whole matter, but the matter did not calm down. After this, the 6 councillors opposing the mayor met State President Pankaj Chaudhary, and not only that, the councillors even reached Defence Minister Rajnath Singh to present their case, but the dispute did not stop. After this, on June 18, councillor Pawan Gupta complained about the mayor by giving a letter to the CM during a program at the CSA campus. After a complaint to the CM, the dispute escalated again, and BJP councillors, led by councillor group leader Naveen Pandit, unitedly held a press conference on behalf of the mayor and demanded the expulsion of all six councillors from the party. Following this, an audio clip of Naveen Pandit, the leader of the councillor group who held a press conference against the rebel councillors, has now surfaced.

stories.title: Brother arrested after sister's murder:Suspected affair behind killing; hospital tips off police
stories.summary: In Meerut, a brother, angered by his sister's affair, shot and killed her. He shot his sister in the head. As soon as she was shot, the sister fell there, covered in blood. After shooting her, the brother remained hidden in the house. When the mother arrived, the brother and other family members rushed the daughter towards the hospital. During this time, blood kept flowing from the house to the hospital. They reached Jagdamba Hospital at 7:10 AM on Saturday. They told the doctors that the daughter was injured from a fall. However, due to it being a gunshot wound, the doctors informed the police and started treatment. Aksa (21) died there. Being a case of a gunshot, the police took cognizance of the matter and investigated. It was found that the family members had concealed the incident. The accused brother, Aarish (23), has been arrested. Also, at his instance, a .315 bore country-made pistol used in the murder has been recovered. The accused has confessed to the murder during interrogation. The incident took place in Zakir Colony, under the Lohia Nagar police station area. See 3 pictures Mother said I was in the bathroom Aksha's mother Asifa said- I didn't see anything. I had just gone to the toilet after offering prayers. When I came out, my daughter was lying covered in blood. I immediately put a sheet over her. The mother tearfully said- I and the children live alone in this house. Aksha has studied up to 8th grade. Aksha doesn't have a father. He died 12 years ago. Aksha is the only sister among four brothers. The eldest son is Arish and Aksha is second. While Kaif is third. Then there are Ahad and Junaid. Read what SP City said SP City Vinayak Gopal Bhosle said that on Saturday morning at 7:10 AM, Jagdamba Hospital informed the concerned police station that an injured young woman had been brought to the hospital. Upon receiving the information, the police reached the spot. It was found to be a gunshot case. The girl had been shot. After this, the CO Kotwali himself went to the girl's house for investigation, and during questioning and investigation, it was revealed that her own brother, Aarish, had shot the girl around 6 AM. After this, the family members took the girl to the hospital, where she died during treatment. The reasons for the murder are also being investigated. Suspicion of murder due to an affair From the police interrogation so far, it appears that Arish killed his sister Aksa on suspicion of a love affair. Aksa used to talk to a young man from the neighborhood. The family had become aware of this. Therefore, the family wanted to arrange their daughter's marriage. But Aksa had refused to marry. The teenager continued to talk to that young man. According to the police, there was an argument in the family over this matter on Friday night as well. It is suspected that due to this, the brother killed her on Saturday morning.

stories.title: Ex-IAS claims ₹5 cr gold-plated Ramcharitmanas Missing:Says Champat Rai gave no receipt; Kedarnath-Badrinath also face donation theft allegations
stories.summary: Amid the donation theft controversy at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir, former Union Home Secretary Laxmi Narayan has claimed that his gold-plated Ramcharitmanas has gone missing. He said he had donated a 1.25-quintal Ramcharitmanas to the Ram Temple Trust on 8 April, 2024, but has not received an acknowledgment receipt to date. He further alleged that the Ramcharitmanas disappeared from the temple 3-4 months later. The 1,000-page Ramcharitmanas is coated with 24-carat gold and is valued at Rs 5 crore. Speaking to a media channel, he said, When I reached Ayodhya, Champat Rai made me wait for nine hours. I folded my hands and said, 'Sir, this is the savings of my entire lifetime. Please ensure that the Ramcharitmanas is kept in the temple.' He replied, 'Many people give me jewellery and various other items. Should I keep displaying only such things? The former IAS officer said he contacted Temple Construction Committee Chairman Nripendra Mishra and Trust member Gopal Rao, but nothing happened. He then visited Ayodhya again. After waiting for four hours, he finally met Champat Rai, who allegedly told him, 'I can't do anything. Go wherever you want.' Meanwhile, on Saturday, the Ram Mandir Trust released the agenda for its meeting scheduled for 6 July. The meeting will decide on the resignations of Trust General Secretary Champat Rai and Trustee Dr. Anil Mishra. It will also discuss the preliminary SIT report and issues related to temple management. Reacting to reports of Champat Rai's resignation from the Trust, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand took a jibe, saying, Will resigning after theft in the court of such a great deity be enough to escape? What kind of drama is this? You will be beaten. If the government does not send them to jail and ensure proper punishment, the public will beat them. After Ram Mandir, donation theft allegations surface at Kedarnath and Badrinath Following the allegations of donation theft at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir, similar allegations have now surfaced at the Kedarnath and Badrinath temples. Sandeep Khatri, president of the religious organisation Bhairav Sena, has written to the Badrinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee (BKTC), accusing the personal assistant to the BKTC chairman of theft. After receiving the complaint, BKTC CEO Sohan Singh Rangar issued notices to the personal assistant and all staff on duty, seeking their response within three days. CCTV footage from the temples has also been secured for investigation. BKTC Chairman Hemant Dwivedi said the temple committee is taking the matter seriously. Notices have been issued to the employees against whom allegations have been made, asking them to submit explanations. If any employee is found guilty, strict legal action will be taken. No statement has yet been issued by Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami. The government is waiting for the temple committee's report on the matter. Ram Mandir donation theft, Avinash gets the biggest share, ₹20.39 lakh recovered Note: Avinash was also found with 112 US dollars, two gold chains, one ring and silver jewellery.

stories.title: Govt offering up to ₹1.08 lakh for installing solar panels:UP administration plans to reduce public power bill; here's how to apply
stories.summary: You can make your home's electricity bill 'zero'. This means you will use the same amount of electricity, but you won't have to pay the bill. For this, you will have to install solar panels on the roof of your house. The cost is also not too high, as the government provides a subsidy of up to Rs 1.08 lakh. You will have to install solar panels according to your home's electricity load. It is important that you ensure the quality of the panels is good. What things should be kept in mind while installing a solar plant? How many watts of panel is appropriate to install? Read in this report Understand how the electricity bill becomes zero Alok Srivastava, who lives in the old city, was paying an electricity bill of 3 to 4 thousand rupees every month. He installed a 4 KW solar panel on the roof of his house. He says - when the sun shines well, the panels generate about 25 units of electricity every day. This amounts to 750 units in a month. Now, if he consumes up to 750 units of electricity, only the meter charge is added to the bill, which is around 300 rupees. If he consumes more than 750 units, then he has to pay the bill at the rate of ₹7 per unit. Government provides subsidy based on load Bank provides loans for solar panels Installing a 3 kW solar system costs between ₹1.68 lakh to ₹1.93 lakh, depending on the brand. This includes the cost of solar panels, inverter, structure, wiring, and installation. If you don't have the full amount, you can also take a solar loan from any government or private bank. Interest rates of government banks are around 7%. Whereas, private banks charge interest from 9% to 12%. Upon receiving the subsidy, you can deposit it into your loan account. This will reduce your monthly EMI and your total cost will be around ₹60,000 to ₹85,000. Keep these things in mind before installing solar panels Before installing solar panels at home, it is important to check some important things. A 1-kilowatt system requires about 100 square feet of space. Whereas, a 3-kilowatt system requires 300 square feet of space. Choose a solar system based on your needs Install solar panels in a place that receives good sunlight throughout the day. Shade from trees or buildings can reduce electricity generation by 30-40%. Panels are quite heavy, so checking the strength of the roof is also important. Regular cleaning and maintenance should also be done so that the system continues to provide better electricity. Off-grid systems do not receive subsidies Solar consultant Manish Mishra explains - Solar systems work in two ways. One- On-grid and Second- Off-grid. What is an On-grid Solar System? This system is connected to the electricity department's grid. During the day, electricity generated by solar is used in the home. Excess electricity goes into the grid via a net meter. At night, electricity is received from the grid. At the end of the month, the bill is generated based on the electricity sent to and received from the grid. This system also shuts down during power outages. It is cheap because it does not incur battery costs. PM Surya Ghar Yojana and UP government subsidies are available on this system. A 3 kW solar plant gets a subsidy of ₹1.08 lakh Note: No subsidy is available for solar plants with a capacity above 3 kW. What is an Off-Grid Solar System This system is not connected to the electricity department's grid. It requires a battery. It works similarly to an inverter system installed in a home. The only difference is that instead of storing electricity from the government grid (electricity department), it stores electricity generated from solar power in the battery. This system keeps the supply on during power outages. Due to the battery, its cost is higher than an on-grid system. A normal battery needs to be replaced every 5-7 years. Lithium-ion batteries can last for 10-12 years. These are even more expensive. Subsidies are not available for this system. 2,000 Rooftop Solar Systems are being installed daily in UP Uttar Pradesh ranks first in the country in terms of rooftop solar, meaning installing solar plants on the roofs of houses. Here, about 2,000 rooftop solar systems are being installed daily. More than 6,000 registered vendors are working for this. From February 2024 to June 2026, more than 5.57 lakh solar systems have been installed. These include 9200 government and 691 private commercial buildings, and solar plants have also been installed on the land of water tanks and tube wells/pumping stations being built under the Jal Jeevan Mission. For this, more than 3602 crore rupees have been provided as subsidy by the central government and more than 1200 crore rupees by the state government.

stories.title: Day 3 of UP-TET 2026:Strict checks continue, female candidates asked to remove hairpins, jewellery; 26 held for alleged cheating
stories.summary: Saturday marked the third and final day of the Teacher Eligibility Test (UP-TET) 2026 in UP. Candidates were allowed entry into the examination centers from 7:15 AM to 8:45 AM. During this time, admit cards were checked, biometric details were matched, and retina scans were performed. The first shift examination will run from 9:30 AM to 12:00 PM, and the second shift examination will run from 2:30 PM to 5:00 PM. In Gorakhpur, female candidates were asked to remove hair claws, hairpins, and jewellery. In Hathras, belts and shoes were removed for checking. In Kanpur, women's bangles were removed. In Lalitpur, a woman's amulet and necklace were removed from her neck. In Hathras, a female candidate from Aligarh was denied entry for arriving two minutes late. As the gate did not open, she returned disappointed. In Raebareli, a dog suddenly appeared in front of a student's car who was going to take the exam. In an attempt to save it, the car went out of control and fell into a canal. The student and her father were pulled out by nearby people. After this, both left for the examination center in another car. Today, on the final day, 3,78,655 candidates will appear for the examination. In two days, 26 cheaters have been caught from across the state. Among these, 15 candidates were caught on the first day and 9 on the second day. As many as 955 examination centers have been set up in 60 districts of the state. A total of 19.94 lakh candidates are taking the examination, including 1,85,791 in-service teachers.

stories.title: Wife kills husband, buries body in bathroom, covers with tiles:Uses same bathroom daily, misleads family for 45 days
stories.summary: A man from Bharatpur was murdered by his wife. The accused woman buried the body in the bathroom of the house itself. She had tiles laid over it. The accused continued to use this same bathroom for bathing. She misled people for about 45 days. On Friday (July 3), the entire matter was exposed. The police recovered the body of Surendra Kumar Sharma (44) buried in the bathroom. The police also arrested the accused woman Ruby. The incident is from Renuka Dham Colony in the Sikandra police station area of Agra. First see - pictures of the crime scene... Marriage happened 16 years ago, there was discord between the two Surendra Kumar Sharma (44), originally from Bharatpur, Rajasthan, was living in Renuka Dham Colony in Dahatora, Sikandra area of Agra, along with his mother, wife Ruby and their two daughters. He was married to Ruby from Etawah in 2010. The couple has two daughters, Ridhi (13) and Siddhi (9). His brother Anil Sharma said there had been long-standing disputes between the husband and wife. Now know the complete matter Information given to brother-in-law on 18th May Surendra’s brother Anil Sharma said that Ruby called him on the morning of May 18. She informed him that there was some police-related issue at home and asked him to take away their mother and both daughters. When Anil tried to get full details, she did not explain anything clearly. She only said not to come home and added that she had made the mother and children sit at a nearby shop, from where they should be taken. Second call claiming Surendra had left home Anil said he was about to reach his home in Awadhpuri with the mother and both daughters when Ruby called again. She said Surendra had forcibly opened the house lock, taken ₹5,000, and left after a quarrel. She further claimed that he had said he would call after 2–3 days to inform them of his whereabouts. Ruby stayed at brother-in-law’s house for 7–8 days On the evening of May 19, Ruby again contacted her brother-in-law Anil Sharma and said she was not feeling comfortable staying there and should also be taken to where the children were. That night, Anil brought her to his house. Ruby then stayed there with both children for around 7–8 days. Missing report filed on May 26 During this period, there was no trace of Surendra. Anil Sharma and other family members repeatedly questioned Ruby, but she kept misleading them with different versions of events. When no clue was found despite continuous efforts, Anil Sharma lodged a missing person report on May 26 for his brother. Told brother-in-law - I have buried the body in the house Anil Sharma said that he later asked Ruby directly about Surendra’s whereabouts. She then told him that she had buried him inside the bathroom of the house. He further stated that on June 27, when suspicion increased, he brought his mother from Surendra’s house and took her to Bharatpur, where he obtained the bank account statement. He alleged that Ruby was using the pension money credited to the mother’s account. According to Anil, on Friday around 6 am, Ruby called him again and asked him to come to the house. When he reached Renuka Dham Colony, he asked about Surendra. Initially, Ruby avoided answering, but when he reassured her and asked her to tell the truth, saying he would support her if she was in trouble, she became emotional and confessed everything. She said Surendra had hanged himself and that in panic she buried the body under the bathroom floor of the house. Police action and arrest According to Agra Police, during investigation, CCTV footage from around the house was checked and Ruby was seen present during various moments, but she never disclosed the truth. She was arrested on Friday. Sleeping pills in food and concealment of body During interrogation, Ruby told police that on the night of May 17, she allegedly mixed more than a dozen sleeping pills into kheer and served it to her husband Surendra. After the incident, she buried the body under the bathroom floor, got it plastered, and later installed tiles over it. She continued using the same bathroom for bathing, while keeping the concealment hidden for a long period.

stories.title: Kanpur sees wettest day in 15 years:Rain alert issued for 28 UP districts
stories.summary: The monsoon continues to remain active across Uttar Pradesh with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing a rain alert for 28 districts on Saturday. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are also likely. Most districts saw sunny spells in the morning with intermittent cloud cover. Kanpur recorded its wettest 3rd July in 15 years, receiving 108 mm of rainfall. The previous record was 101 mm, logged on 1 July 2011. Rain lashed 20 districts across the state on Friday. In Mathura, heavy showers left several roads submerged under up to a foot of water, causing vehicles to break down. A railway underpass was flooded up to neck level, disrupting movement. The state received an average of 6.2 mm of rainfall over the past 24 hours, around 9 per cent above the normal 5.7 mm. However, cumulative rainfall since 1 June stands at 64.5 mm, which is 43 per cent below the seasonal normal of 112.5 mm. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said the monsoon has now become active over Uttar Pradesh and persistent rainfall is expected in the coming days. Temperatures have dropped by up to 8°C, and similar weather conditions are likely to continue for the next week. However, he added that the state, including Lucknow, is still expected to receive below-normal rainfall during the monsoon season.

stories.title: Firing at Kashi Vishwanath Temple:PAC jawan's carbine falls, two shots accidentally fired; 3 injured
stories.summary: On Saturday morning at 7:30 AM, a carbine fell from the hand of a PAC jawan at the gate of Kashi Vishwanath Temple. Following this, two rounds were fired from the carbine. Fortunately, the bullets directly hit the road. Subsequently, gravel and small stones bounced up and hit three people. Police personnel present at the scene took all three to the divisional hospital. According to doctors, everyone's condition is currently out of danger. The injured have been identified as Nikki Gupta, Rambabu, and Vikas Yadav. All three injured are flower and garland vendors who operate outside the temple. According to doctors, they are in a stable condition and out of danger. They sustained injuries after being hit by stone fragments dislodged by the bullets. The incident occurred at VIP Gate No. 4 of the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. The sudden gunfire in the middle of the crowd triggered panic, with people scrambling for safety. For a few moments, no one could understand what had happened. On hearing the shots, security personnel immediately rushed to the spot and brought the situation under control. They informed people that the rounds had been fired accidentally and assured them that the situation was under control.

stories.title: Dwarka Shankaracharya angry over Ram Mandir donation theft:Says shrine entrusted to unfit people; accuses govt for treating site as tourist spot
stories.summary: Anger continues to mount among devotees over the alleged donation theft at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. Joining the growing criticism, Dwarka Shardapeeth Shankaracharya Swami Sadanand Saraswati has levelled serious allegations in an interview with Divya Bhaskar. He said, “Tampering with donations offered at the feet of Lord Ram was not merely a financial offence but a betrayal of the faith of millions of devotees”. According to him, “Governments that lack an understanding of Sanatan Dharma and scriptures cannot administer temples properly. They view temples as tourist destinations rather than centres of faith and spiritual practice”. The Shankaracharya also cautioned against making lower-level employees scapegoats to shield those truly responsible. He demanded that a white paper detailing all temple donations be made public and called for an end to government interference in temple administration through the creation of an independent Sanatan Board. Read the sensational interview of the Shankaracharya that holds a mirror to religious leaders, trustees and the government. Question: Allegations of donation theft have been made at Ram Mandir. What do you have to say about this? Answer: “Donations given to God become divine wealth. If theft has actually occurred, this is not just a financial crime but a betrayal of faith with Lord Shri Ram and millions of devotees. An impartial and fearless investigation should be conducted”. He claimed, “People are saddened by what has happened in Ayodhya. This incident means that the government has neither knowledge of scriptures nor experienced officials. The government's job is to provide facilities to people, not to perform religious rituals”. He further stated, “People consider religious places like Ayodhya, Dwarka, Badrinath, Tirupati as the land of penance of sages and saints. The government, leaders and system consider them tourist spots. Therefore, religious sentiment does not awaken in them. It should be understood that entrusting work to incompetent people yields the same result that was obtained in Ayodhya”. He added, “The government does not have the moral authority to manage temples. There is no government interference in any mosque, church or gurudwara. Only in Hindu religious places is there government interference. Temples should be free from such governance”. Question: Donations have been stolen from a nationwide center of faith like the Ram Mandir. What kind of act is this religiously? Answer: Shankaracharya said, “In Sanatan Dharma, a temple is considered to be the form of God. No person has any right over it. Therefore, what happened at Dev Dham is not just theft but also a serious religious crime”. He further said, “The question arises that how was this possible at the sacred birthplace of Lord Shri Ram in a religious city like Ayodhya? This is like a poisonous snake living in a sandalwood forest”. He added, “The scriptures say that a person who steals the wealth of deities out of greed is guilty of a grave sin. Therefore, if there has been fraud in the donations offered at the feet of Lord Ram, it is also an attack on the faith of millions of devotees”. Question: Do you think that in the Ram Mandir, small people are being trapped while big people are being saved? Answer: He said, “It is inappropriate to make accusations against any person or organization without evidence. However, if action is taken only against lower-level people and big people are not questioned, then naturally society's faith in the justice system begins to waver”. He claimed, “It is said in the Mahabharata that where there is no truth, there is no dharma, so my only expectation is that the investigation of this matter should not be influenced by any position, influence, prestige or political pressure”. He added, “The innocent must be protected and the guilty, no matter how influential, must be held accountable before the court. This is also in accordance with the dignity of Lord Shri Ram”. Question: This controversy has hurt the faith of crores of Ram devotees. What would you say to the Trust and the government to keep the faith of devotees steadfast? Answer: Shankaracharya stated, “I would tell the Trust to make transparency your strength, not a burden. Prestige increases not by hiding the truth but by revealing it”. He added, “I would tell the government that this is not just a matter of law, but also a matter of faith for millions of people. Therefore, justice should be completely impartial, swift and fearless, and my request to Ram devotees is to have faith in Lord Shri Ram, not in any individual”. He further said, “Individuals may err, but the glory of God, the sanctity of Ram Janmabhoomi and the dignity of Sanatan Dharma never diminish”. Question: Is there a need to change the entire structure of the Ram Temple Trust? Answer: He said, “My request is not to change individuals but to change the rules and improve the system. That is, management should be entrusted to capable persons”. He stated, “The country has seen the consequences of entrusting management to incompetent and unqualified people. Any organization becomes great not because of individuals but because of its principles and transparent system”. He added, “If there are flaws in administration or the system, solutions should be brought courageously. There should be a system in which guidance of religious leaders, financial transparency, regular audits and accountability are permanently established”. He further said, “Ram Mandir belongs to the entire Hindu community and therefore its management should also be exemplary”. Question: What is your demand now? Answer: Shankaracharya said, “I have no demand against any person or party. My demand is only to protect religion and truth”. Question: So much politics is played in the name of Ram Mandir in the country, votes are sought, then why do politicians remain silent when theft occurs? Answer: He said, “This is a matter of introspection. Lord Shri Ram does not belong to any party but to the entire nation. If public support is sought in the name of Ram, then equal responsibility and sensitivity on issues related to Ram Mandir is necessary”. He added, “I am not a supporter of any party nor am I an opponent. I am merely a religious seeker. The acharyas of Sanatan Dharma are above politics”. He further said, “Political parties have divided Hindu society into many parts. There are Hindus in every party, therefore if any saint or acharya supports a political party, it will unknowingly result in injustice to other Hindus”. Question: If questions arise regarding the use of donations by a temple trust or management, what steps should the trust take? Answer: Shankaracharya said, “The answer to doubts is not silence but transparency. The trust should come forward and disclose all details. Independent investigation should be welcomed and if there are any mistakes, they should be corrected immediately”. Question: Should organizations like the Ram Janmabhoomi Trust have a guiding committee consisting of Shankaracharyas or leading saints from the four seats of the country? What are your thoughts on this matter? Answer: He said, “The great religious places of India are not just administrative centers, they represent the faith of millions of devotees and eternal traditions”. He added, “There should be a guiding religious council consisting of Shankaracharyas from the four seats of the country, the five leading Vaishnavaacharyas, other respected and esteemed Acharyas, and leading saints to provide guidance from time to time according to Dharma and scriptures”. Question: Do you think the darshan of Ram Mandir is being commercialized? Answer: He said, “Temples and pilgrimage sites are centers of religion and faith. They should not be developed as tourist destinations”. He added, “Accumulating wealth in the guise of religion is inappropriate. A temple is a center of service, not business. It is necessary to arrange systems but their nature should be according to religious standards”. Question: What rules should be in place to maintain transparency in temple donations? Answer: Shankaracharya said, “Faith in religion is based not on secrecy but on purity and transparency. Where accounts are clear, faith becomes stronger”. He added, “I believe that 5 principles should be mandatory for the management of divine wealth”, Question: According to scriptures, where should temple donations be used? Answer: He said, “They should be used for worship of deities, Vedas, protection of gurukuls, protection of cows, food donation, hospitals, religious propagation, Sanskrit education, honoring scholars and public welfare”. He added, “Temple funds are often used for non-religious activities or other projects which are against the faith of devotees and principles of scriptures”. Story Input: Kamal Parmar

stories.title: 3 miscreants enter soldier's home using ruse of wedding card:Gang nabbed after encounter with police
stories.summary: Three miscreants entered a soldier's house in Kasganj, on Friday evening at 4:30 PM on the pretext of delivering a wedding card. All three had pistols. They took the soldier, his son, daughter-in-law, and grandson hostage. After this, they started looting. However, the family seized an opportunity and locked all three miscreants inside the house. After this, the police were informed. The police cordoned off the entire area. An encounter between the police and the miscreants lasted for about two hours. In this, two miscreants were shot in the leg. The third miscreant was injured while trying to escape by jumping from the third floor. Know the full story The incident took place near Ganjdundwara in Patiyali town. The house which was targeted belongs to Army jawan Ravindra Singh (55). Ravindra is posted in Guwahati for the Assam Rifles. His son Rahul Singh (32), daughter-in-law Pinky (28), and grandson Aryansh (10) were at home during the burglary. On Friday evening, around 4:30 PM, three youths arrived on a Splendor bike. They knocked on the door of the house. When Pinky opened the door, the miscreants entered the house on the pretext of giving a wedding card. Rahul said that as soon as the miscreants entered the house, they hit him on his face with the butt of a pistol. Due to this, he was seriously injured. “After this, the criminals held me, my wife, and my son hostage at gunpoint and started looting,” Rahul recalled. Pinky raised an alarm Rahul's wife Pinky said that a miscreant had held her with one hand. He had a pistol in his other hand. While the second miscreant had held her son. During this, Pinky, showing courage, pulled the miscreant's scarf and started shouting 'thief-thief' loudly. Hearing the screams, some people passing by the house gathered and started banging on the door. This scared the miscreants, and they ran to the roof. Seeing an opportunity, Rahul came out of the house with his wife and child. They locked the house from the outside. Then they informed the police about the incident. Police surrounded the house, two miscreants injured in firing As soon as the police received information about the incident, they reached the spot. They surrounded the entire house from all sides. A tall ladder was called to go inside. Around 7:15 PM, the police team entered the house. A short while later, sounds of firing started coming from inside. Two criminals shot in the leg during encounter According to the police, the criminals inside the house fired at the police team. In retaliation, the police also fired. During the encounter, two criminals were shot in the legs. After this, the police apprehended both of them. The injured criminals were sent to the hospital for treatment under police guard. Meanwhile, another criminal jumped from the third floor in an attempt to escape. He was seriously injured after the jump. All three accused are residents of Kasganj Police have identified the three accused as Abhishek (19), Vikas (20), and Shaurya Pratap Singh (20). All three are residents of Kasganj district. The injured accused have been admitted to the hospital for treatment. Upon receiving information about the incident, Superintendent of Police O.P. Singh reached the spot. He inspected the crime scene and gathered information about the entire incident from the officials. Currently, the police are investigating the matter.

stories.title: 'Dad climbed on mum's stomach and kept stabbing her':Son's chilling account of influencer mother's murder
stories.summary: “Mother was lying in the courtyard. All her clothes were red with blood. Blood was flowing from her hands, face, and neck. Mommy was screaming - 'Help! Help! Let go!', but father was sitting on mother's stomach. He had a knife in one hand, and with the other, he was holding Mommy. He was stabbing Mommy with the knife. Even after much pleading, Papa did not stop. He just kept saying, ‘Make a video, you make a video. I will make your reel.’ After this, Papa also stabbed himself.” The children gave this account to the police after witnessing their mother's murder. In Harra Khiwai village, under the Sarurpur police station area of Meerut, Pradeep Chauhan stabbed his wife Nisha Chauhan (40) on July 3 (Friday). Pradeep first threw Nisha to the ground in the courtyard and beat her severely. Then he kept stabbing Nisha till she breathed her last. A team of Dainik Bhaskar reached Harra Khiwai, 35 km from the city. Here, Nisha's children narrated the entire story. Arranged marriage took place 18 years ago Pradeep, an AC mechanic, lives in Harra Khiwai. Pradeep was married 18 years ago to Nisha, a resident of Garhmukteshwar, Hapur. It was an arranged marriage for both. They have three children – elder son Dev, second son Rohit, and a daughter Angel. All three children study in the village. Nisha ran a beauty parlor at home. For the past few years, she used to create reels and post them on social media. She had become an influencer. Pradeep had returned to India from Dubai just 2 years ago. He used to do AC repairing in Dubai. Then he came to Meerut, where he did the same work. Pradeep's younger brother lived in a separate house near him. His younger brother lives with his wife Rinki, and two sons. Pradeep's parents have passed away. Meanwhile, at Nisha's maternal home, her elderly mother Nanda, two brothers, and their family live in Garh. Son says his father sat on mother's stomach and stabbed her Nisha's elder son Dev said, “It was around 6 AM on Friday. I was sleeping in the room with my younger siblings. Suddenly, loud screams from Mom started coming from the courtyard. We woke up. I immediately got out of bed, opened the room door, and ran outside. I saw Mom lying on the courtyard floor. Blood was flowing from Mom's hands, neck, face, and chest. There was blood on the floor too. Mom's clothes were red with blood.” “Mom was struggling to save herself. She was trying to get free from Dad. Mom was screaming, 'Help...help. Let go, let go of me.' Dad was sitting on Mom's stomach. He had a knife in one hand, and with the other, he was holding Mom. He was repeatedly stabbing Mom,” Dev said. “This knife was from our own kitchen. Dad was angrily saying, 'Go on, make videos. Make reels. I told you nothing would come of videos, but you wouldn't listen. You make a lot of reels.' I tried to stop him by grabbing Dad's hand, but he didn't stop.” Father also stabbed me, says son Dev said, “When I started intervening, Dad stabbed me. The knife hit my hand and my finger got cut. Blood started flowing from my hand. I said 'Dad, stop it, leave it, but he didn't listen. He kept shouting and stabbing.” “Meanwhile, mom's voice stopped, and her hands and feet also stopped moving. She was dead. Then Dad took the knife and ran towards the upstairs room. When we followed him, he stabbed himself in the hand. Blood started flowing from Dad's hand,” Dev said. “After this, both my siblings went screaming to our uncle's house in the neighborhood. They told them that Dad was stabbing Mom. Then our uncle, aunt, and neighbors came, and they called the police. They bandaged me and then those same people took Dad for treatment. By then, the police had also arrived,” he recalled. Mom and Dad had a dispute over getting the land registered in their name Dev said, “My mom and dad had no dispute. Dad loved Mom very much. He was the one who opened a parlor for Mom. Dad himself told Mom to make videos and post them. The account is doing well. We will get money from this.” “Mommy bore all the expenses of our house, because her parlor was doing very well. Many girls used to come daily. Mommy's social media account and YouTube were also doing very well. She used to get a lot of views. She was famous. Mommy used to pay for all our education,” he said. “On Friday, mommy and daddy were going to buy a piece of land. The sale deed for that land was to be done, and that was what the argument was about. Daddy wanted the land to be registered in his name but, mommy said that it was her money, and she would register the land in her name. An argument ensued between mommy and daddy over this. Daddy earns a little less money, but mommy's income was much better,” he said. ‘Dad was instigated by a relative’ Dev said, “My dad is very simple. He himself used to encourage mom. But our neighbour, a relative (uncle), used to instigate dad. Dad did all this under his influence.” “The relative (uncle) was jealous of mom's parlour and YouTube. That's why he was opening his cyber cafe next to our parlour. Where boys would stand all day and smoke cigarettes, gutkha. The atmosphere around our parlor would deteriorate and girls would not come to the beauty parlor,” he said. “This would have shut down mom's beauty parlor, but mom used to oppose it. The uncle misled dad. He said that mom makes wrong videos. She is doing wrong, maybe dad was angry about this. He got provoked and killed mom,” he said. The children said that their uncle should be punished. “We have lost our mom and dad. We have become homeless, orphans. We have lost everything. Who will take care of us now, but all this happened because of Vikas (uncle). The police should also catch Vikas and punish him,” the children said. Sister-in-law says Nisha was lying covered in blood Nisha's sister-in-law, Rinky, told Dainik Bhaskar, "We had never heard Nisha and Pradeep fight. They lived very well together. Today, I don't know why Pradeep bhaiya took this step. I can't understand anything. On Friday morning, we were in our house. My sister-in-law's house is outside in the lane. They were in their house. Suddenly, their children came screaming and knocked on the door. When we opened the door, the children said that ‘Auntie, Papa is stabbing Mummy.’" "Then we went to their house and saw that my sister-in-law Nisha was lying on the floor in the courtyard. Just then, our neighbours also arrived. Her breathing had stopped. Brother-in-law Pradeep was in the room on the roof. We took Nisha to the hospital, where doctors declared her dead," she said. Nisha has over 24,000 followers on Instagram Nisha Chauhan's Instagram ID is named rajputnisha_5m. The name written is Nisha Rajput. It has 24,400 followers. She has made 960 posts so far. She used to follow 10 people. In the bio, 'Your love', 'Target 50,000', 'Jai Shri Ram' and 'Jai Bhawani' are written. A link to her YouTube channel is also provided.

Devkinandan Thakur defends son amid trolling:'His only fault is that he's my son'
stories.summary: After the son of a religious preacher, Devkinandan Maharaj, appeared on a religious platform in Mathura, he has been continuously discussed and criticised. On this, Devkinandan Maharaj reacted openly, saying, "His (son) biggest 'fault' is only that he is my son." It is the responsibility of every parent to impart religion, service, and values to their children. On July 3 (Friday), in a special conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Devkinandan said that some people target those who perform Katha-bhajan but they do not question those who do wrong deeds. On the matter of theft of offerings at the Ram Temple, Devkinandan Maharaj said that it would not be appropriate to reach to any conclusion before the investigation is complete. He also reiterated the demand for forming a Sanatan Board with the participation of religious leaders for better utilisation of donations from large temples. Read the full conversation Question: Amid the Ram Temple dispute, there is a demand for a Sanatan Board. What is your opinion? Answer: The management of big temples like Vaishno Devi and Tirupati Balaji is with the governments. We do not understand how the donations received there are being utilised. Therefore, a Sanatan Board should be formed, which includes religious leaders like four Shankaracharyas and five Vaishnavacharyas. Question: Are the religious leaders satisfied with the action taken so far in the Ram Mandir offering theft case? Answer: It would be premature to say anything on this now. The investigation is ongoing. Only when the investigation is complete will it be known whether it proceeded in the right direction or not. Question: Are only the named accused involved, or could other people also have a role? Answer: As reported, around 50-60 people are to be interrogated. The picture will only become clear after the investigation is complete. Question: You are promoting your son in the religious field. There is also trolling on social media. What would you say? Answer: What is the trolling about? Is religion a business, that people are saying such things? Do they understand religion? Every parent imparts their values to their children. We are doing the same. Is it right to say anything to anyone just to get some views? Question: What was the thought behind giving your son a religious environment from childhood? Answer: My son is 14 years old now. To this day, he doesn't have a mobile phone. We have given him the same values that every parent should give to their children. If you hold a child's hand and take them to the temple from childhood, make them sit in satsang (spiritual gathering), they will learn to respect others. Good values make a child prosperous in every way. Question: What would you say about today's society and religion? Answer: The Ramayana tells us that there have always been two types of people in society. One, those who want the development of religion, and the other, those who want the destruction of religion. Ravana wanted to destroy yagnas and penance, while Lord Rama protected dharma and righteousness. Such people existed in the Treta Yuga as well, and they exist even today. The difference is that even today, society worships Lord Rama and burns effigies of Ravana. Question: Have you adopted a different tradition for your son's birthday as well? Answer: My son does not celebrate his birthday in a hotel or at a party. He celebrates his birthday by providing food and essential items to needy people. I believe that children should imbibe the values of service and compassion from childhood. Question: There are constant comments about your son. Does this bother you? Answer: Some people troll for narrating stories and singing bhajans. But, they don't question those who drink alcohol, gamble, or do wrong things. Someone said he didn't take the NEET exam. I want to ask, which NEET exam is there at the age of 14? His biggest 'fault' is simply that he is the son of Devkinandan Maharaj. Know what's happening on social media regarding Devkinandan Thakur's son Recited Bhagwat on a public platform Preacher Devkinandan Thakur has three daughters and one son. The son's name is Devansh. Devansh is currently studying in class 10. Devansh Thakur started studying Vedic texts, Bhagwat Katha, and Sanskrit shlokas at a very young age. Some time ago, Devansh recited Bhagwat Chintan for the first time on a public platform at a religious event organised in Somnath, Gujarat. Its video has also surfaced online. In the video, Devkinandan Thakur is seen sitting on a high stage. Meanwhile, Devansh Thakur was seen chanting bhajans on a white sofa located a short distance away. During this, father Devkinandan was seen looking at his son very attentively. After the video surfaced, a debate has started on social media. Some people started calling it a legacy of Sanatan tradition and family values, while others started linking it to the growing nepotism in the religious sector.

stories.title: Artist dressed as Lord Hanuman dances at BJP roadshow:Complaint filed in Chandigarh, alleges insult to deity
stories.summary: A controversy has erupted over a roadshow led by BJP President Nitin Naveen in Lucknow after an artist dressed as Lord Hanuman (Bajrangbali) was seen dancing while holding a BJP flag. On Monday at 12:55 pm, Advocate Vasu Ranjan, a lawyer at the Punjab and Haryana High Court and Chairman of the Council of Lawyers, sent a complaint by email to the Director General of Police (DGP) and the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) in Chandigarh. The complaint alleges that during the roadshow, a person dressed as Lord Hanuman was made to dance in front of BJP President Nitin Naveen, hurting the religious sentiments of millions of Hindus. The complainant described the act as an inappropriate and disrespectful use of the sacred image of Lord Hanuman. He has demanded the immediate registration of an FIR against those responsible, an impartial investigation into the incident, and the preservation of all digital and other evidence related to the event. What the complaint alleges Lord Hanuman is one of Hinduism's most revered deities Advocate Vasu Ranjan stated in the complaint that Lord Hanuman is one of the most revered deities in Hinduism. He alleged that using the deity's sacred attire for political campaigning and propaganda amounts to a direct insult to the religious sentiments of devotees and constitutes a deliberate act of desecration. According to the complaint, the use of a revered religious symbol for political purposes is objectionable and has deeply hurt the sentiments of devotees. Alleged offence under Section 299 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita The complaint states that, prima facie, the incident falls within the scope of Section 299 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. According to the complainant, the provision applies to cases involving the deliberate insult of a religion or religious beliefs in a manner that hurts religious sentiments. He alleged that using the sacred image and attire of Lord Hanuman during a political roadshow falls under this provision. Demand for investigation into the role of organisers and leaders The complaint states that the incident took place in the presence of senior BJP leaders, including the party's national president and a chief minister. It therefore calls for an investigation into the role of the organisers, event managers, the person dressed as Lord Hanuman, and all individuals who allegedly authorised, encouraged or knowingly permitted the act. The complainant also urged the investigating agency to examine the conduct of every person present at the event, including the senior leaders. Demand for preservation of evidence and legal action The complaint seeks the immediate preservation of all electronic, digital, and documentary evidence related to the incident. It further demands that strict legal action be taken against anyone found responsible during the investigation, irrespective of their position or status, in accordance with the law.

stories.title: Akhilesh fumes over Ram Mandir allegation:Asks BJP MP to delete post in 10 minutes or face FIR
stories.summary: The alleged theft of donations from the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya has escalated into a political controversy after Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav strongly objected to attempts to link him with one of the accused, Ram Shankar Yadav alias Tinnu. The row began after BJP MP Nishikant Dubey, who represents Godda in Jharkhand, posted on X, suggesting that Tinnu Yadav had been in contact with Akhilesh Yadav. Reacting sharply on Monday evening, Akhilesh demanded that the BJP MP delete the post within 10 minutes, warning that failure to do so would result in a named FIR being filed against him. Akhilesh demands public apology In a statement posted on social media, Akhilesh said not only should the BJP MP remove the post, but anyone who had shared or amplified it should also delete it immediately and issue a public apology. He warned that legal action would be initiated against those who continued to circulate what he described as false information. Akhilesh alleged that the BJP and its supporters were spreading misinformation to defame the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) community and asserted that the community would respond collectively. 'Delete the post or face legal action' Akhilesh said parliamentary privilege applies equally to both ruling and opposition MPs. Respecting what he described as the dignity of Lord Ram and parliamentary traditions, he said he was giving the BJP MP 10 minutes to delete the "false" post. "If the post is not removed, an FIR will be lodged immediately," he said, adding that BJP leaders would eventually have to face prolonged court proceedings and should not expect support from their political colleagues. He also accused the BJP of deliberately maligning the PDA community through misinformation. Why is Tinnu Yadav being linked to Akhilesh? Media reports recently claimed that Tinnu Yadav spoke with Akhilesh Yadav once or twice almost every day. Some reports further alleged that call records indicated Tinnu had spoken to the SP chief three times on the day before his arrest. However, there has been no official confirmation of these alleged call records or recordings. It also remains unclear why the conversations allegedly took place, what was discussed, or whether they had any connection to the alleged theft of temple donations. Earlier, after arrests were made in the donation theft case, Akhilesh had posted on X: The twig is punished, while the branch is forgiven. The remark was interpreted as suggesting that lower-level accused were being jailed while influential individuals were being protected. SP leader challenges BJP to produce evidence Former SP MLA from Ayodhya Pawan Pandey dismissed the allegations linking Tinnu Yadav to Akhilesh. He alleged that the temple donation theft had brought disrepute to the Ram Temple and blamed those associated with the Trust. Pandey challenged BJP leaders to publicly produce the Call Detail Records (CDRs) allegedly showing conversations between Akhilesh and Tinnu. He said that if such evidence was produced, he would resign from politics permanently. Otherwise, he demanded that BJP leaders stop making what he called baseless allegations against the SP chief. Akhilesh raises concerns over elections Speaking at a press conference in Lucknow earlier on Monday, Akhilesh also expressed concerns about the electoral process. Referring to allegations of vote manipulation, he remarked that there was now a fear that not only votes but even opposition candidates could be "stolen" or influenced. He urged party workers to remain vigilant and said the SP would discuss additional safeguards in future meetings. Targets BJP government on governance During the press conference, Akhilesh also launched a broader attack on the BJP government, accusing it of undermining public faith and engaging in internal power struggles. He alleged that: Comments on BJP, Uttar Pradesh politics and China Akhilesh also criticised the BJP over internal factionalism in Uttar Pradesh, claiming the party's legislators were attempting to change constituencies but asserting that the SP would instead replace them through elections. In a sarcastic remark, he described Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath as "a very good engineer," while blaming him for the design of Lucknow's ₹70-billion Green Corridor, alleging it had worsened traffic congestion. He further commented on national security, saying China had consistently posed the greatest threat to India's borders and accusing successive governments of remaining silent over repeated border incursions. The controversy over the Ram Temple donation theft investigation continues to fuel political exchanges between the BJP and the Samajwadi Party, with legal action now being threatened over allegations made on social media.

stories.title: Who is Krishna Mohan, new Ram Mandir Trust chief:Filed first donation theft FIR, joined RSS in 2012, became trustee 10 months ago
stories.summary: Just 10 months after being appointed as a trustee of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, retired IFS officer Krishna Mohan has reached the organisation’s most powerful position — the general secretary’s post. Krishna Mohan was appointed as a trustee in September 2025 following the death of Trust member Kameshwar Chaupal. After the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Lalla temple came to light, Champat Rai resigned from the post of general secretary, creating a vacancy. Krishna Mohan, who has now taken charge of the post, is the same person who filed the first FIR on behalf of the Trust in the donation theft case. A 73-year-old member of the Dalit community, Krishna Mohan served as a 1977-batch Indian Foreign Service (IFS) officer. He joined the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) in 2012 and is currently the Kshetra Sanghchalak (regional head) of eastern Uttar Pradesh. During the Ram Mandir consecration ceremony in 2024, Krishna Mohan was among the yajmans who participated in the rituals. Krishna Mohan belongs to Hardoi in Uttar Pradesh Krishna Mohan is originally from Shahabad in Hardoi district of Uttar Pradesh. His father Dharmveer Singh worked with Indian Railways and has passed away. Krishna Mohan completed his MSc in Geology from Lucknow University. He has two brothers and four sisters. His younger brother Mahendra Singh is a doctor at Balrampur Hospital in Lucknow. Krishna Mohan married Kusumlata. The couple has a son, Saurav, and a daughter, Sneha Mohan, both of whom are married. His son Saurav works with the Postal Department in Lucknow, while his daughter Sneha Mohan is a government doctor in Noida. At present, the family of his driver lives at his house in Hardoi. Worked in Atomic Energy Department before joining IFS In the early phase of his career, Krishna Mohan worked for a few years in the Department of Atomic Energy. In 1977, he was selected for the Indian Forest Service (IFS) and served in the Maharashtra cadre. His long administrative experience in the service is considered to have given him strong management skills. Joined RSS after retirement in 2012 Krishna Mohan retired from government service in 2012 and later joined the RSS. Initially, he was appointed as the Nagar Sanghchalak of Hardoi. Later, he handled several responsibilities including: He is considered to have a strong image of being an honest and trusted person among the RSS leadership, BJP leaders and senior officials connected with the Trust. This credibility is believed to have helped him rise quickly to a key position. Why the general secretary post is considered the most powerful in Ram Mandir Trust In the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, the general secretary functions like the chief executive officer of the organisation. The post carries responsibility for almost every major operational aspect, including: Krishna Mohan faces challenge of restoring devotees’ trust After being appointed as acting general secretary, Krishna Mohan said that those accused in the donation theft case would be punished. He said the accused had taken advantage of management shortcomings and that these weaknesses would be removed to prevent such incidents in the future. He added that there was a sense of distrust among people and that efforts would be made to restore confidence. His statement highlights the biggest challenge before him — rebuilding trust after the controversy. However, he also faces several other responsibilities. Completing pending construction work The main structure of the Ram Mandir is ready, but several parts of the complex, including the museum, research centre, visitor facility centre, auditorium and other projects, are still under construction. Ensuring quality and completing these works within the deadline will be a major responsibility. Maintaining transparency in Trust functioning The Ram Mandir Trust receives donations from across India and abroad. Maintaining transparency in donations, expenses and audits will be one of the biggest challenges. Coordination with government agencies Krishna Mohan will have to maintain constant coordination with the central government, Uttar Pradesh government, Ayodhya administration, security agencies and construction companies. Developing Ayodhya as a global religious tourism centre Along with the temple, Ayodhya is being developed as an international religious tourism destination. Managing devotee experience, facilities and long-term plans of the Trust will remain a key focus area. Ensuring smooth leadership transition Champat Rai remained the public face of the Trust for a long period. Maintaining continuity after his departure and ensuring coordination among trustees will be another important challenge. Handling public and media scrutiny The Ram Mandir is one of the country’s most watched religious sites. Every decision of the Trust will remain under public and media scrutiny, making transparent and balanced functioning essential.

stories.title: Debt-ridden sweet shop owner jumps before train:Body dismembered; had borrowed ₹2 crore
stories.summary: A sweet shop owner allegedly died by suicide after jumping in front of the Farakka Express in Barabanki on Monday morning, reportedly due to a debt of ₹2 crore. The train dragged him for nearly 300 metres at around 9:30 am, leaving his body dismembered near the Banwa railway crossing, with his clothes completely torn. Police and Government Railway Police (GRP) reached the scene and sent the body for post-mortem. A motorbike (UP-41AY-2426) recovered from the spot was found to be registered in the name of the victim's neighbour, Himanshu Rastogi. The incident took place in the Jahangirabad police station area. See 3 pictures Complete matter in detail Anoop Gupta (40) was considered a big businessman in Barabanki. He owned a sweet shop named Krishna Sweets. His shop, located at the big intersection, was quite famous throughout the city. He lived with his wife Nidhi, daughter Bhavya (20), and son Manan (9). Anoop Gupta left home on Monday morning to drop his son at school. For this, he borrowed his neighbor Himanshu Rastogi's bike. After dropping his son at school, he did not return home. Around 9:30 AM, he committed suicide by jumping in front of the Farakka Express (number-15744) near the Banwa railway crossing. According to gateman Dharmendra and eyewitnesses, a young man arrived at the crossing on a bike. He parked the bike aside and stood near the tracks before the train arrived. As soon as the Farakka Express approached, he was hit by the train. The train was moving at high speed, so the young man was dragged for 300 meters. The body was torn into pieces. Daughter is state merit holder Anoop's daughter, Bhavya Gupta, secured the 18th position in the state's toppers list in the Intermediate examination. She is currently pursuing B.Tech from a university in Lucknow. Upon hearing the news of the incident, a large number of traders, relatives, people from social organisations, and family members reached the post-mortem house. Brother said - he was worried about his business Anoop's brother, Rajiv Gupta, said, In the morning, my brother went to drop his son at school, but did not return. Later, it was found that he had committed suicide by jumping in front of a train. He had been somewhat worried about his business these days. But, we never thought he would take such a big step. Rajiv Tandon, a close businessman of Anoop Gupta, said, Earlier Anoop used to run a grocery business. At that time, he had taken about two crore rupees on interest from moneylenders. With this money, about 6 months ago, he opened a sweet shop named Krishna Sweets at Bada Chauraha (Big Square). The shop was doing well. But, he used to say that the expenses were too high.Meanwhile, the moneylenders were demanding their money and interest back. Anoop was very troubled by this. He had told me these things many times. We used to explain to him that everything would be alright. Troubled by this, he jumped in front of a train today and took his own life. Meanwhile, Jahangirabad police say, The investigation of the case is being conducted with complete impartiality. The police are investigating the entire incident based on the post-mortem report, evidence collected from the crime scene, statements of eyewitnesses, and questioning of family members.

stories.title: 'Stepfather called me to maternal home to rape me':Daughter tells police; accused dies of heart attack at station
stories.summary: A man accused of raping his stepdaughter died during police questioning at Sidhauli police station in Shahjahanpur on Sunday night. The woman alleged that her stepfather had sexually assaulted her for the past three years, claiming he would even call her from her maternal home to rape her. Police said the accused's health deteriorated during questioning. He was taken to a Community Health Centre and later referred to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The post-mortem report stated that he died of a heart attack. The death has raised questions over police action. The accused's family alleged he died at 1:40 am, while the FIR against him was registered at 2:19 am. Earlier on Sunday, the woman and her husband had filed a complaint at the police station. Police called the accused for questioning at around 3 pm, and he arrived with his wife. After an argument between the two sides, everyone else left, while the accused was detained for questioning. Questions on police FIR Around 1 am, the accused's health suddenly deteriorated. Police immediately took him to CHC Sidhauli, from where he was referred to the district hospital. Doctors at the district hospital declared him dead at 1:40 am. However, the FIR registered by the police states the time as 2:19 am. This raises the question of whether the FIR was written after the accused's death at night, following a complaint in the afternoon. Brother demands justice The deceased's brother has accused his niece and son-in-law of falsely implicating his brother. The brother says, We lived in the same house. My brother was very straightforward. He cannot do such a thing. We received this information at 1 am. When we reached the police station, my brother was not there. Upon going to the hospital, we found his body. Our family wants justice at any cost. Mother said that Daughter-son-in-law framed my husband The deceased's wife has also accused her daughter, son-in-law, and a middleman who arranged her daughter's marriage, of framing her husband. She said, After the daughter's allegations, the police took my husband to the police station. We left him at the police station and came home, but he died the same night. When the police took us back at night, my husband had already passed away. The CHC doctor said, Policemen brought a patient at night. His blood pressure had risen sharply to 210. The oxygen level was also not good. Considering it a case related to heart disease, the patient was referred to the district hospital for better treatment and ECG. SP Saurabh Dixit said, The FIR was registered at 12 o'clock. It takes some time for the FIR to be uploaded online. That's why there is a difference in time.

stories.title: 'Wife fights with me constantly':Man dies by suicide after recording video; says she should get nothing after his death
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, a truck owner, Arvind Tiwari (38), died by suicide by hanging himself at 1:30 am on Sunday. Before this, Arvind made a video. He forwarded it to his relatives on mobile. In the 49-second video, he accused his wife, father-in-law, and brother-in-law of fighting and quarreling. In the video, Arvind said, After I die, I want my wife to get nothing. Her father and brother, everyone fights with me. They don't make their daughter understand. They see flaws in me. I do everything. I give everything. Still, they say - what do you do? I tolerate it. My capacity to tolerate is very low. Therefore, there is no hope of living now. I want to die. Arvind also posted the video on social media around 1 am. After that, he tied a noose to a protruding rod from the roof of the house next door and took his own life. Around 2 am, when Arvind's mother came out, she saw her son's body hanging. She screamed. Hearing the noise, family members and people from the surrounding area gathered at the spot. They informed the police. The police brought the body down. Sent it for post-mortem. Questioned family members and neighbors. The case belongs to the Ghurpur police station area. Full incident details Arvind lives with his family in his ancestral house in Iradatganj. His father, Dayashankar Tiwari, has passed away. He used to run the family by driving a truck. After his death, Arvind continued the work. Arvind married Richa (34) 4 years ago. They have two children, an elder daughter aged 2 and a son aged 5 months. When his business went well, Arvind bought 2 trucks. Arvind himself drove one truck. Police said, Arvind lived at home with his mother, Shyama Devi (68), 3 brothers, wife Richa, and 2 children. On Sunday night at 12 o'clock, he had an argument with his wife Richa over something.He left the house in anger. He went outside and made a video at 1 am. He posted it on social media. He also sent it to his relatives. Then he made a noose out of a towel and committed suicide. ‘He used to help his brother, daughter-in-law did not like this’ At 2 am, mother Shyama Devi suddenly woke up. She got up, came out of the house, and saw her son Arvind hanging from a noose. Shyama Devi told the police that her daughter-in-law, Richa, used to fight with her son every day. He used to help his three brothers financially. All three brothers drive other people's trucks. Arvind wanted to give them his truck. Richa did not like this. Richa's father and brothers also used to trouble Arvind. For the past four days, Arvind was very disturbed. Wife says allegations are false Arvind's wife Richa, has denied the allegations. She said that minor arguments used to happen at home. The talk of harassment is wrong. The house is small. There is only one bathroom. Her husband's elder brothers use it. She used to object if it got late, which made them angry. There was also a slight argument at night. She thought he had left in anger and would return. But, his body was found. Ghurpur Police Station in-charge Atul Kumar Mishra said- The young man's mobile phone has been seized. The matter is being investigated. No complaint letter has been received so far. Further legal action will be taken after investigation into every aspect.

stories.title: DDU speeds up recruitment promotions:Ravi Kishan appointed professor of practice; 156 faculty elevated
stories.summary: Under the leadership of Vice-Chancellor Prof. Poonam Tandon, Deendayal Upadhyay Gorakhpur University has accelerated the filling of vacant posts and staff promotions through a transparent, impartial, and time-bound process aimed at improving education, research, and administration. Since the 2023–24 academic session, 156 faculty members have been promoted under the Career Advancement Scheme (CAS), including 42 Senior Professors, 6 Professors, 1 Associate Professor and 107 Assistant Professors. During the same period, the university also recruited 109 new faculty members- 27 permanent teachers (11 Assistant Professors, 10 Associate Professors, and 6 Professors) and 82 contractual Assistant Professors. The information was shared in a DDU Media Cell press release issued at 10:30 am on Monday. Students to gain practical knowledge from experts To provide students with practical and industry understanding alongside theoretical knowledge, the university has taken a new initiative by appointing three experienced experts as 'Professors of Practice'. Under this, Gorakhpur MP Ravi Kishan Shukla has been given responsibility in the Department of Fine Arts and Music, while renowned industrialists C.P. Agarwal and Atul Sarraf have been given responsibility in the Department of Commerce. Jobs for 14 employees In addition to teachers, the university administration has also made appointments to non-academic positions. Since September 4, 2023, 14 people have been given jobs under the compassionate appointment quota in various positions such as Junior Assistant and Attendant. Vice-Chancellor expressed confidence Vice-Chancellor Prof. Poonam Tandon said that having the right staff is most important for good education and better administration. She expressed confidence that with these new appointments, promotions, and the joining of experts, DDU will achieve new milestones at national and international levels under the New Education Policy.

stories.title: 80-year-old woman dies 35 days after being raped:Accused entered victim's home to commit assault when she was alone
stories.summary: An 80-year-old woman in Uttar Pradesh’s Hathras district has died after being hospitalised for 35 days following an alleged case of sexual assault. The woman, who had been undergoing treatment since the incident, died around 12:30 am on Sunday night during treatment. According to police, a 35-year-old man named Salman allegedly entered her home on the night of May 31 and assaulted her after finding her alone. He then fled the scene, leaving her unconscious. The incident came to light the next morning when neighbours found her house door open. She was discovered in a seriously injured condition and was later admitted to a district hospital before being referred to a medical college. Although there was some improvement in her condition, she was later shifted back to the district hospital, where she eventually passed away. Police had arrested the accused shortly after the incident and registered a case under relevant sections following a complaint lodged by a neighbour. A medical examination had confirmed the assault. Officials said the post-mortem examination of the body will be conducted, and further legal sections will be added to the case based on the report.
