stories.title: VIDEO | SI manhandled by truck driver:Claims policeman stole ₹20,000 from his truck while taking lift
stories.summary: A truck driver allegedly thrashed a sub-inspector in Hamirpur in broad daylight on Monday around 9:30 am after accusing the police official of stealing ₹20,000 from the truck's cabin. According to the driver, the incident began on NH-34 when the officer reportedly took a lift in the truck near Ghazipur (Ghata Khand area). Near the Aliyapur toll plaza under Sajeeti police station limits, the sub-inspector allegedly took ₹20,000 from the truck cabin and fled in a van. The driver pursued him for nearly 13 kilometres and eventually caught up with him near the Yamuna bridge. He then grabbed the officer by the collar and allegedly assaulted him repeatedly on the highway. In the video that has surfaced, the driver is seen delivering multiple slaps within seconds, while the officer’s uniform is torn during the scuffle. The driver further claimed that when he pulled the officer’s uniform, the allegedly hidden cash fell out. Following the incident, the sub-inspector, identified as Girish Mishra, posted in court security duty in Hamirpur, has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been ordered by the Superintendent of Police. An FIR has also been registered against him at Sajeeti police station on the complaint filed by the driver. Details of the case According to truck driver Manish, he was returning after selling gravel when he picked up sub-inspector Girish Mishra near Ghata Khand area of NH-34, mistaking him for a regular passenger. The journey remained normal until the vehicle reached near the Aliyapur toll plaza under Sajeeti police station limits, where the driver claimed he discovered ₹20,000 missing from the cabin. The driver alleged that the officer had concealed the cash inside his uniform and, when confronted, got down from the truck and fled in a van. Manish said he did not give up and chased the vehicle for nearly 13 kilometres. After crossing the Yamuna bridge, the officer reportedly got off the van and started walking, where the driver finally caught him. On searching him, the driver claimed the missing ₹20,000 was recovered, following which he lost his temper and slapped the officer two to three times on the roadside. A large crowd gathered on the highway after seeing a uniformed police officer being assaulted. Locals intervened and informed emergency police response service UP-112. The officer was taken to the local police station. A video of the incident was also recorded and later went viral on social media. Circle Officer Yashpal Singh said that based on the viral video and complaint, a case has been registered at Kotwali Nagar under relevant sections. The sub-inspector has been suspended with immediate effect, and a departmental inquiry has been ordered. Further action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation.

stories.title: Truck rams 2 traffic constables, one dead:Erring truck driver dies while trying to escape from the scene
stories.summary: In Kanpur, on the Barra Elevated Road, at 4 AM on Monday, two traffic constables on duty were crushed by a truck. One constable died on the spot. The other is seriously injured. After the accident, in an attempt to flee, the erring truck driver tried to drive away but he lost control and crashed into a container truck moving ahead. In this, the truck driver also died. The collision was so severe that the truck's cabin was crushed. The driver's body got stuck in the cabin. The body was removed by cutting the cabin. The deceased Jitendra was a constable of the 2018 batch. He was originally from Agra. While constable Rakesh Kumar is injured. He has been admitted to Kashiram Hospital. Rakesh is originally from Bulandshahr. The truck driver has not been identified. Constables were going to clear a traffic jam when accident occurred According to the police, both constables Rakesh and Jitendra were on duty at Naubasta Bypass. Information was received that there was a traffic jam on the elevated road. Both left on a bike from Naubasta towards Barra Elevated Corridor. As they reached the elevated road, suddenly a speeding truck hit their bike. As soon as they were hit, both constables fell to the ground. The container crushed Jitendra and moved forward. After the accident, the truck driver panicked. He started speeding the truck on the elevated road itself. A little further ahead, he crashed into a container. He died in it. Elevated Road remained jammed for 2 hours As soon as the news of the constable's death in the accident was received, Additional Commissioner of Police (Law and Order) Dr. Vipin Tada and DCP Traffic Ravindra Kumar reached the spot. They inspected the accident site. Information was gathered regarding the causes of the incident. After the accident, traffic remained jammed on the elevated road for about 2 hours. See 3 pictures of the accident... Constable Jitendra Kumar's brother Khyali Ram said - I run a salon in Agra. Brother Jitendra's marriage took place on December 2, 2020, with Varsha, daughter of Kailashchandra, a resident of Etawah, who was posted in PAC. They have a two-and-a-half-year-old daughter, Bhumika. Father Veerdharam used to do labour work. The family includes mother Phoolwati and five sisters. The sisters are already married. Jitendra's brother-in-law Keshav said the information about the accident was given by a traffic constable living near the village. Jitendra was living in a rented house in Nirala Nagar with his wife and daughter since his marriage.

stories.title: Wife allegedly dies by suicide after husband cancels flight ticket:Dowry murder case registered against 5; husband in custody
stories.summary: The death of a newly married woman in Lucknow has led to a dowry murder case against her husband and five members of his family. The victim, Sonali, had been married for just four months and was found dead under suspicious circumstances at the couple's rented flat in Shivajipuram, Indiranagar. According to police, Sonali and her husband, Kamalakant, originally planned to travel to Kashmir by flight. However, Kamalakant, a deputy manager at a private bank, cancelled the flight tickets and booked train tickets instead. The change reportedly upset Sonali, leading to an argument between the couple. Although the dispute later subsided, Kamalakant left for work as usual. When he called his wife from work, she did not answer. He then asked the landlord to check on her. The landlord found the flat locked from inside and discovered Sonali hanging. She was later declared dead. Sonali was a resident of Kharharad Simri in Bihar's Buxar district, while Kamalakant belongs to Pinjaroi village in the Sandesh area of Bhojpur district. The couple had married in February this year and had been living in Lucknow. Following a complaint by Sonali's family, police registered a case of dowry murder against Kamalakant and five members of his family. The husband has been taken into custody for questioning. Sonali's brother, Abhishek Ojha, alleged that the husband murdered his sister and that her in-laws, including her mother-in-law, father-in-law, elder brother-in-law, elder brother-in-law's wife and sister-in-law, had been mentally harassing her over dowry demands. He further alleged that Kamalakant photographed Sonali's body to make the death appear to be a case of suicide. Husband says, ‘He sent train ticket on WhatsApp before calling’ During police questioning, Kamalakant said that due to work commitments, he and his wife had not been able to go on a honeymoon after their marriage. A month ago, they planned a trip to Kashmir and booked flight tickets. Sonali arrived in Lucknow on 28 June. On Friday, he cancelled the flight tickets and booked train tickets instead. Sonali became upset, leading to an argument between them. On Saturday, he went to work as usual. From there, he sent the train ticket to his wife via WhatsApp. He said that when he later called her, she did not answer. After several unsuccessful attempts, he asked the landlord to check on her. The landlord found the door locked from inside. Kamalakant then rushed home and found Sonali hanging inside the room. Family arrives from Bihar, FIR registered On Sunday, Sonali's family arrived in Lucknow from Bihar. Based on their complaint, police registered a case of dowry murder against the husband and five members of his family. The family alleged that Sonali was repeatedly harassed over demands for a car and cash. They claimed she had come to Lucknow on 28 June to stay with her husband and that he killed her on 4 July before trying to present it as a suicide. They also alleged that he took photographs with the body before informing the family. The victim's family submitted the photographs to the police, alleging that instead of taking Sonali to hospital immediately, the husband first posed for photographs with her body. Brother alleges harassment over dowry demands Abhishek said that on Saturday night, his brother-in-law called to inform him that Sonali had died by suicide and had been taken to hospital, where doctors declared her dead. He alleged that ever since the marriage, the husband and his family had been demanding a car and cash. According to him, Sonali was continuously insulted and mentally harassed by her husband Kamalakant, mother-in-law Ramawati, father-in-law Shardanand, sister-in-law Girija Choubey, elder brother-in-law Laxmikant and elder brother-in-law's wife Laxmi. Family says, ‘₹15 lakh cash and furniture worth ₹2.5 lakh were given at marriage’ In his complaint at Indiranagar police station, Abhishek stated that the bride's family had spent lavishly on the wedding. They gave ₹15 lakh in cash and furniture worth around ₹2.5 lakh. Despite this, he alleged, the husband's family continued to harass Sonali and repeatedly demanded a car. Dowry murder case registered; husband in custody Based on the complaint, Indiranagar police registered a case of dowry murder and other relevant offences against the husband and five members of his family. Police have detained the husband for questioning. Senior officers said the post-mortem report lists the cause of death as hanging. They added that the investigation is continuing on the basis of other available evidence.

stories.title: Man kills girlfriend for refusing to show WhatsApp chats:Body dismembered; accused arrested after police encounter
stories.summary: In Jaunpur, a young man murdered his married girlfriend on Saturday by slitting her throat for not showing her WhatsApp chat. He cut the body into three pieces with a billhook. He severed both hands and both legs. He filled the hands and torso in black polythene bags and threw them in bushes along the roadside at different locations. On Sunday morning at 6 AM, people out for a walk became suspicious due to a foul smell. When they went closer, they saw polythene bags. Upon receiving information, the police arrived and opened the polythene bags, finding the woman's torso. When they started searching for the remaining parts, hands were found one kilometre away. 3 teams were formed to search for the remaining parts of the body. The entire area was cordoned off. Meanwhile, late on Sunday night, an informant reported that a person was carrying similar black polythene bags on a bike. Around 12:30 AM, the police surrounded him. Fearing capture, the accused opened fire. In retaliatory action, the accused was shot in his right leg. He fell on the road. Police arrested him and took him to the hospital. The woman's leg, the axe used in the crime, and a pistol were recovered from him. During interrogation, he confessed to the crime. The woman was identified as Reshma Khatoon alias Sana (38) from Varanasi. Her husband has identified the body. The incident took place 25 km from the district headquarters in the Madiyahun Kotwali area. Understand the entire case in a sequential manner- Woman's legs, mobile recovered from accused Police recovered a knife, a cleaver, a .32 bore pistol, cartridges, the woman's severed legs, a bike, and the woman's mobile phone used in the crime from the accused. A case has been registered against him under various sections including murder, destruction of evidence, deadly assault on police, and illegal possession of weapons, and further legal action has been initiated. Woman has three children, family lives in Varanasi The accused told the police that Sana was married. She has three children. The eldest son is 20 years old. The two daughters are 19 and 14 years old. She was married to Rahim Khan, a resident of Kewalipur, Varanasi. CO Vijay Chaudhary said- Accused Dilip has been arrested. He had an argument with the woman, after which this incident occurred. The woman's husband, Rahim Khan, has identified her. The body has been handed over after post-mortem. Rahim will also be interrogated.

stories.title: UP's Jalalabad to be renamed Parashurampuri:Yogi cabinet approves name change after Centre's nod
stories.summary: A Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was held in Lucknow at 10 am on Monday. The Cabinet approved 28 proposals, including the renaming of Jalalabad in Shahjahanpur district to Parashurampuri. Cabinet Minister Suresh Khanna said Jalalabad is believed to be the birthplace of Lord Parashuram. The Uttar Pradesh government had sent the proposal to the Central Government on 25 June, 2025. After receiving a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Centre, the Cabinet approved the name change. Another major proposal provides cashless medical treatment of up to ₹5 lakh for Uttar Pradesh Home Guards and their families. The state currently has 1.18 lakh Home Guards. In addition, the recruitment process for 41,000 Home Guards has been completed. As a result, more than 1.60 lakh Home Guards and their family members will benefit from the scheme. The cabinet also approved the establishment of an ESIC Medical College in Varanasi. Fifty per cent of the seats at the medical college will be reserved for the children of workers. Details of cabinet decisions: 1. Uttar Pradesh startup mission directorate to be established The Yogi Cabinet approved the establishment of the Uttar Pradesh Startup Mission Directorate, the UP Startup Policy-2026, and the Data Centre Policy. The Chief Secretary will head the Mission Directorate. An Empowerment Committee will also be formed. A Startup Fund of ₹1,000 crore has been created, including ₹400 crore from AKTU. 2. Livestock insurance scheme approved for animal rearers The Cabinet approved the Chief Minister Risk Management and Livestock Insurance Scheme for livestock owners across all 75 districts of the state. Under the scheme, the state government will bear 85% of the insurance premium, while livestock owners will contribute 15%. Cabinet Minister Dharampal Singh said the scheme will reduce the financial burden on farmers and livestock owners. The insurable value of livestock has been fixed as follows: The minister said there are currently around 1.35 lakh cattle in government cow shelters across the state, with nearly ₹8 crore being spent daily on their upkeep. The insurance premium will be shared as follows: Insurance benefits will be available if an animal dies due to natural disasters, disease, or accidents. 3. ESIC hospitals for workers in Gorakhpur and Moradabad The Cabinet approved the construction of 100-bed ESIC hospitals for workers in Gorakhpur and Moradabad. It also approved free land allocation for establishing an ESIC Medical College in Varanasi. Cabinet Minister Anil Rajbhar said five acres of land each have been allotted for the hospitals in Gorakhpur and Moradabad. The medical college in Varanasi will be built on 13 acres of land. Half of the seats at the medical college will be reserved for workers' children. Out of 50 seats, 25 will be reserved for them. 4. Direct government recruitment for international medal winners The Cabinet approved amendments to the Direct Recruitment Rules-2022 for international medal-winning athletes. The state government will now be able to appoint international medal winners directly without requiring them to undergo the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) selection process. Cabinet Minister Girish Yadav said the provision applies to medal winners at the Olympics, Women's Olympics, Asian Games and other international sporting events. The policy will apply to Group 'A' and Group 'B' government posts. Direct recruitment will be made for: Bronze and silver medal-winning athletes will be eligible for appointment. 5. First private agriculture university to come up in Kanpur The Cabinet approved the establishment of three private universities in Uttar Pradesh: The Cabinet also approved the allocation of 20 hectares of land and ₹50 crore for establishing a Horticulture College and Research Centre in Raebareli. stories.title: Ruchi Veera on BJP defection buzz:'Show the evidence'; says Kamal Akhtar should follow Akhilesh's order
stories.summary: The conflict between SP MP from Moradabad, Ruchi Veera, and SP MLA from Kanth, Kamal Akhtar, is in the headlines. To end this dispute, SP President Akhilesh Yadav stripped Akhtar of the post of Chief Whip of the legislative party. Despite this, the matter does not seem to be cooling down. Meanwhile, news of Ruchi Veera joining the BJP has spread rapidly. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Veera on speculations of her joining BJP. She said, “If anyone has any proof, present it. My ideology never aligns with BJP. I am a soldier of SP, and will remain with the SP until my last breath.” On the conflict with Kamal Akhtar, Ruchi Veera said, “They (Kamal Akhtar and his supporters) should heed the message Akhilesh-ji has given them.” Veera answered candidly on questions ranging from factionalism in SP to efforts for former MP Azam Khan's release. Read the full interview Question- What is the real reason for the conflict between you and Kamal Akhtar? Answer- There is no question of conflict. I am an MP and he is an MLA. I don't have to contest the MLA election, so there won't be any conflict. That episode is now over. There are many people in the party, so there can be differences, but there is nothing significant like that. Question- Akhilesh had reconciled you and Kamal Akhtar, but the situation hasn't changed? Answer- If there is any issue, we should inform our leader. Every party has minor issues. I have no personal conflict with him. Nor is there any conflict over land, property, or business. With (state) elections approaching, we should keep meeting the leader. If anyone is still making statements, it is wrong. When the episode was closed and the national president resolved it, there should be no more statements. Question- Kamal Akhtar even helped you contest elections. Your relations were good, so why such a conflict? Answer- I am a loyal soldier of the SP. Including me in any programme will only add some votes. I don't think this was such a big issue. The BJP has blown it out of proportion through the media. Appearing in a photo at an event, or having my photo on a poster or not, is not a big deal for me. I live in people's hearts. I don't need to be on posters. Question- It is being said that you want to field your daughter from the Moradabad Nagar seat, which is why there was a conflict? Answer- Let anyone in Moradabad tell me if I ever said that I want to field my daughter from here. This could be misinformation. This could also be a BJP plan. I have said before that my daughter never had, nor will ever have, any intention of contesting elections from Moradabad district. Question- It is being said that you are in contact with BJP and might join BJP? Answer- Let anyone provide such proof... My ideology does not align with the BJP. My father-in-law has been a MLA three times and a minister. I have a secular mindset. Yes, some small-time people are writing that guidelines have come from the center for 37 Samajwadi Party MPs. I want to tell these people to at least leave the family members and loyal people alone. Neither am I in touch with anyone, nor can anyone prove it. BJP and BJP MLAs are scared of my popularity. The way I stay among people in every joy and sorrow, because of that, I have become a challenge for BJP MLAs. Question- By making your photo with the Speaker viral, it is being said that you are joining BJP. Answer- Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla ji had come to Moradabad last year. It is my responsibility that if the Speaker of my house has come to my constituency, I should at least welcome him with a bouquet. This is both my responsibility and my right. As a local MP, I had welcomed the Speaker. This picture is from that time. In politics, this courtesy is a common thing. Question- You had talked about sidelining a woman MP in the party, are you not given time? Answer- Whenever I ask for time, I get time from the party leadership. It might be a day or two earlier or later. He (Akhilesh) is a former Chief Minister and a future Chief Minister. He has a busy schedule, but my leader also gives me time and listens to me. Question- Who will benefit from the conflict between you and Kamal Akhtar? Answer- BJP wants to capitalize on this. The strength with which SP is entering the election arena has disturbed BJP's sleep. In the last general election, SP won 37 seats in UP. We are people who struggle. SP is a struggling party. There is no sabotage here. BJP should not dream Mungerilal's beautiful dreams. Everyone will unite to defeat BJP and make Akhilesh Yadav the Chief Minister of UP again. Question- Azam Khan is your political guru. What efforts did you make for his release after becoming an MP? Answer- Whatever is happening with Azam Sahab, it has not happened with any leader in independent India. He is a very big secular leader. Azam Sahab has dedicated his entire life to SP. Everyone has benefited from the university he built. He is being targeted. He is not a criminal. I and all SP leaders want Azam Sahab to come out and guide us in the elections. But, the government has decided not to let him out. Fighting with the government is difficult, but we are confident that justice will surely be served one day. Question- Is SP moving towards soft Hindutva? Answer- The first thing is that whether it's Akhilesh Yadav's family or us, we all are followers of Sanatan Dharma and Shankaracharya ji. The position of Shankaracharya has always been respected. Even in the past, if a king was wrong, Shankaracharya would instruct him and work on correction. But, the government is now not ready to accept his correct words. All of us and our party's leader are followers of Sanatan. What's new in this, they have always been revered. Question- What message do you want to give to Kamal Akhtar? Answer- Who am I to give a message? The message has been given by the National President ji, follow that. I would only say that we have to fight against BJP. We don't have to fight among ourselves. It's possible that some people's mutual views don't align or we have our own ambitions, but the party is supreme for us. If the government is formed and Akhilesh becomes the Chief Minister, then the strength of all of us will increase. In such a situation, we will be able to serve people with more strength. Question- What do you have to say about the theft of offerings at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya? Answer- It is a great misfortune for the country. It is an attack on the faith of people of Sanatan Dharma. First, these people benefited from Ram's name, and now they are stealing Ram's donations. This is a big robbery. The government should resign. You are playing with people's faith by stealing from the temple of the very deity because of whom you are in power. An investigation should be conducted by forming a committee of a sitting judge. Justice cannot be expected from a Special Investigation Team (SIT) in this matter. Now understand why the dispute between the MP and the MLA occurred? Actually, SP MP Ruchiveera is upset about not being invited to the 'PDA conference'. She believes that MLA Kamal Akhtar was behind this. However, Kamal Akhtar says that he worked hard for Ruchiveera in the Lok Sabha elections, considering her as his sister. The PDA conference, to which she claims not to have been invited, took place on the occasion of Amjad Pathan being made the Metropolitan Vice President. The event was organized on June 14 by Rajya Sabha MP Javed Ali in the Moradabad Rural assembly constituency. Find out next, what happened in the Lucknow meeting MP-MLA clashed in front of Akhilesh According to sources, there was a heated argument between MP Ruchi Veera and Kamal Akhtar in front of Akhilesh Yadav during the meeting. Ruchi Veera alleged that she was not invited to party programs and her photo was not put on posters. Meanwhile, Kamal Akhtar alleged that he was not invited to the Mushaira and Azam Khan's birthday program organized by Ruchi Veera. There was also a lot of debate regarding another person, Khushnood, who was present at the meeting with Akhilesh. Khushnood, present at the meeting, was speaking in favor of Ruchi Veera. Kamal Akhtar objected to this and said - Javed Ali is an MP, Madam is also an MP, I am an MLA, is Jaiveer the district president? Who is this? What is his work here? On this, Ruchi Veera said- This is Khushnood and he has come with me. Then Kamal Akhtar said- We also have many people outside with us, should I call them too? As the dispute escalated, Akhilesh Yadav stopped Kamal Akhtar and Ruchi Veera and asked Khushnood where he was from? Khushnood said that he was from Bijnor. Then Akhilesh said that when I call the people of Bijnor, then you speak. After this, Ruchi Veera also asked Khushnood to remain silent.

stories.title: Farmer ID now mandatory in UP:No fertiliser or seeds without it; know how to apply online via mobile
stories.summary: The UP government is preparing a 12-digit unique ID for farmers, calling it 'Farmer ID' or 'Kisan Registry'. The ID will record information related to farmers' land and the amount of farming being done on it. This ID will be mandatory to procure fertiliser, seeds and even to avail government schemes like PM Kisan Samman Nidhi, crop insurance, Kisan Credit Card, and loan waiver. The government claims that this will ensure that the benefits of schemes reach needy farmers and fraudulent practices are stopped. Complete farm data in Farmer ID Farmer ID is a digital database, in which the farmer's name, Khasra-Khatauni (essential land record documents) data, and information about the crop sown in the field will be digitally recorded. After the Farmer ID is created, when a farmer goes to get fertiliser, the Farmer ID will be scanned. This will let the system know how much land the farmer has. How many bags of fertilizer he needs. This will ensure that eligible farmers receive the correct amount of fertilizer. It is often observed that when there is a shortage of fertiliser, black marketing begins. Some people hoard stocks of urea or DAP. In such a situation, the Farmer ID will curb black marketing. Registered farmers will receive benefits of PM Kisan Samman Nidhi According to the UP government, farmer IDs have been created for about 75 per cent of the state's farmers. This means that out of 2.4 crore farmers, the digital registration work for over 1.8 crore has been completed. A special campaign is being run to connect the remaining farmers. After this, the Agriculture Department will make the Farmer ID mandatory in schemes related to fertilisers, seeds, pesticides, and other agricultural materials. The selection of beneficiaries for the schemes will also be done based on the Farmer ID database. In the future, installments of PM Kisan Samman Nidhi will also be given only to those farmers who have a Farmer ID. It has also been decided to make Farmer ID mandatory in schemes of Horticulture, Animal Husbandry, Fisheries, Cooperatives, and Sugarcane Development departments. No need for repeated registration at centers Currently, farmers have to register anew every season to sell crops like paddy and wheat at government procurement centers. After the creation of the Farmer ID, this hassle will end. By entering the ID, information about the farmer and their land will appear. It takes a lot of time to get a Kisan Credit Card (KCC) due to land documents and verification. With the Farmer ID, this process will become digital, which will help in getting loans quickly. What is the last date to get a Farmer Registry made? The campaign to create Farmer Registry in UP has been ongoing since 2024. Initially, it was started as a pilot project, but in 2025 and 2026, it was run in mission mode. The government first set its last date as April 30, then extended it to May 15, 2026. Currently, registration is ongoing and a new last date has not yet been decided. However, from June 1, 2026, Farmer Registry has been made mandatory for government agricultural schemes. Contact here for help or complaints If there is an error in the name, Khasra number, or land record in the Khatauni, there may be problems in creating the Farmer ID. Therefore, the revenue records will have to be updated first. If a farmer wants to register a complaint related to any agricultural scheme, including PM Kisan, they can contact the government helpline 0522-2317003 or the toll-free Kisan Call Center 1800-180-1551. For complaints, the Chief Minister's helpline 1076 can also be contacted. 5 Important Questions Related to Farmer ID Question 1. Will there be any fee for this ID? Answer. No. Jan Seva Kendra (Public Service Center) may charge ₹20 to ₹50 for filling the form, uploading it to the computer, and e-KYC. Question 2. What are the rules for sharecroppers (tenants)? Answer. The Farmer ID of tenant farmers can be created after the consent of the landowner. Both will undergo digital verification. After the Farmer ID is created, tenant farmers will also be able to sell their crops at MSP. Subsidies for fertilizers and seeds, crop insurance, and compensation benefits will also be directly deposited into their bank accounts. Question 3. Can the tenant farmer misuse this? Answer. Land ownership does not change with farmer registration. The tenant farmer receives consent for only one crop season. The landowner can withdraw their consent at any time if they wish. Question 4. How will the ID be created in the case of a joint account? Answer. Even with a joint land record (khatoni), a separate Farmer ID will be created for each account holder in the family. The ID will be linked to Aadhaar and e-KYC. If the share is recorded in the land record, benefits like fertilisers, seeds, and others will be received in the same proportion. If the share is not recorded, benefits will be determined based on digital crop survey and actual cultivation. Question 5. Can Farmer ID data be used in cyber fraud? Answer. The government has arranged for encryption, a consent-based system, and secure government servers for data security. Farmers have been advised to use only official portals or apps.

stories.title: Ram Mandir Trust accepts Champat Rai's resignation:Krishna Mohan named New General Secy; trust expresses shame over theft
stories.summary: In the ongoing controversy over the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Ayodhya Ram Temple, the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has accepted the resignations of General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Anil Mishra. Retired IFS officer and trustee Krishna Mohan has been appointed as the acting General Secretary, replacing Champat Rai. The trust's first meeting after the theft lasted nearly three hours. Addressing the media afterwards, Treasurer Govind Dev Giri said, Champat Rai felt it was not appropriate to remain in office until the culprits were arrested. What happened is deeply painful. We are all saddened by it. The donation theft is a shameful incident. During the meeting, trustee K. Parasaran said the trust's constitution provides that a resignation is deemed accepted as soon as it is submitted, which is why both resignations were accepted. Krishna Mohan said those responsible for the donation theft would be brought to justice. He added that the accused had taken advantage of shortcomings in the trust's management, and those gaps would now be addressed to prevent such incidents from happening again. He also said the trust would work to restore public confidence, which had been affected by the controversy.

stories.title: Heavy rain floods Bareilly as 57 cities remain on alert:Roads flooded, e-rickshaws overturn; monsoon to strengthen from Tuesday
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh has witnessed highly variable weather since the onset of the monsoon. Intense heat has persisted during the day, with spells of rain accompanied by strong winds. Bright sunshine after showers has pushed up humidity levels. Most cities, including Lucknow, Bareilly and Kanpur, have been experiencing strong sunshine with intermittent cloud cover. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a thunderstorm and rain alert for 57 cities on Monday (6 July), along with a warning of lightning. According to the IMD, a weather system over the north-west Bay of Bengal is expected to cross the north Odisha coast by Monday evening and move towards Chhattisgarh. Its interaction with the existing western disturbance could trigger sudden heavy rainfall in parts of Uttar Pradesh, with hail also possible. The monsoon is then expected to strengthen across the state from Tuesday. At around 1 am on Sunday, Bareilly witnessed heavy rain accompanied by strong winds. Several roads were waterlogged, with flooding persisting until morning. A number of e-rickshaws overturned in the water. During the day, intermittent rain was recorded in 18 cities, including Lucknow, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Ghaziabad, Ballia and Jalaun. Lucknow and Barabanki also experienced rain accompanied by strong winds. According to the IMD, Uttar Pradesh received 67.7 mm of rainfall between 1 June and 5 July, against the normal of 125.6 mm for this period. This means the state has so far recorded 46 per cent below-normal rainfall this monsoon season. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: The weather system near the north Odisha coast has influenced weather conditions in Uttar Pradesh, causing the monsoon to weaken temporarily. Light rain is occurring in some districts due to local weather systems. Humidity and heat have increased across eastern and central Uttar Pradesh. The monsoon is expected to regain strength within the next 24 hours, after which rainfall activity will intensify across the state. Monsoon Meter Note: Data is up to 5 July 2026. Heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places. 9 July: Heavy rainfall is expected across Uttar Pradesh, accompanied by thunderstorms and the possibility of lightning. 10 July: Rain and thunderstorms are forecast across the state, with heavy rainfall likely in isolated areas. 11 July: Rain and thunderstorms are expected in western Uttar Pradesh, while eastern Uttar Pradesh is likely to receive light showers.

stories.title: Ram Mandir offering theft case:Will Champat Rai and Anil Mishra be charged with criminal conspiracy?
stories.summary: In the Ayodhya Ram Mandir offering theft case, Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust's General Secretary Champat Rai and member Dr. Anil Mishra remain outside the purview of the police investigation. In such a situation, the big question is whether these senior officials are guilty or not? According to legal experts, two charges can be levelled against them. First is concealing the crime. Second is that though they were in important positions in the trust, they were unable to detect the crime that was happening right under their nose. Trust officials were informed about the theft on 4 June 2026. On June 5, cash was recovered from the residences of some suspicious employees. On June 7, Champat Rai released a video, in which he stated that no theft had occurred. On June 25, eight people associated with the offering and cash counting process were named in the FIR. This determines that it was an attempt to conceal the crime. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to senior lawyers regarding this case. Senior lawyers of the Ayodhya Bar Association said, “Senior office bearers of the trust will come under legal scrutiny. They cannot escape”. Another senior lawyer said, ”The name of a trustee has come up in the statements of the accused. It is certain that responsibility will be fixed when new names emerge in the police charge sheet." Lawyers says senior officials will get into trouble for not informing the police Senior advocate Ashutosh Tripathi, associated with the Ayodhya District Bar Association, said, “The role of the senior office bearers of the trust is suspicious. They may come under legal scrutiny. When the information about the theft was received on 4 June itself, then who was hiding it for 20 days?” The law states that as soon as information about a crime is known, the police should be informed. The facts of the offering theft were hidden from the police. Therefore, the office bearers of the Ram Mandir Trust become accused under Section 61 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). This section deals with criminal conspiracy. A case can be registered against the trustees for involvement in the crime. 'Trustees are seemingly guilty of criminal breach of trust' Ayodhya's senior lawyer Kalika Mishra says- The responsibility for the security of offerings in the trust lay with the office bearers. It has come to light that the theft came to their knowledge. Yet they did not take the right steps. Section 316 of BNS (Criminal Breach of Trust) states that if a person, who has property entrusted to them, misappropriates it or allows someone to steal it, then they are guilty of criminal breach of trust. This can lead to a sentence of up to 10 years. Police officers investigating without authority will also be implicated Upon receiving information about the theft of offerings, some police personnel deployed for the security of Karsevakpuram or Ram Mandir violated the Right to Duty and Service Rules. They, without any FIR or search warrant, acting as 'third parties', started searching for items at the suspects' homes. Such police personnel can be suspended under the 'Right to Service'. The senior officers of the department should have submitted a written report on this. It should also be investigated under whose pressure they conducted such an investigation beyond their authority. Accused may get 'benefit of doubt' Ayodhya lawyers believe that the trust's attempt to suppress the case and recover money from the homes of various suspects without any authority could weaken the entire case in court. 1. Police will get stuck during testimony- When testimony takes place in court and the investigating officer or the case's sub-inspector is asked, 'Did you recover this money?' and he denies, 'No... a certain person brought it.' Then the question will arise as to by what authority that money was taken? 2. Accused will get the benefit of doubt- Due to non-compliance with the process and a delay of 20 days, the accused may legally get the 'benefit of doubt', which could lead to their acquittal. Should statements of Dhirendra Shastri and Brijbhushan Singh also be recorded? Senior advocate Ashutosh Tripathi said, “Whispers of theft have been circulating since the land fraud came to light, suggesting something was amiss within the temple and trust.” Recently, statements from two prominent figures of the country on this matter - Dhirendra Krishna Shastri (Bageshwar Dham) and Brijbhushan Sharan Singh - have emerged. Both hinted This is a very big matter, I will not take names. Whoever stole Lord Ram's money, they will finish me off too. This raised the question of who is such an influential person, whose fear is so great? The SIT and the investigating officer should take cognisance of these two major statements and issue summons to them. They should be questioned about what information or evidence they have, which they are refraining from stating on an open platform. Lawyer says, ‘If Champat becomes an accused, he will justify himself’ Former Additional Advocate General of Lucknow, Raghavendra Pratap Singh, has a slightly different perspective. He believes that it is difficult for the heat to reach senior officials, because the matter is not of dishonesty but of 'betrayal'. He said, “In this matter, some corrupt people got close to Champat Rai. This is a direct 'betrayal' of 20 years of trust. When someone of your own betrays you, what can a person do? As for the delay, usually when a servant steals in the house, the owner first tries to interrogate and recover the goods himself, and only later goes to the police.” Know the Legal Hurdles in the Case Role of Trust officials not clear The accused include Champat Rai's driver (Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu), the General Secretary of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, and contractual employees associated with the counting room. The counting room and keys were with them. So far, only junior employees have been caught. Until the 'banking and security failure' that occurred under the supervision of senior trust officials is added to the FIR or charge sheet, the accused can avoid major charges by portraying it merely as departmental negligence. Digital evidence is very important in this case So far, ₹79.85 lakh and foreign currency have been recovered from the accused. Under the new criminal laws (BNS/BNSS), the chain of digital and forensic evidence must be extremely strong. If concrete evidence (such as CCTV footage or audit matching) directly linking the recovered cash to the specific theft from temple donation boxes is not presented in court, the accused can complicate the case by claiming the mere recovery of money as their private property. Secret presentation, procedure not followed Several local lawyers have objected that the police presented the accused before the remand magistrate in a very secretive manner. If the necessary legal procedures or timelines for arrest and remand were not fully followed, it could become an issue of 'illegal detention', making it easier for the defense to obtain bail. The lack of legal aid for the accused also provides an advantage The Ayodhya Bar Association has decided not to fight the case of the accused. Article 22(1) of the Indian Constitution grants every accused the right to be defended by a lawyer of their choice. According to the instructions of the Supreme Court, if an accused does not receive fair legal representation, the entire trial of the lower court cannot be considered valid. This technical ground may be sufficient to quash the conviction or overturn the case in the High Court. stories.title: Woman kills husband, buries body beneath bathroom floor:Wife detained; body recovered on 45th day
stories.summary: In Agra, a wife murdered her husband and buried the body inside the house. To hide the body, she had plaster and tiles installed in the bathroom. She continued to feign her husband's disappearance for 45 days. On Friday, when the police arrived for verification, the wife panicked. Police have taken her into custody and are interrogating her. She has confessed to her crime. After the incident came to light, there was a stir throughout the entire area. The case is from the Prakshi Tower police outpost area under Sikandra police station. Read the full story Surendra Sharma, a resident of the Prakshi Tower police outpost area, had been missing since 18 May, and his wife filed a missing person report on 26 May while repeatedly telling family members and neighbors that he had disappeared. On Friday, police visited the house for verification in an old case and grew suspicious of the woman's behavior. Acting on crucial information provided by the deceased's brother, they searched the house and noticed signs of suspicion around the bathroom floor. After excavating it, they recovered Surendra's body, triggering shock in the area as a large crowd gathered at the spot. Body buried and then plastered and tiled Preliminary investigation revealed that after the murder, the body was buried in the bathroom and then plastered and tiled over, so that no one would suspect. Police believe that another person may also have played a role in this incident. The investigation is being advanced keeping this aspect in mind. Police have taken the body into custody and sent it for post-mortem. Meanwhile, Ruby Sharma is being interrogated to gather information about the reasons for the murder and the sequence of events. Police officials say that all aspects of the case are being investigated and further action will be taken based on the evidence. Wife Ruby Sharma has been taken into custody, and interrogation has begun.

stories.title: UP TET candidates report changed exam paper pattern:Aspirants claim AI-generated questions made exam different
stories.summary: The first shift of the Uttar Pradesh Teacher Eligibility Test (UP TET) on the second day concluded peacefully under tight security in Gorakhpur. Candidates emerging from examination centres, including St. Andrew's College, said the paper was generally easy but followed a noticeably different pattern compared to previous years. Many said the questions were concept-based, while the Sociology section was relatively difficult. Some candidates also claimed that the question paper appeared to have been prepared using artificial intelligence (AI), leading to a significant change in the style of questions. Candidates share mixed reactions Anita Soni, who travelled from Farenda in Maharajganj district, said she has been teaching for 17 years and was initially nervous about the exam. "I was very anxious before the test, but after taking it, I feel confident. The questions were practical in nature, and I believe I will clear the exam," she said. Pramod Kumar Maurya from Sant Kabir Nagar alleged that the new examination commission had used AI-generated questions, which he felt could confuse candidates and negatively affect child-centric teaching and learning principles. Meanwhile, Kamlesh Kumar Yadav from Azamgarh said candidates were not provided with rough sheets for solving Mathematics questions, making calculations difficult. He urged the commission to provide rough paper in future examinations. Strict security checks at examination centres Candidates were allowed to enter examination centres only after thorough security screening. Female candidates were asked to remove hairpins, jewellery and hair accessories, while male candidates had to deposit belts and scarves before entering. Entry was permitted only after retina scanning and metal detector checks. The examination is being conducted at 32 centres across Gorakhpur. The first shift was held from 9:30 a.m. to 12:00 noon, while the second shift is scheduled from 2:30 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. A total of 72,020 candidates are appearing for the examination in the district. Sector magistrates and static magistrates have been deployed at every centre to oversee the process. Officials stress transparency and security Additional District Magistrate (City) Gajendra Kumar instructed officials to ensure complete transparency and fairness during the examination. He directed centre superintendents and magistrates to work in coordination and ensure the availability of essential facilities such as drinking water, electricity, toilets and seating arrangements. SP City Nimish Patil said adequate police personnel had been deployed at all examination centres. Sensitive centres are under special surveillance, and authorities have been instructed to take immediate action against any suspicious activity while ensuring smooth traffic management around the venues. Double-lock system for question paper security Officials said a double-lock security system has been implemented for the safekeeping of question papers. Examination centres are also being monitored through CCTV cameras, while strict entry checks and all prescribed examination protocols are being followed to ensure a fair and transparent examination process.

stories.title: Missing Class 9 student found following post on Facebook:Youth ran away two years ago after fight with father
stories.summary: A ninth-grade student who went missing about two years ago from the Gulriha police station area of Gorakhpur was found in Ajmer, Rajasthan. A missing person report was filed at Gulriha police station on September 3, 2024, and a police team was engaged in the search for the student. The student's family informed the police after seeing their son's photo on Facebook. When the police investigated, they found the location to be Ajmer, Rajasthan. After this, a police team left for Ajmer on Tuesday after talking to the local police there. Upon reaching there, it was found that the student, Shashikant, was working in a hotel. Gulriha police, along with the local police, made contact with the student on Thursday. After this, the police arranged a conversation between the boy and his family. During the conversation on the mobile, the student and his family members started crying. After completing necessary legal procedures, the police left for Gorakhpur with the boy. The team arrived with the student around 12 PM on Friday and handed him over to his family. Know the full story Shashikant, the 15-year-old younger son of Tarkeshwar Pandey, a resident of Sneh City Colony, Mugalaha, under Gulriha police station area, left for school on the morning of September 3, 2024, and did not return. The family members searched for a long time. They inquired at the school and with relatives but no trace was found. By evening, they reached the police station and filed a missing person report. In the complaint, the family expressed apprehension of kidnapping. According to information, a day earlier, the father had scolded Shashikant for his studies, which had made him very angry. He was not eating dinner at night either. After much persuasion from his mother, he ate and went to sleep. He woke up in the morning and quietly got ready for school. He had breakfast, took his lunch, and left. Concern grew when he didn't return from school Everyone was thinking that he had gone to study. But he did not return home long after school was over. Family members searched for him nearby. When they inquired at the school, they found out that he had not even reached the school. There was a fear of kidnapping His parents also inquired at the homes of friends and relatives, but there was no trace of their son. After which, they feared kidnapping. Father saw photo on Facebook 10 days ago According to information, about 10 days ago, Shashikant's father saw Shashikant in a post on Facebook. He immediately informed the police. As soon as the information was received, the police team immediately became active. They tried to find the location of that ID with the help of surveillance. The investigation revealed the location of Ajmer, Rajasthan. The police first tried to contact them by phone. Police team reached Ajmer Even after many attempts, when contact could not be established from here, a team left for Ajmer on Tuesday. After reaching there on Wednesday morning, a thorough search was conducted with the help of photos. Then the location of a hotel was found. When the police reached that hotel, Shashikant was seen working there. He was recovered with the help of local police around 9 AM on Thursday morning. After completing the proceedings, the police arranged for him to speak with his family. After that, around 12 PM on Friday afternoon, the police brought him to Gorakhpur and handed him over to his family after necessary action. Reached Rajasthan to meet YouTuber 'Indian Hacker' During police interrogation, Shashikant stated that he is a very big fan of YouTuber 'Indian Hacker'. He used to watch his videos a lot. He lives in Ajmer, Rajasthan. I left home upset to meet him. After going to Rajasthan, when I couldn't meet him, I started looking for work in a hotel.

stories.title: 38-year-old man rapes minor sister:Accused tells police he saw his wife in the victim
stories.summary: A 38-year-old man who repeatedly raped his minor sister for about one-and-a-half years in Fatehpur was sent to jail by the police on Thursday evening around 4 pm. While being taken to jail, the accused said, “I used to see my deceased wife in my younger sister, which is why I raped her.” According to the police, the accused had beaten his wife to death about three years ago for refusing to consume drugs. After that, he went to jail. The rape-accused was released from jail in June 2024 and returned home. Since then, he raped his 16-year-old biological sister. The sister complained to her family members many times, but no one believed her. After this, with the help of her friends, the victim made a video of the accused committing the rape and showed it to her family. After watching the video, the family was stunned. The case is from a village in the Thariyaon police station area, 28 km away from the district headquarters. Based on the complaint filed by the victim's other brother's wife, the police registered an FIR on Wednesday under several serious sections, including the POCSO Act. Case filed on sister-in-law's complaint, accused sent to jail after medical examination Based on the complaint of the younger sister-in-law, Thariyaon Police Station registered a case under several serious sections, including the POCSO Act. The police arrested the accused and presented him in court, from where he was sent to jail. The victim has undergone a medical examination and the police are collecting other evidence. Father died 7 years ago According to information received from family members, the victim's family includes her mother, middle brother, and his wife. Her father died seven years ago due to illness. The victim is currently studying in high school, while the accused worked as a laborer. We will ensure the strictest punishment for the accused, says Station In-charge Thariyawan Police Station in-charge Inspector Shamsher Bahadur said A 16-year-old sister has accused her 38-year-old biological brother of rape. Video evidence has also been provided. Medical examination has confirmed the rape. A case has been registered under the POCSO Act and other sections, and the accused has been sent to jail.

stories.title: 40-year-old influencer stabbed to death:Husband injures himself to mislead the police; dispute over land registration cited as reason
stories.summary: Social media influencer Nisha Chauhan (40) was stabbed to death by her husband in Meerut at 6 AM on Friday morning. After the killing, Nisha's husband Pradeep Chauhan (42) inflicted several wounds on himself. He was severely injured. At the time, witnesses said the couple's children came out of the house screaming. When neighbors entered the house, Nisha was lying on the floor, covered in blood. A short distance away, Pradeep was writhing in pain. Police, who arrived after being informed, took both to the hospital. There, doctors declared the female influencer dead. The reason for the incident is said to be a dispute over the registration of a 1,170 sq ft plot of land. According to police sources, the land was to be registered today (Friday) itself. Nisha wanted the registration to be in her name, but Pradeep was not ready. Forensic teams and officials reached the spot. They collected evidence. Police questioned the children. CCTV footage from around the house is also being scanned. The incident took place in Harra town, under the Sarurpur Police Station area. See 3 pictures Dragged from the bedroom to the hall, stabbed with knives So far, in the investigation, the police have found that there was a dispute between Nisha and Pradeep. Pradeep dragged Nisha from the bedroom to the hall. He attacked her with a knife. He also attacked her throat. Nisha fell, covered in blood. After this, Pradeep also stabbed himself with a knife. 24K Followers on Instagram Nisha Chauhan's Instagram ID is named rajputnisha_5m. The name written is Nisha Rajput. She has 24,4000 followers. She has made 960 posts so far. She used to follow 10 people. In the bio, 'Your love', 'Target 50 thousand', 'Jai Shri Ram' and 'Jai Bhawani' are written. A link to her YouTube channel is also provided.

stories.title: 24-year-old Army aspirant found dead:Family cries foul, expresses suspicion of murder
stories.summary: A 24-year-old man, who was preparing for Army recruitment, was found dead, hanging from a noose in an under-construction house in Jangal Mahadeva village, under the Chauri Chaura Police Station limits of Gorakhpur, late on Thursday night. As the body was found about 200 meters away from the deceased's home, family members and villagers have expressed suspicion of murder. Police have sent the body for post-mortem and started investigating the matter. The deceased was identified as Kush Chaudhary, a resident of the village. Kush's father, Gaurishankar Chaudhary, had passed away. He was the younger of two brothers and was unmarried. According to family members, Kush was preparing for Army recruitment. His elder brother, Dinanath Chaudhary, is a sanitation worker in Brahmpur block. Late on Thursday night, around 11 PM, villagers saw the youth's body hanging from a noose on the doorframe of an under-construction house outside the village. Upon receiving information about the incident, Chauri Chaura Station House Officer Inspector Ved Prakash Sharma arrived at the scene, took possession of the body, and sent it for post-mortem after necessary procedures. The police also inspected the incident site. No signs of injury were found anywhere. Meanwhile, the family members have not expressed suspicion on anyone. Station House Officer Ved Prakash stated that the exact cause of death will only be known after the post-mortem.

stories.title: Security tightened for UP-TET:15 solver gang members caught, constable dies en route to duty
stories.summary: UP-TET 2026 entered its second day on Friday amid heightened security across Uttar Pradesh following the recent teacher eligibility test paper leak in Maharashtra. Candidates underwent admit card verification, biometric authentication and retina scans before entering exam centres. Entry for the first shift was allowed between 7:15 am and 8:45 am. The first paper was held from 9:30 am to 12 noon, while the second shift will run from 2:30 pm to 5 pm. At a centre in Lalitpur, a woman candidate arrived wearing a veil, saying she had accompanied her brother-in-law. In Gorakhpur, women candidates were asked to remove hair clips, hairpins, bangles and jewellery, while men underwent belt checks. In Hathras, women were asked to untie their hair buns, and men removed their shoes during frisking. In Lucknow, a woman constable gave a candidate a lift to her exam centre on a scooter. In Basti, a 51-year-old head constable on exam duty was killed in a road accident early Friday morning. The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission is monitoring the examination for the first time through an AI-integrated command and control centre, while intelligence agencies remain on alert. On the first day of the exam, held on Thursday, 15 impersonators were caught attempting to write the test on behalf of other candidates. The attendance stood at 84.76%, with 6,84,614 of the 8,07,636 registered candidates appearing across both shifts. The examination is being conducted at 955 centres across 60 districts and will continue on 4 July. Nearly 19.9 lakh candidates are expected to appear, including 17.7 lakh from Uttar Pradesh and 2,27,481 from other states. Among them 1,85,791 are in-service teachers. stories.title: VIDEO | LPG tanker crash footage surfaces:Generator spark ignited gas leak; 5 died in the incident
stories.summary: A video has emerged of an LPG tanker colliding with a toll booth in Kaushambi. It shows that the tanker exploded after hitting the toll plaza, and gas started leaking. Within seconds, gas spread 30-40 feet. A generator was running right at the toll plaza. The gas reached the generator and there was a loud explosion. Fire spread everywhere. Flames rose 25-30 feet high. The accident occurred on 26 June at 6:38 AM at the Sirohi Toll Plaza under Kokhraj police station limits. Five people, including the tanker driver, had died. The driver was burnt alive inside the tanker. While the remaining three toll workers and a passerby died during treatment. One injured person is undergoing treatment in Prayagraj. The CCTV footage emerged on Thursday night at 10 PM. 4 pictures of the accident After the accident, all the CCTVs and systems installed at the toll plaza were destroyed. Later, experts recovered CCTV footage from the server. The CCTV shows that after the LPG tanker exploded, a white smoke-like gas spread. In a few seconds, the gas covered the entire toll plaza. Then, a spark from the generator ignited the fire. The fire engulfed the entire toll plaza. Sihori Toll Plaza was burnt to ashes. Sixteen bikes and two cars parked in the yard also caught fire and were burnt. The driver's bones were found in the tanker After the accident, the fire brigade team that arrived on information brought the fire under control after about 30 minutes of effort. When the team inspected the tanker, the bones of driver Dharmendra Dubey (40) were found. The tanker was going from Kanpur towards Pratapgarh. Toll employee Alok Singh also died in the accident. Toll employee Anil Kumar, a resident of Handia, died on July 1 during treatment. On July 2, two other injured persons died. These include Heeramani Singh (29), a resident of Rajapur, Raebareli, and Krishnapal Maurya (23), a resident of Katheli village in Sidhi, Madhya Pradesh. Toll employee Sanjay Nirmal said, "There was light rain for 10 minutes before the accident. Don't know what happened suddenly that the entire vehicle fell with a thud. The fire, fuelled by a gas leak, spread to the yard and toilet adjacent to the plaza. Supervisor Alok Pandey, who was in the toilet, was severely burnt. A video of him running on the road has also surfaced.

stories.title: RSS on Ram Mandir theft:‘Grave sin’; guilty must be punished, Vinay Katiyar says Champat, Anil may face jail
stories.summary: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) on Friday issued its first statement on the alleged theft of donations from the donation boxes at the Ayodhya Ram Mandir RSS General Secretary Dattatreya Hosabale described the incident as "unfortunate" and said it had deeply hurt the faith and sentiments of lakhs of Lord Ram devotees. He said that whoever is found guilty in the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe should face strict punishment. "The theft of money collected in the donation boxes of the Ram Lalla Mandir is unfortunate. It has hurt the emotions and devotion of Ram devotees. Whoever is found guilty in the SIT investigation must be given stringent punishment," Hosabale said. Vinay Katiyar alleges embezzlement of temple funds Meanwhile, in Ayodhya, senior BJP leader Vinay Katiyar alleged that there had been a clear embezzlement of temple funds. He claimed that Ram Mandir Trust former General Secretary Champat Rai, trustee Dr. Anil Mishra, and invited trust member Gopal Rao had escaped legal action for now. "It is clear that there has been embezzlement of money. Champat Rai, Dr. Anil Mishra, and Gopal Rao have somehow escaped and have not gone to jail. They may end up in jail later," Katiyar said. Meanwhile, Ram Mandir donation theft accused Avinash Shukla has been taken into police custody for 24 hours. Police reached Ayodhya Jail at 9 am on Friday and left for Pratapgarh with him. Avinash is originally from Pratapgarh district. He worked as part of the team that counted donations at the Ram Mandir and lived in a rented room in Ayodhya. Police recovered ₹20 lakh in cash, 1,000 US dollars, jewellery and a box labelled 'Ram Rajya Fund' from his room. According to sources, police learnt during questioning that Avinash hid the gold and silver jewellery, along with cash donated to the Ram Mandir. Investigators are expected to take him to the locations identified by him to recover the items. Meanwhile, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) has once again summoned trustee Dr Anil Mishra and invited trust member Gopal Rao for questioning today. They have been asked to bring their bank details and documents related to the appointment of Ram Mandir staff. The SIT had already questioned both men behind closed doors for five hours on Thursday. Preparation underway for bulldozer action at accused's homes Meanwhile, the Ayodhya Development Authority (ADA) is preparing to demolish newly built houses linked to Ram Mandir donation theft accused Lavkush Mishra and Anukalp Mishra. The ADA has also issued a notice to Lavkush's wife, Supriya Mishra. However, Lavkush's wife said they had not received any notice. She claimed the house was built with an approved plan and said her only prayer was for her husband to return home safely.

stories.title: India's first urban ropeway ready in Varanasi:45-minute journey cut to 16, fares start from ₹10
stories.summary: The country's first public transport ropeway is ready in Varanasi. This high-tech service could start around Dev Deepawali (November 24, 2026). Built at a cost of ₹800 crores, this ropeway will take you from Cantt Railway Station to near Kashi Vishwanath Dham (Godoulia) in just 16 minutes. The same route takes 45 minutes by road. After Mexico and La Paz-El Alto in Bolivia, Varanasi is going to become the third city in the world where ropeway will be used as a public transportation system. Why is Varanasi Ropeway special worldwide? Solution to traffic in densely populated areas: This 3.85-kilometer long urban ropeway will pass over extremely densely populated and narrow areas. It is estimated that road traffic will be reduced by up to 40% once it starts. Excellent Capacity: Cable cars (cabins) will operate in both directions in this aerial corridor. 3,000 passengers will be able to travel in one direction, and a total of 6,000 passengers per hour combining both directions. Approximately 96,000 people will benefit from it daily. If compared to other cities in the world- Claim: Ropeway corridor will reduce traffic by 40% According to the Varanasi Development Authority (VDA), the launch of this ropeway, passing over the city's busiest and narrowest areas, will reduce ground traffic by up to 40 per cent. A total of five stations have been built along this corridor. 1. Varanasi Cantt Railway Station (Starting Terminal) It has been designed as a state-of-the-art multi-modal transport hub. This will allow passengers to alight from the train and directly board the ropeway without exiting the station premises. It will feature airport-style lounges, high-tech digital cloak rooms, and short-stay mini-hotels (refreshing rooms) for pilgrims staying only a few hours. 2. Kashi Vidyapeeth Station This will be a major stop for students, researchers, and local shopkeepers. The 15-20 minutes wasted in traffic jams on the road between Cantt and Vidyapeeth will now be eliminated. 3. Rath Yatra Station Varanasi's main commercial hub, connecting large textile markets like Luxa Road, Bhelupur, and Sigra. Tourists staying in these commercial areas and hotels outside the main temple area of Godaulia will be able to catch a cable car directly from here and reach the ghats in just a few minutes. 4. Girjaghar Station (technical Stop Only) Here, the cable car doors will not open for passengers, nor will tickets be available. Actually, due to the narrow and sharp turns between Rath Yatra and Godaulia, the cable car cannot turn directly at 90 degrees. Therefore, this station has been built as a 'turning point' and emergency backup to turn the cable car in the air at a safe angle of 65 degrees. 5. Godowlia Chowk (Last Terminal) From here, Kashi Vishwanath Temple and Dashashwamedh Ghat will be just 400 meters away. Earlier, one had to face severe traffic jams while traveling from Cantt to here by auto or e-rickshaw, but now the journey will be easier. To showcase Varanasi's cultural identity, the exterior of this station is being decorated with Chunar red stones and carved glass. Travel in an AC Cabin for just ₹10 Keeping in mind the pockets of the common public, the journey on this high-tech ropeway has been kept very affordable. According to the official fare list released on 23 June, the minimum fare has been fixed at ₹10. This will increase based on the distance of the station under a 'slab system'. The fare from Cantt to Vidyapeeth is ₹10. Then, the fare will increase by ₹10 for each subsequent station. For the entire journey from Varanasi Cantt to the last station, Godowlia Chowk, ₹50 will have to be paid. However, this seems cheaper when compared to road traffic jams and e-rickshaw or auto fares. E-rickshaws or autos charge ₹30 to ₹40 per passenger for this distance. In heavy traffic, more than 45 minutes are also wasted. However, there is a provision for a 1 per cent to 5 per cent increase in ropeway fares every year on April 1st. 20% Discount on 'Kashi Smart Pass' Keeping in mind local shopkeepers and students of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapeeth, the Kashi Smart Pass System is being implemented. Using this QR-based smart card will provide a direct 20% discount on every trip. With the smart pass, the entire journey from Cantt to Godaulia, which costs ₹50, will be covered for just ₹40. Meanwhile, the ₹10 fare from Vidyapeeth to Rath Yatra will become ₹8. Those who get a fixed monthly pass will receive a huge discount of up to 30 per cent. This will benefit daily commuters. Tourists can book entire cabins There is also a provision to book an entire cable car for corporate VIPs, special VVIP families, and luxury tourists. If a whole group or family wants to travel privately alone, the entire ropeway cabin can be booked at a rate of ₹2,000 per trip. If a travel agency, hotel, or institution makes a group booking in advance, they will receive a discount. They will only have to pay ₹1200 per cabin. Whether power cuts or a storm comes, the ropeway is safe International safety standards have been adopted in the Varanasi ropeway, so that passengers do not face problems during power cuts or storms. In case of a main power cut, the entire system will shift to automatic generator and heavy-duty inverter backup within one second. Even if the entire power system fails, 'emergency diesel engines' have been installed as backup at every station. Their job will be to safely pull all cable cars stuck in the air to the next station, so that passengers do not remain stranded in the air. 'Anemometers' have been installed on the towers to measure wind speed. If the wind speed exceeds 65 to 70 km per hour, the system will automatically slow down the cable car's speed by sounding an alarm. After this, passengers will be disembarked at safe stations and operations will be stopped.

stories.title: DSO rejects land mafia links:UP PCS officer says 'Mother sold 17 bighas for ₹68 lakhs'
stories.summary: "I didn't even know that an FIR had been filed in Saharanpur. I got to know from the news on Thursday morning. When I checked, I found out that my mother herself had filed a case against me and my family. The police neither investigated nor tried to find out the truth." “An attempt was made to tarnish my image. How can I have a connection with land mafias? My mother sold 17 bighas of land to a person from Dehradun, and that money came into her account.” This is what Dr. Seema Chaudhary, a 2017 batch PCS (Provincial Civil Service) officer and DSO (District Supply Officer) of Hapur, has to say. The woman officer's mother, Munesh Rani, filed an FIR against her in Saharanpur on June 30. The Sarsawa police station has registered a case against 5 people, including Seema. Mother Munesh Rani says that her daughter Seema, brother-in-law Sanjeev Kumar Chaudhary, sister-in-law's father Rajendra Rana, Gambhir, and Naresh Kumar conspired together to seize her land. My daughter opened my bank account without permission to hide her 'black money'. She deposited ₹15 lakh into the account. When I found out and protested, she threatened to kill me. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to DSO Dr. Seema about the allegations. Read the full interview Question: Has an FIR been filed against you in Saharanpur? Answer: I came to know by reading the news that an FIR has been filed against me in Saharanpur district. I had no information about this before, nor has there ever been any dispute with my family. I keep talking to my mother. My photos and other information were also picked up and made viral everywhere and given to the media. My uncle Sanjeev Chaudhary's name is also included in this FIR. Question: What is the real dispute in the family? Answer: My father, Mahipal Singh, is a farmer by profession. He is 65 years old. Due to heart surgery and other illnesses, he remains unwell. My grandmother is also still alive. We still have a joint family. Instead of transferring my grandfather's share of land to my father's name, the family transferred it to my mother Munnesh's name. My mother Munnesh has 32 bighas of land in her name. My mother sold 17 bighas of land, which was in her name, to Anupam Joshi of Dehradun. This land is very expensive and was sold at a rate of 4 lakh rupees per bigha. That money must have come into my mother's account. The family went to court against this land sale, and the case is currently ongoing in court. Question: How did the land dispute arise? Answer: Among us four sisters, there is one brother, and the family sent him abroad for studies. The family spent money on his education. Mom said I need to give more money to my son, to which we replied ‘the money given so far is already too much’. We don't know what happened to that money. Once you go abroad, you can even see it. MBA studies do not cost that much. On this, Mom started saying that I will sell the land and give the money to my son. This is where the dispute started. Mom secretly sold the land at very cheap prices. Question: Why was an FIR filed against you? Answer: Mom started feeling that I am an officer and opposed the sale of the land. The land that has been sold is still under the family's possession. Anupam Joshi, who fraudulently bought the land, wants to take possession, but the matter is currently in court. My uncle Sanjeev Chaudhary said that we will give the amount for which the land was purchased, the land is ours. The land buyer is now asking for 18 lakh rupees per bigha for the land. That's probably why mom filed an FIR against me. Question: Your mother alleges that you deposited black money into her account? Answer: The bank account mentioned is mom's own bank account. I have not deposited any money into it. The bank opens an account after a full investigation and seeing the customer in person. Mom herself completed the KYC. In that account, ₹10 lakh were UPI transferred by maternal grandfather Rajendra Rana and ₹5 lakh by Sanjeev Chaudhary. Mom had also asked for this money for my brother abroad. The truth will come out in the bank investigation. Question: Did the police call you to Saharanpur? Answer: The police neither called me nor recorded my statement. My mother submitted an application letter. My name and DSO post are written in the very first line of it. The police should have known the truth. I should have been asked about the whole matter. Now I have told the police and administrative officers the truth of the whole matter. An attempt was made to tarnish my image without knowing the truth. Know the profile of the DSO's family

stories.title: Heavy rain hits Lucknow and 5 cities, water enters houses:Rain alert issued for all 75 UP districts; hail and lightning likely
stories.summary: The monsoon has now covered the entire state of Uttar Pradesh. At around 3 am on Friday, heavy rain lashed 5 cities, including Lucknow, Barabanki, Unnao and Jalaun. Cloudy skies have been reported in more than 30 cities, including Agra and Mathura, with sunshine appearing intermittently. By 6 am, Unnao had received so much rainfall that streets were waterlogged. Rainwater entered several houses. It has been raining continuously since 7 am in Jalaun. In Kanpur, at around 10 am on Thursday, a drain connected to a sewage treatment plant burst, flooding roads and affecting 12 nearby villages. A rain alert has been issued for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh today. Heavy rainfall is likely in 11 districts. Warnings have also been issued for hailstorms and lightning. Winds may blow at speeds of up to 40 kmph, with gusts reaching 50 kmph in some places. Earlier, on Thursday, rainfall was recorded in around 30 cities, including Lucknow and Kanpur. Strong winds swept through Varanasi. In Shamli, potholes appeared on the Delhi–Dehradun Expressway after the season's first rain. A mother and her eight-month-old daughter were swept away in the strong flow of a drain in Sonbhadra. In Ballia and Fatehpur, two people died after being struck by lightning. See the rain pictures- Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: "The monsoon has become active in Uttar Pradesh. There is now a possibility of continuous rainfall. The temperature has dropped by up to 8 °C. The weather is expected to remain the same for the next one week. However, during the monsoon season, Uttar Pradesh, including Lucknow, is likely to receive below-normal rainfall." 54% more rainfall than normal in the last 24 hrs; Sambhal and Mirzapur receive highest Uttar Pradesh recorded an average of 8.4 mm of rainfall in the last 24 hours, while the normal average rainfall for this period is 5.5 mm. This means the state received 54% more rainfall than normal. However, from 1 June to 2 July 2026, the state has received a total of 58.3 mm of rainfall, against the normal figure of 106.8 mm for the same period. This means Uttar Pradesh has so far recorded 45% below-normal rainfall. In the last 24 hours, Sambhal recorded the highest rainfall at 46.3 mm, followed by Mirzapur (43.9 mm), Azamgarh (41.3 mm), Badaun (29.8 mm), Moradabad (24.8 mm), Varanasi (20.9 mm), Hardoi (19.6 mm), Bijnor and Etah (18.7 mm each), and Lakhimpur Kheri (18.4 mm).
